stories.title: Trader’s son says, ‘Minister Nishad is coming to make photo-videos’:Father raised Nishad community’s voice; was beaten to death in Gonda
stories.summary: Raja Sahni, son of Gonda trader Vinod Sahni (Nishad), who was killed, said his father had been raising his voice for the Nishad community. He alleged that his father responded to people on Facebook in the same language they used with him. “Mahant Raju Das abused my father, but no encounter took place against him. His people were not killed, but my father was murdered. Sanjay Nishad is only coming here to get his video made for social media,” Raja said. Family demands arrest, strict action against accused Raja said the family’s immediate demand was the arrest of the accused at the earliest. “The action that Chief Minister Yogi talks about, including encounters and bulldozers, should be taken. If action is not taken now, then when will it be? We are continuously receiving threats on social media,” he said. He said the family was not satisfied with the action taken so far and remained concerned about its safety. Family speaks to Dainik Bhaskar about its concerns The Dainik Bhaskar team spoke to the bereaved family and learnt about their grief, concerns and demands following Vinod Sahni’s murder. Read the full report... First, know what happened Utensil trader Vinod Kumar Sahni, 45, lived in Reksadia village under the Parspur police station area. His family includes his wife, Usha; two daughters, Ragini and Vijaylakshmi; and son Raja Sahni. His elder daughter Ragini is married. His younger brothers, Vinay and Amit, also live with their families. Vinod attacked while returning home from shop At around 8 pm on Wednesday, September 9, Vinod was returning home after closing his shop when 8-10 people allegedly stopped and attacked him. He was beaten severely and left covered in blood. As his condition was critical, doctors referred him to King George’s Medical University (KGMU) in Lucknow. Vinod died during treatment at around 3 pm on Thursday, September 10. Sanjay Nishad stages protests after trader’s death After learning about Vinod’s death, Minister Dr Sanjay Nishad reached KGMU and sat in protest. Following this, the SP suspended three police personnel. The next day, Sanjay Nishad reached Gonda and marched on foot from the Circuit House to the Collectorate, where he staged another protest. So far, three accused have been arrested in connection with the case. Now, read what the family told us... Son says, ‘I am receiving threats on social media’ Vinod Sahni’s son, Raja Sahni, said there had been a delay in arresting the accused. “The kind of encounters and bulldozer action Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath talks about is needed.” He added, “We have continued to receive threats even after my father’s murder. They tell us, ‘This is nothing yet; more will happen.’” Facebook dispute took place 18 months ago Raja said the Facebook incident took place around a year and a half ago. Someone had tagged his father in a post using abusive language, to which he responded in similar language. His father was subsequently jailed and fined in the case. Raja recalls Ayodhya ‘fish feast’ controversy Speaking about the ‘fish feast’ controversy in Ayodhya, Raja alleged that Mahant Raju Das had used extremely abusive and profane language. He said his father had raised his voice against the remarks. ‘The administration is trying to suppress the case’ Raja alleged that the administration was trying to suppress the case by preventing people from outside the area from coming. He said Cabinet Minister Sanjay Nishad belongs to their community, but alleged that his efforts to seek justice had not produced the expected results. Raja said, “We feel he comes because he wants to post videos on social media.” Brother says family may be forced to leave home Vinod’s younger brother, Vinay Kumar Sahni, said opponents disliked his brother for raising his voice for the fishing community. He said, “None of our demands have been met so far. We are receiving threats on social media. We will have no choice but to leave our homes.” He added, “Sanatan has grown so much that it is gradually becoming hollow from within.” Cause of murder unclear, investigation under way on several fronts... Had switched between SP, Nishad Party and Azad Samaj Party Vinod was active in politics and had initially joined the Samajwadi Party, but left within a few days. He later joined the Nishad Party, but eventually quit after opposing the party’s policies and its leader, Sanjay Nishad. Joined Mukesh Sahani’s VIP before his murder Vinod later joined Chandrashekhar Azad’s Azad Samaj Party for some time. After his murder, Chandrashekhar claimed that Vinod had contacted him a few months ago to contest the election from the Colonelganj Assembly constituency. At the time of his death, Vinod was associated with Bihar-based leader Mukesh Sahani’s Vikassheel Insaan Party (VIP). Sanjay Nishad active since Vinod Sahani’s murder Sanjay Nishad has remained active since Vinod Sahani’s murder. He has stayed in touch with the bereaved family, staged a sit-in protest and taken out a foot march demanding justice. Vinod had accused Sanjay Nishad of betraying the community However, Vinod Sahani had repeatedly accused Sanjay Nishad and his sons of deceiving the Nishad community. He had alleged that they were only enjoying the benefits of power, cheating the community and betraying its interests. Some of Vinod Sahani's posts against Sanjay Nishad... Questions raised over Sanjay Nishad’s support for Vinod After Vinod’s death, Dr Sanjay Nishad described him as the Nishad Party’s “district campaigner”. However, questions are being raised over why Sanjay Nishad came out in support of Vinod despite his repeated opposition to the minister. Nishad Party confirms Vinod left three years ago Ram Anand Nishad, Nishad Party’s Gonda district president, confirmed that Vinod had left the party three years ago and was currently associated with the VIP. He acknowledged that Vinod had consistently written against the party. However, Ram Anand said party office-bearers had to be present when the minister visited because they belonged to the same community.

stories.title: ‘I came to make others contest, not contest myself’:Rohini Ghavri says she will back those, not Akhilesh or Congress, who give Valmiki's political representation
stories.summary: After spending 6 years in Switzerland, Rohini Ghavri has returned to India to work towards strengthening the Valmiki community politically. She completed her doctorate and worked in Switzerland for two years before returning. After visiting Delhi, Haryana and Meerut, she has now reached Lucknow. In an exclusive interview with Dainik Bhaskar, Rohini spoke openly about the creamy layer in reservations, political representation for the Valmiki community, the 2027 Assembly elections, Akhilesh Yadav, Mayawati and Chandrashekhar Azad. She said her personal goal is not to contest elections but to help people from her community contest and reach the Assembly and Parliament. Read the full interview… Question: Why did you return to India after spending 6 years in Switzerland? Answer: I went to Switzerland for my studies and completed my PhD. People often forget their families after living abroad, but I could not forget the pain of my community and its people. I was constantly writing about their issues. I returned to India to do the work I wanted to see bringing about change in my country. Question: You had said that you would make a person from the Valmiki community, CM within the next 5-years. What is the roadmap? Answer: I am not saying that the Chief Minister has to be from Uttar Pradesh. We have a significant population in states such as Delhi, Punjab, Haryana, and Madhya Pradesh. Every section of society has been given opportunities in our country. We demand that a community which was for years considered fit only for sanitation work should also reach positions of power. Question: You had spoken about economic-based reservation and changes to the existing caste system? Answer: We support the classification of reservations as per the Supreme Court’s 1st August, 2024, judgment. If it can be implemented in Haryana, Telangana, and Punjab, why not in Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, or Rajasthan? Only a few castes have been benefiting from reservation for generations. The benefits of reservation should reach people from communities living in slums. Question: Do you want the creamy layer system to be implemented? Answer: Absolutely, I support the implementation of the creamy layer. My mother, grandmother, and maternal grandmother were sanitation workers. I benefited from reservation, went abroad to study, and later worked on a good package. Now, the next generation of my family should not get the benefit of reservation. Question: Have you decided to enter politics? Answer: The journey from a slum to Switzerland was extremely difficult for me. I went from a home where I had to depend on others for food as a child to eventually reaching Switzerland. Now, my next goal is to bring my community into positions of power. Even in the 80th year of Independence, the Valmiki community is still looking for national leadership of its own. Question: There is talk of you joining Akhilesh Yadav or Congress? Answer: Our condition is clear: We will go with the party that gives us political representation. We will support any party that implements reservation classification and gives the Valmiki community its due share. If the BJP accepts our demands, we will go with the BJP. If Akhilesh Yadav implements reservation classification and gives us proper representation, such as 10 tickets, we will support him. Question: Will you contest the 2027 UP Assembly elections? Answer: I have not come here to contest elections, but to help people from my community contest them. A true leader is one who creates new leadership. Simply holding a position and sitting there is not leadership. Question: What guarantee is there that the people you help contest elections will stay with you after winning? Answer: The first priority is to get tickets for my brothers and sisters, help them win, and get them into the Assembly. Question: How do you view Akhilesh Yadav’s ‘PDA’ (backward classes, Dalits and minorities) slogan? Answer: Akhilesh ji’s work over the past year has been commendable. He is trying to bring together victims, Dalits, the oppressed, and minorities. He is also talking about issues concerning youth and education. UP wants change, and he should be given a chance once. Question: Is there a possibility of meeting Akhilesh Yadav during the two days? Answer: Absolutely. I had also spoken to him while I was living in Switzerland. At the time, he told me to let him know when I came to Lucknow. I will meet him and put the demands and rights of my community before him. Question: Have you spoken to or met your sister Mayawati? Answer: I have not spoken to Behenji directly, but I have been in touch with people close to her. Behenji will always remain my role model. Question: Of the three models of the Dalit movement: BSP, SP’s PDA, and Chandrashekhar Azad, which do you consider better? Answer: When the BSP first emerged, its model was widely appreciated. People joined and supported it. This is why Behenji became Chief Minister four times. The PDA model is still new. Akhilesh Yadav has been working for a long time, and now a large section of the Jatav community is also aligning with him. They see him as an alternative. I have also seen people from the Valmiki community joining him. As for the third model, I do not consider it a model. It is a strategy to establish one individual. I do not see any model for the welfare and upliftment of the community in it. Question: What would you say about slogans raised in your support during Chandrashekhar Azad’s programme in Barabanki? Answer: I came to know about it late at night. I do not know who those people were. The police have also denied that any such incident took place. But whoever does anything wrong will face the consequences. People across the country who consider me their sister are standing up for justice for me. Question: After returning to India, Karni Sena appears to be supporting you Answer: Karni Sena has supported my fight without any vested interest. Since I addressed the United Nations (UN) in 2023, people from all sections of society have been standing with me. Question: Based on your experience of working with Chandrashekhar, what do you consider his strengths and weaknesses? Answer: His strength is his ability to influence people through his words. But his weakness is that he has no clear vision, policy, or blueprint. A person who is concerned about his position, pension, bungalow, and luxury rather than the welfare of society cannot be a leader of social movements. Question: What was the reason for separating from Chandrashekhar? Answer: A person who cannot be honest in personal relationships cannot be honest in society or politics either. Several state presidents of the organisation were in touch with me, and the truth from within the organisation was that only hype was being created in the name of the community. There was no ground-level work. Question: How did your family and father support you in this fight? Answer: My father is known for his honesty in Indore. He even left his job for our education. When I faced a crisis, my parents and brother stood firmly by me. It is because of my family’s trust that I am standing fearlessly today. Question: Will you get married? Answer: Absolutely not. ''I have made a very strict decision on this. I don’t have time anymore. I am 33 years old. The five to six years that were wasted could have been the time when I got married. That opportunity was lost. If I had met an honest person at that time, perhaps I could have built a family. I also wanted to become a bride. I had dreams too. I had dreamed of a beautiful wedding. I had the same dreams as any ordinary girl, about what kind of lehenga I would wear and what kind of gold jewellery I would buy. But I know what it feels like to have those dreams shattered. Even after making so many sacrifices, people are still telling me that I am wrong. Why? Because I am an ordinary girl and he is an MP. The same people who are abusing me today, I feel, will soon circulate edited pictures of me without clothes and say, ‘This is the kind of girl she is.’ Where is the Bahujan unity? No Brahmin is doing this to me. No Rajput is doing it. Neither a Thakur nor a Muslim. It is the same people from the Bahujan community who talk about unity.'' Question: After turning 33, are you planning to dedicate your entire life to society? Answer: Yes, I have given up my personal life. I no longer have any plans to marry or start a family of my own. Inspired by the lives of Babasaheb Ambedkar, Manyavar Kanshi Ram, and Behen Mayawati, I have decided to dedicate my entire life to fighting for the rights of the Valmiki community and the Bahujan community.

stories.title: UP leaders are organising religious stories, not public rallies:Raja Bhaiya invites Dhirendra Shastri; Manoj Pandey organises Shiv Mahapuran
stories.summary: UP Assembly elections may be fought this time with faith at the centre. Several political leaders are turning to religious events to strengthen their electoral prospects. Ram Katha, Shiv Mahapuran and Shrimad Bhagwat are being organised in different places, with well-known storytellers being invited for these events. Leaders are also planning to attract large crowds through bhajan evenings during Ganesh Utsav and Navratri. What can leaders gain from organising so many religious events in UP? Experts believe it is no longer easy to gather crowds in the name of election rallies. Religion and faith make it easier to bring people together at one place. Such events can also help leaders build and strengthen several electoral equations. This trend is more visible among leaders from eastern UP. UP Cabinet minister Manoj Pandey is organising a Shiv Mahapuran Katha by famous storyteller Pandit Pradeep Mishra, popularly known as ‘Sehore Wale’, in Unchahar, Rae Bareli. Around 50,000 to 80,000 people are reportedly gathering every day. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath also visited the event on 13 September and addressed the gathering. BJP organisation office-bearers are also visiting the venue. Kunda MLA Raja Bhaiya is set to organise a Hanumant Katha by Pandit Dhirendra Shastri, popularly known as Bageshwar Baba, from 17 to 19 November. More than 2 lakh people are expected to come to Kunda every day from Pratapgarh, Kaushambi, Prayagraj and nearby districts. Raja Bhaiya’s party is preparing to field candidates not only from Babaganj but also from several seats in Pratapgarh, Kaushambi and Prayagraj in the upcoming Assembly elections. In Diuli, Ballia, minister Dayashankar Singh had organised a Shiv Mahapuran Katha by Pandit Pradeep Mishra near Baba Balkhandi Temple from 9 to 15 June. Earlier, from 20 to 28 March, he had organised a Shri Lakshmi Narayan Yagya at Rajghat on the banks of the Saryu in Ayodhya. On the final day, the entire pandal caught fire and was destroyed. Former BJP MLA Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh organised a Ram Katha by Sant Riteshwar Maharaj in Kaiserganj, Gonda, from 4 to 6 January. During the event, Sant Riteshwar Maharaj praised Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh for his spirituality and spirit of service. BJP aspirants are also organising religious events Neeraj Bora (BJP MLA, Lucknow North) From 1 to 9 June 2026, he organised a Ram Katha by Jagadguru Rambhadracharya at his office on Sitapur Road. Yogi Adityanath also attended the event. During the Katha, Jagadguru Rambhadracharya said politics should not be about holding a position but should be a means of serving religion and people selflessly. Ketki Singh (BJP MLA, Bansdih, Ballia) From 22 to 30 June 2026, she organised a grand Shri Ram Katha by Rajan Ji Maharaj. The event was held at Baba Amarnath Temple premises in Karihara, Beruarbari. Around 50,000 to 60,000 people attended every day. Dr Uday Pratap Singh (BJP ticket aspirant) To strengthen his claim for the Prayagraj West and South seats, he spent crores of rupees to organise Pandit Dhirendra Shastri’s ‘Shri Hanumant Katha’. The event was held from 21 to 23 April 2026. Abhay Singh (MLA, Gosainganj, Ayodhya) From 14 to 20 March 2026, he organised a Shrimad Bhagwat recital at his ancestral home in Rajepur village, which was attended by several ministers and MLAs. Through the event, he attempted to change his strongman image and embrace the BJP’s political identity after joining the party. Udaybhan Karwariya (BJP leader, Prayagraj) A nine-day Shri Ram Katha was held at Devbra Dham in Handia from 28 March to 5 April 2026. The storyteller was Rajan Ji Maharaj. RSS pracharak Sanjay Bhai Joshi also attended the event. Arun Singh (Chairman, District Cooperative Bank, Unnao) He is staking his claim for the BJP ticket from Bhagwantnagar Assembly seat. Arun Singh has organised a Shiv Mahapuran Katha by Pandit Pradeep Mishra, which will be held from 30 October to 5 November 2026. Rajeshwar Singh (BJP MLA, Sarojini Nagar) He organised a music show by Honey Singh on 22 November 2025 and a grand roadshow by Sanjay Dutt on 22 February 2026. After receiving feedback that elderly voters were unhappy despite the efforts to attract young people, he organised a bhajan evening by Kanhaiya Mittal at Natkur ground in Sarojini Nagar on 22 April 2026. Grand plan for bhajan evenings during Navratri BJP MLAs and legislators from its alliance partners are preparing to organise bhajan evenings on a large scale during Navratri. Some MLAs are booking bhajan singer Kanhaiya Mittal, while others are competing to bring Bundelkhand-based bhajan singer Sunil Lodhi, who has gained attention through songs from the film ‘Hanuman Ansh’, to their constituencies. How do religious events influence voters? Senior journalist Suresh Bahadur Singh says reels and videos of storytellers’ discourses go viral on social media in large numbers today. Compared with political speeches, ordinary people tend to trust the messages delivered by religious storytellers much more and accept them more easily. This is why MLAs, ministers, MPs and election aspirants are spending lakhs and crores of rupees on events featuring high-profile storytellers to strengthen their presence among voters. This can be understood through these examples: Jagadguru Rambhadracharya has praised CM Yogi Adityanath and PM Narendra Modi on several occasions and supported Yogi’s style of functioning. Rajan Ji Maharaj described BJP’s victory in West Bengal after the Assembly elections as “Raghunath Ji’s blessing”. This was seen as a hint towards the future Hindutva agenda of the Shubhendu Adhikari government. Pandit Pradeep Mishra compared the RSS with Lord Shiva at an event in Bhopal. He said that just as Shiva consumes poison to protect the nation, the Sangh too is working to protect the nation by taking on its share of poison. SP leaders are also joining race for faith SP leader Pawan Pandey is set to organise a Bhagwat Katha from 2 to 9 October, which Akhilesh Yadav will also attend. Earlier, when Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati visited Ayodhya on 17 July 2026, SP leader Pawan Pandey gave him a grand welcome. He took the Shankaracharya to his ancestral home in Krishnapur on Rasoolabad Marg, where a sizeable crowd of 8,000 to 10,000 people gathered. Akhilesh Yadav will inaugurate Kedareshwar Temple in Etawah in October. More than 1 lakh people are expected to attend the event. Meanwhile, Congress and BSP have not organised major events through religious storytellers so far.

stories.title: Man feeds wife biryani, gives her lassi, then stabs her:Har­doi man pierced her heart; couple had no child for 12 years
stories.summary: In Hardoi, a husband stabbed his wife to death after feeding her biryani and giving her lassi. He stabbed her so many times that her heart also ruptured. They had been married for 12 years. Despite this, they had not had a child. The husband suspected that his wife was having an affair with someone. Police revealed on Thursday evening that the woman had been murdered in the early hours of Wednesday. Based on the husband's information, police recovered the small Rampuri knife used in the murder. After arresting the accused, police sent him to jail. The incident took place in the Islamnagar Tiliya area. He switched on the high-speed fan to prevent his wife's screams from being heard Parvez (34), a resident of Islamnagar Tilia, had a love marriage with his niece by relation, Nagमा (30), 12 years ago. The couple had no children. The husband suspected that his wife was having an affair with Nazim, a motorcycle mechanic. The couple had frequently quarrelled over this issue for eight months. On Tuesday night, Nagमा was lying on a wooden cot in the room when Parvez killed her. The door was locked. As a high-speed fan was running in the room, no one realised that a murder had taken place. At 3:30 a.m. on Wednesday, Parvez called his sister Jubina and informed her about the incident. Now read the accused's confession... During questioning, Parvez told police that before the incident, he had fed his wife Nagma biryani and then given her lassi. The two began arguing after this. Nagma brought a knife to attack him. The husband snatched the knife from Nagma. He then repeatedly stabbed her in the chest and neck with the same knife. After the incident, the accused took a bath and admitted to the murder in front of police. Police arrested him. Husband had told police he feared for his life from his wife The investigation revealed that five days before the murder, the accused had lodged a complaint at the Kotwali police station, saying he faced a threat to his life from his wife and her lover. The police are now investigating the complaint and the lover's role as well. The police have sent the accused husband, Parvez, to jail. According to the post-mortem report, the woman had suffered serious injuries to her chest. The police said the blows to her chest had ruptured her heart. The body was buried at the cemetery near Bilgram Chungi on Wednesday night.

stories.title: No vigilance probe against IAS Abhishek Prakash:Lucknow HC questions why affidavit wasn’t filed; complainant admits mistake
stories.summary: The Lucknow High Court has quashed the vigilance inquiry initiated against IAS officer Abhishek Prakash. Justice Rajiv Singh accepted Abhishek Prakash's petition on Thursday and cancelled the inquiry proceedings initiated through government orders issued on 20 and 28 March 2025. Abhishek Prakash has served as secretary of the Industrial Development Department and CEO of Invest UP. Case began in March 2025 The case was related to a complaint filed by an official of a company on 20 March 2025. It alleged that a senior Invest UP official had given the complainant Nikant Jain's mobile number and asked him to contact Jain. Nikant Jain was alleged to have demanded 5% of the project's value to secure its approval from the empowered committee and the Cabinet. FIR against Nikant Jain had already been quashed An FIR was registered against Nikant Jain on the basis of the complaint. Meanwhile, a letter was sent for a vigilance inquiry along with the initiation of departmental action against Abhishek Prakash. During the hearing, the High Court considered it significant that no affidavit had been filed along with the complaint. A major development later took place in the case. In a counter-affidavit filed in court, company official Biswajit Dutta said the complaint dated 20 March had been made due to a misunderstanding. At the time, he was unaware that reports from YEIDA and UPCL on land availability and other related issues were still awaited. Biswajit Dutta also made it clear that he had not paid any money to Nikant Jain. The company proposed establishing a solar cell and solar module manufacturing unit in Invest UP on 3 December 2024. Meetings of the evaluation committee were held on 24 February, 12 March and 25 March 2025 to consider the proposal. At the 12 March meeting, the company was asked to provide further information, as details related to land and electricity subsidies were not available. Following this, the committee recommended at its 25 March meeting that the company's proposal be placed before the High-Level Empowered Committee. Complaint described as a misunderstanding in an affidavit Senior advocate Gaurav Mehrotra, appearing for Abhishek Prakash, told the court that the project was already under consideration at the evaluation committee level. The meeting held on 25 March had also recommended placing it before the High-Level Empowered Committee. He said the complainant had later submitted an affidavit himself, stating that the complaint was the result of a misunderstanding. The petition also argued that initiating a vigilance inquiry on the basis of a complaint without an affidavit and failing to obtain the prescribed approval of the State Vigilance Committee was not in accordance with government rules. Affidavits are required to prevent fake complaints Advocates Shailendra Kumar Singh and Anirudh Singh, appearing for the state government, opposed the petition. They said the administrative department had decided to order a vigilance inquiry in view of the seriousness of the allegations. The complaint could not be treated as fake outright. During the hearing, it was also accepted that the 1997 government order provides for an affidavit to be submitted along with a complaint to prevent fake complaints against Group A officers. In its judgement, the High Court said that the requirement to submit an affidavit along with complaints against Group-A officers is intended to protect honest officers from harassment based on false or fabricated complaints. Investigation launched without waiting for the outcome of the proceedings The court also found that, despite departmental proceedings having been initiated against Abhishek Prakash, the matter was referred to the Vigilance Department without waiting for their outcome. In addition, approval was not obtained from the State Vigilance Committee in accordance with the prescribed procedure. The court said that when the complainant himself has stated that the complaint was the result of a misunderstanding, the basis for any action taken further on the complaint also ceases to exist. On this basis, the court quashed the vigilance investigation initiated against Abhishek Prakash and the related government orders. What was Abhishek accused of regarding corruption? Read the allegations point by point 1. Defence Corridor Land Scam The role of then District Magistrate Abhishek Prakash was also found to be suspect in the case involving land acquired for the Defence Corridor in Bhatgaon, Lucknow. While serving as chairman of the land acquisition committee, he colluded with the tehsil administration to arbitrarily fix land prices. Land allotted to members of the Scheduled Caste category in 1984 was illegally made eligible for sale. A compensation amount of ₹20 crore was claimed through collusion between brokers and officials in the buying and selling of the land. 2- Allegations of irregularities while serving as LDA vice-chairman Abhishek was accused of favouring several builders and issuing sealing orders and licences arbitrarily while serving as vice-chairman of the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA). According to sources, he had several illegal constructions demolished during his tenure as LDA vice-chairman, but also benefited builders close to him. Licences were issued to favoured builders in several areas, including Ashiyana. He was also accused of keeping builders' files pending in collusion with LDA officials. 3. Corruption allegations in Aligarh, Lakhimpur and Hamirpur Abhishek Prakash has served as the district magistrate of Aligarh, Lakhimpur Kheri and Hamirpur. Complaints had been filed against him in Aligarh over irregularities in the purchase and sale of land. He was accused of manipulating government tenders in Lakhimpur and colluding with the mining mafia in Hamirpur. 4- Accused of buying 700 bighas of land while serving as DM in two districts Abhishek has been accused of buying 700 bighas of land in Lakhimpur Kheri and Bareilly in the names of his family members. He allegedly bought the land in the names of his relatives-his mother, father and brother-and by setting up some fake companies. He has similarly been accused of buying 400 bighas of land in Bareilly. There are also allegations of stamp duty evasion in both places.

stories.title: Resort near Taj Mahal gets bomb threat:Message warns of blast within 8 days; police force, BDS team reach spot
stories.summary: An email threatening to blow up a resort near the Taj Mahal in Agra was received. The threat was sent via email. The email said that a bomb had been placed inside the resort and could explode at any time within eight days. The resort operator was shocked after receiving the email. He immediately informed the police. The police department was thrown into a panic as soon as it received the information. The Tajganj police, circle officers, the BDS and the dog squad teams reached the spot. The police first evacuated the resort and cordoned off the entire area. The BDS team then began an intensive search operation inside. See three pictures... Resort owner informs police A threatening email was received by the Taj Resort near the Jalma Institute in the Tajganj area. Resort owner Ramesh Wadhwa said the email arrived on the resort's ID in the evening. It said that a bomb had been placed at the resort and that it could be detonated at any time within eight days. The resort owner informed the police. Following the information, the ACP Taj Security and police force reached the spot. The bomb disposal squad was called in. The resort was checked. Every inch searched, every room inspected The BDS team thoroughly checked every room, hall, kitchen, storeroom, parking area and basement of the resort. No suspicious object was touched. The team scanned the entire premises using modern equipment. No explosive material has been found so far during the investigation, which continued for around two hours. The police said they were treating it as the handiwork of miscreants while taking all necessary precautions. Email being checked According to the police, the email contains only a threat; no information has been provided about the location or the type of bomb. Taking the matter seriously, the cyber cell has been assigned to investigate it. Efforts are under way to trace the ID from which the email was sent, as well as the IP address and location from which it was sent. DCP City Syed Ali Abbas said, The resort owner informed us about the threatening email. The police team conducted an investigation. No suspicious object was found. Further action will be taken after a written complaint is received from the resort owner.

stories.title: UP PCS Mains result out:2,297 candidates qualify for interview; 814 posts to be filled, selected from 10,284 aspirants
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission (UPPSC) released the results of the PCS-2025 written examination on Thursday evening. A total of 10,284 candidates appeared for the examination, and 2,297 candidates have been declared successful for the interview. Recruitment is to be conducted for a total of 814 PCS posts. Of these, selection for 812 posts will be based on the written examination and interview. For the remaining two posts, selection will be based solely on the written examination. The result for these two posts will be declared along with the final selection results. Examination held between 29 March and 1 April The PCS-2025 main written examination was held from 29 March to 1 April in 2026 at several examination centres in Prayagraj and Lucknow. Girijesh Kumar Tyagi of the commission said that the recruitment drive has 814 vacancies across 28 types of posts. Of these, selection for 812 posts will be based on the written examination and interview. A total of 2,297 candidates have been declared successful for the next stage – the interview – for these posts. Candidates who have passed the main examination will now have to appear for an interview. The commission will soon separately release complete information on post preferences and the interview. The interview dates and other necessary instructions will be announced thereafter. Result available on commission’s notice board and website Earlier, 10,284 candidates had cleared the preliminary examination. Secretary Girijesh Kumar Tyagi said the main examination result is available on the commission’s notice board and website. Selected candidates can check their roll numbers in the list. All information related to the next stage of the process will also be released on the website. Results Related to Cases Pending in the High Court While releasing the results, the commission also mentioned two important legal conditions. In Writ Petition No. 4253/2026, Arpit Shivam Mishra versus the State of Uttar Pradesh and Others, the petitioner's result will remain subject to the final decision of the Allahabad High Court. Similarly, the results of female candidates from outside Uttar Pradesh will also remain subject to the High Court's final decision in Special Appeal No. 475 (D)/2019. This means that despite the results being declared in these cases, the final status will be determined in accordance with the relevant judicial decision. Cut-off and marks to be released later The commission has also clarified the position regarding candidates' marks and the cut-off. Details of the candidates' marks, cut-off marks and other information will be released only after the final selection results are declared. At this stage, the commission has advised candidates not to file applications under the Right to Information Act seeking this information.

stories.title: Life term for student’s killers who burnt her alive:Wife clings to husband weeping as he goes to jail in Sultanpur; mother gives son ₹500
stories.summary: Two men convicted of killing well-known student Shraddha Singh in Sultanpur were sentenced to life imprisonment and fined ₹50,000 each by Fast Track Court (FTC) II at 4.20 pm on Thursday, with both convicts standing with their heads bowed during the proceedings. As they left the court, Subhash's mother gave him ₹500, prompting him to cry, while his veiled wife clung to him and wept, telling him, "I will not let you go"; she relented after he tried to reassure her. Shraddha's father, Pradeep Singh, said, "In my view, the punishment is inadequate. They should have been hanged. However, I accept the court's verdict." The case falls under the jurisdiction of Baldirai police station. Both Convicts Stood Quietly in the Lockup When the court sentenced both convicts, Subhash and Jaykaran, to life imprisonment, they stood quietly in the lock-up. Their lawyer comforted them by saying that he would appeal in the High Court and assuring them that they would be released soon. After the sentence was pronounced, as the police brought Subhash out, his wife held his hand. She began crying with her head resting on his shoulder and refused to let him go. Her husband comforted her and freed his hand. The police then took Subhash away. His wife sat on the bench and burst into tears. Shailendra Kumar Pandey, the complainant's lawyer, said, "Subhash Singh Chauhan and Jaykaran have been convicted in the Shraddha Singh murder case. Both have been sentenced to life imprisonment and fined ₹50,000 each." Twelve witnesses presented by the victim's side In the fast-track court, the victim's side presented twelve witnesses to prove the incident. ADGC Criminal Sanjay Singh and the complainant's lawyer, Shailendra Pandey, represented the case. On Wednesday, the court convicted Subhash Singh Chauhan and Jaykaran Chauhan. Jaykaran is unmarried. The High Court had rejected his bail pleas three times. Subhash, meanwhile, is married. He has a son and a daughter. His bail plea had also been rejected by the High Court four times. Both were arrested on 24 September 2020. The third accused's case stayed, separate hearing under way for the fourth Further proceedings against another accused in the case, Jagbaran Yadav, have been stayed by the High Court. It has been reported that the student did not name him in the statement she gave before the magistrate. Another accused, Mahant, had remained absconding for a long time. In July 2026, the police arrested him from Dehli Bazaar and sent him to jail. His trial is being conducted separately. Now, a look at the murder case... The incident took place on the morning of 21 September 2020. Shraddha, the 17-year-old daughter of Pradeep Singh, a resident of Tarsa, was studying in the first year of a BSc and was alone at home. At the time, her mother had gone to the jail to meet her husband. Meanwhile, Subhash Singh Chauhan, Jaikaran, Mahant and Jagannath, all from Ainjar village, around 500 metres away, reached her house. They tied up Shraddha's hands, feet and mouth, poured kerosene over her and set her on fire. She named three people in her statement to the magistrate Shraddha suffered severe burns. She was then taken to the Community Health Centre in Dhanpatganj. In her statement to the magistrate there, Shraddha named Subhash Singh Chauhan, Jaikaran and Mahant. As her condition was critical, she was referred to Sultanpur District Hospital and then to Lucknow. She died during treatment in Lucknow. Father had been released on parole to perform his daughter's last rites On the day after Shraddha's death, her father, Pradeep Singh, was released from prison on parole and performed his daughter's last rites. Her father said that the police registered a case only after considerable pressure. Pradeep Singh said he owned three bighas of land, which his daughter's killers wanted to seize. On 8 June 2020, he was ploughing the field when they arrived there. A quarrel broke out during this. Subhash Singh's father, Kunwar Singh, 70, died in the altercation. Case registered against 29 people, including the student's father In the case of Kunwar Singh's death, police had registered a murder case against 14 named people, including Pradeep Singh, and 15 unidentified people. Subsequently, the case of Shraddha's murder came to light. Now, in this same murder case, the court has sentenced Subhash Singh Chauhan and Jaikaran to life imprisonment.

stories.title: Snake hidden in blanket bites brother-sister:Sleeping on same cot in Agra; sister dies at nephew’s naming ceremony
stories.summary: Snake hiding in a blanket bit a brother and sister who were sleeping on the same cot to protect themselves from the cold in Agra. The sister did not even realise that she had been bitten. When the brother's condition deteriorated, his family took him to hospital for treatment. The sister, unaware that she had been bitten by a snake, began feeling unwell shortly afterwards. She was then taken to hospital, where she died during treatment. The incident took place on Wednesday. The brother's son was due to have his naming ceremony today, Thursday. The case is from Murkiya village in the Kagarol area. See two pictures... The son had been born only 10 days earlier Rakesh, Pankaj's father, said that Pankaj's son was born 10 days earlier. The naming ceremony was scheduled for Wednesday, and relatives had come home for it. Kamini and Pankaj were sleeping on a charpoy in the room. They felt cold at night and were given a blanket to cover themselves. A snake was hiding in the same blanket. It bit Kamini first. It then coiled around Pankaj's leg and bit him as well. As soon as Pankaj realised that he had been bitten, he raised the alarm. Sister kept screaming, "Save my brother" Rakesh said Kamini also woke up after hearing the noise. She was the one who saw the black snake on Pankaj's leg. However, Kamini did not realise that the snake had bitten her too. She kept screaming, "Snake, snake," as she tried to save her brother. She repeatedly said, "Take my brother to hospital quickly. Save him." She began vomiting half an hour later Rakesh said Pankaj was brought to the district hospital that night. His treatment began. Just then, a call came from home saying that Kamini's condition had deteriorated. She was vomiting and complaining of a burning sensation in her chest and dizziness. It was later discovered that she too had been bitten by a snake. She was also brought to the hospital, where she died during treatment. Family had faith healers perform rituals to save their daughter's life After Kamini was brought home, the family called snake charmers who performed exorcism rituals. But there was no improvement. The family cremated her at around 8 p.m. on Wednesday. Meanwhile, Pankaj has been admitted to GR Hospital on Shamsabad Road. According to family members, Kamini was the daughter of Rakesh's late brother. The family is in mourning following Kamini's death. While the family is grieving the loss of their daughter, they are also praying to God to save Pankaj's life. Pankaj's father, Rakesh, said that his son had studied up to Class 11. Pankaj had married Khushboo around ten months ago. Pankaj had become a father to a son just ten days ago. Preparations for the baby's naming ceremony were under way at home, but the death of his daughter a day earlier turned the celebrations into mourning.

stories.title: Apple manager murder case:Constable convicted of culpable homicide, second cop acquitted; wife calls verdict ‘shameful’, says will move HC
stories.summary: Constable Prashant Chaudhary has been convicted by a court in the killing of Apple manager Vivek Tiwari in Lucknow eight years ago. In its verdict delivered on Thursday, the court found Prashant Chaudhary guilty of culpable homicide not amounting to murder. The other constable, Sandeep Kumar, has been acquitted. Vivek's wife, Kalpana Tiwari, expressed her displeasure with the court's verdict. Calling the decision "substandard", she said she would appeal against it in a higher court. Kalpana said, "We had been watching the court's decision since this morning. We had hoped that we would get justice, but the verdict that has been delivered is unjust. If the death penalty was not awarded, he should at least have been sentenced to life imprisonment." Wife says, 'He was a trained constable, how could he have made a mistake while firing? Kalpana Tiwari said, “Prashant Chaudhary was a trained constable. So how could he have made a mistake while firing? My husband was shot dead. Both constables were present at the spot.” Sandeep’s acquittal is also wrong, both were equally responsible Kalpana also questioned the acquittal of the second accused, Sandeep Kumar. She said, “Acquitting Sandeep is also the wrong decision. Both constables were equally at fault.” Visibly emotional over the court’s verdict, Kalpana said she did not know what she would tell her children now. The family had been waiting for justice in the case for a long time, but the court’s decision had left them disappointed. Vivek died after being shot by Police in 2018 Late on September 29, 2018, Vivek Tiwari, an area sales manager with Apple, was returning home in a car with his colleague Sana Khan. Near the Makdoompur police outpost in Gomti Nagar Extension, constables Prashant Chaudhary and Sandeep Kumar tried to stop his car. According to police, the car did not stop and a collision appeared imminent. During this, Prashant Chaudhary fired a shot that hit Vivek. He died while undergoing treatment at a hospital. Both constables faced trial After the incident, a case was registered at the Gomti Nagar police station in Lucknow based on a complaint by Vivek Tiwari’s colleague, Sana Khan. Both constables were subsequently arrested and suspended. The case was investigated by an SIT, which filed a chargesheet after completing its probe. The trial was then conducted in the Lucknow district court. After the judicial process, including statements from witnesses and examination of evidence, was completed, the final arguments concluded on August 6. News is being updated...

stories.title: 'Dewar-Bhabhi' die by suicide after jumping into canal:Affair for a year; left home 9 days ago, told elder brother they would die
stories.summary: Bodies of a brother-in-law and his sister-in-law were found in a canal about 13 kilometres from their home in Kasganj. The two had left home nine days earlier after having an affair. The elder brother said his younger brother had called to say that he and his sister-in-law were near the canal and were going to die by suicide. Their mobile phones were switched off after that. Fearing that something untoward had happened, the police were informed. The police and the PAC Flood Unit searched the canal for several days, but the two were not found. The bodies of both were recovered from the canal on Thursday. The man was identified as Krishnakant, 27, a resident of Manauta, while the woman was identified as Priyanka, the wife of his elder brother, Pankaj. Priyanka lived in Panipat with her husband Pankaj, while Krishnakant lived in the village. According to the police, the two had been having an affair for about a year. They had left their respective homes to meet each other. They died by suicide out of fear of society. See three pictures... On Thursday morning, passers-by saw two bodies floating in the canal and informed the police. Read the full story... Krishnakant (27), a resident of Manauta in Kasganj, was the third of four siblings. His elder brother, Pankaj (33), and sister Madhuri (29) are married. Krishnakant and his 15-year-old younger sister Lalita are unmarried. After completing his BSc, Krishnakant was preparing for police recruitment. Priyanka, meanwhile, was pursuing her BSc. Around four years ago, Priyanka eloped with Pankaj and the two had a love marriage. After their marriage, they began living in Panipat. According to the family, Krishnakant often visited his brother's home on the pretext of meeting him. Around a year ago, Priyanka and Krishnakant began having an affair. Krishnakant had left home on 7 September Pankaj said he worked at a textile warehouse in Panipat. At around 1 p.m. on 7 September, he returned to his room for lunch. His four-year-old daughter was lying on the bed, and a cold drink and a packet of crisps were in the room, but his wife Priyanka was not there. Pankaj then called his mother, Ramwati, at around 1.30 p.m. and asked about Priyanka. His mother said Priyanka had not come there. At around 6 p.m., Pankaj called his younger brother, Krishnakant. Krishnakant said Priyanka was with him and that they were in Delhi's Kashmere Gate-Chandni Chowk area. When Pankaj said he would come there, Krishnakant said they would come themselves and that he did not need to come. Told his father, ‘I have come to get medicine...’ Meanwhile, a family member in the village said that Krishnakant had left home at around 11 a.m. on 7 September, saying he was going to get medicine. He did not return until late evening. At around 6 p.m., when his father called him, Krishnakant said there was a queue to get the medicine and that it would take some time. At around 3 a.m. on 8 September, Krishnakant called Pankaj. He told him that he and Priyanka were near the picnic point at Hazara Canal in Nadrai. Swearing on his mother's life, Krishnakant said that the two were going to end their lives. Priyanka also spoke to Pankaj over the phone during the call. Pankaj sent Krishnakant a message urging him not to take such a step and to stay safe. Shortly afterwards, Krishnakant's mobile phone was switched off. Both their belongings were found at the spot On 8 September, police reached the spot after receiving information that some belongings had been found in a bag near the picnic point at Hazara Canal in Nadrai, Kasganj. The investigation revealed that Krishnakant and Priyanka were missing. Police found both their purses, clothes and other belongings at the spot. The items were secured and an investigation was launched. Police and the PAC Flood Unit searched for the two in the canal for several days, but could not trace them. Jewellery, cash and photographs found in the purses Police found gold jewellery, ₹4,510 in cash and a passport-sized photograph of Priyanka in one purse. The other purse contained a bindi and passport-sized photographs. Four ATM cards, a driving licence and ₹510 in cash were found in the men's wallet. Both bodies found in canal after 9 days The bodies of both were found in Etah's Hazara Canal, around 8 kilometres from Kasganj, on the morning of Thursday, 17 September. Villagers who had gone out for their morning walk spotted the bodies and informed the police. The police reached the spot and had both bodies pulled out of the canal. The two bodies appeared to be connected to each other. After news of the bodies being found spread, family members and villagers gathered at the spot. Family suspects murder Station House Officer Videsh Rathi said, The bodies of a brother-in-law and sister-in-law have been found. Both bodies have been taken into custody and sent for post-mortem examination. An investigation is under way. Further action will be taken based on the post-mortem report. Meanwhile, the family members have expressed suspicion that both were murdered. The actual cause of death will become clear only after the post-mortem report and the police investigation.

stories.title: Akhilesh wears blue scarf again at press meet:Says SP-built roads are No.1; former BJP minister joins SP
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav held a press conference at the party headquarters at 1pm on Thursday. Just before it began, party workers and journalists were shown a special film. It featured a ground report on the poor condition of various expressways in Uttar Pradesh, including damaged sections of the Kanpur-Lucknow and Ganga expressways, as well as alleged corruption in their construction. Meanwhile, former cabinet minister Prof Ram Asare Kushwaha returned to the Samajwadi Party along with his supporters after leaving the BJP. Prof Ramshray Vishwakarma and prominent Mathura businessman Ashok Agrawal also joined the SP. Akhilesh Yadav welcomed them into the party wearing a blue scarf around his neck. Mayawati, the BSP supremo, had earlier launched a sharp attack on Akhilesh over his wearing of a blue scarf. She said wearing blue clothes or a blue scarf does not change the casteist mindset of opposition parties and alleged that they were trying to mislead the Bahujan community. Read 5 major things said by Akhilesh… Roads are built later, but start breaking first Akhilesh Yadav said, “I would tell BJP leaders that if Maa Ganga ever calls you, don’t travel via the Ganga Expressway. After the first rain, it became a ‘water expressway’. Carpets were brought from Bhadohi to cover its potholes.” He also listed shortcomings in three other expressways: Bundelkhand Expressway: The expressway inaugurated by the Prime Minister sank soon after it became operational. Repair work is still underway there. Purvanchal Expressway: “They copied us and even landed a fighter jet there. But today, as soon as you pick up speed, your vehicle could land you in hospital or leave you needing back treatment.” Kanpur-Lucknow Expressway: “Two days ago, an RCC bridge started collapsing and the reinforcement bars became visible. I don’t know whether the cement was poor quality or the sand. I have now heard that the company has been blacklisted.” Race for profits between Lucknow and Delhi Akhilesh Yadav also attacked the government over the economy, unemployment and digital transactions. He said, “At the time of demonetisation, it was said that it was meant for the wealthy, but ordinary people suffered. Now even UPI has become a system for extracting money and collecting tolls. This game by these ‘toll collectors’ must stop.” He said more than 20 recruitment examination papers had been leaked in Uttar Pradesh, asking whether any major accused had been sent to jail. He said that if the Samajwadi Party came to power, young people would get employment and social justice (PDA) would be established. He also said, “I have heard that 2 billion trees have been planted on paper. During the SP government, 134,000 trees were planted on 1,000 acres of land. If 2 billion trees have been planted, the government should explain where that land is.” ‘Quality of roads built by us is still number one’ Akhilesh Yadav said, “No one can question the quality of the infrastructure built by the Samajwadis even today. The Agra-Lucknow Expressway is the best expressway in the country. NHAI tried to copy its design but could not replicate it.” He alleged that BJP leaders had even misappropriated money meant for expressway maintenance and failed to build markets along the expressways. He said, “The laptops distributed during the SP government still switch on today. The nozzles at the Gomti Riverfront have not rusted even now. The RCC roads built for the cycle highway during our tenure remain just as strong.” He further said, “What do those who do politics over cow dung and cow urine have to do with a perfume park? Who built the place where the Chief Minister himself sits? If the truth comes out, they will return by boat.” ‘Law and order has collapsed, LDA has become a deal-making agency’ Akhilesh Yadav alleged that murders were taking place continuously across the state, including in Lucknow and Gorakhpur. He said NCRB data showed that women and girls were not safe. He also alleged that Uttar Pradesh had become number one in cybercrime and harassment of journalists. He said the Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) had now become a “deal-making agency”. Referring to a video that had gone viral in Shahjahanpur, the home district of the Finance Minister, he said people allegedly involved in taking bribes were seen swearing not to expose each other. He questioned the situation in a district belonging to a minister who sits beside the Chief Minister. ‘We will build a temple for Vishwakarmaji and declare a holiday on his jayanti’ On the occasion of Vishwakarma Jayanti, Akhilesh Yadav made a major announcement. He said the public holiday observed during the SP government had been discontinued by the BJP. He said the holiday would be restored if the SP returned to power. He also announced that a grand and beautiful temple dedicated to Lord Vishwakarma would be built along the Gomti Riverfront in Lucknow. Ram Asare Kushwaha says, ‘Akhilesh ji honoured me by seating me beside him’ Former minister Prof Ram Asare Kushwaha, who returned to the Samajwadi Party, presented Akhilesh Yadav with a photograph of ‘Netaji’ (Mulayam Singh Yadav). He also handed over a cheque for ₹1 million, of which ₹500,000 was donated to Netaji’s trust. Kushwaha said, “Akhilesh ji honoured me by giving me a chair beside him, just as Netaji used to. Party workers will not sit quietly until Akhilesh Yadav takes oath as Chief Minister again. Netaji used to call me his ‘Birbal’ because I always spoke the truth.” Kushwaha’s return to the SP is being viewed as significant in the context of Uttar Pradesh politics and the upcoming Assembly elections. After returning to the Samajwadi Party, Ram Asare Kushwaha said, Respect is the most important thing in politics. Wherever I am respected, that is where the relationship will remain.

stories.title: Yogi, Rajnath distribute cake at Kashi Vishwanath:Naidu-Paswan also attended; Naga Sadhu played damru, Malini Awasthi sang sohar
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is celebrating his birthday today. Modi has turned 76. Grand events are being organised in his parliamentary constituency, Varanasi. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh offered prayers at the Kashi Vishwanath Temple. They then distributed cakes and presented Banarasi sarees to women sanitation workers. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu and Union Minister Chirag Paswan were also present. 76 litres of milk used for Ganga abhishek in Kashi Meanwhile, Batuk Brahmins performed a 'Dugdabhishek' of Maa Ganga using 76 litres of milk. They blew conch shells and performed Ganga Aarti. At Ahilyabai Ghat, former minister of state and MLA Dr Neelkanth Tiwari performed puja with Vedic chants. Naga sadhus played damrus and extended birthday greetings to the Prime Minister. The Namami Gange team offered a 76-metre chunari to Maa Ganga. Cleanliness drive in Ayodhya; special puja at Prayagraj In Ayodhya, Mayor Mahant Girish Pati Tripathi and District Panchayat Chairperson Roli Singh participated in a cleanliness drive by sweeping at Lata Mangeshkar Chowk. In Prayagraj, a special puja and Aarti were performed at the Sangam. Malini Awasthi also congratulated PM Modi on his birthday by singing a sohar. | PM Modi turns 76: Shah flags off 1,300-km Vadnagar-Varanasi bike rally, says 36 countries have honoured the PM Fruits distributed to patients in Lucknow In Lucknow, Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak distributed fruits to patients at the Civil Hospital. He also inaugurated a blood donation camp. He said the ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyan’ was being conducted across the state from 17 September. Under the campaign, activities such as fruit distribution and blood donation camps are being organised at hospitals across the state. The campaign will continue for one month, until 17 October. 1,300-km bike yatras between Vadnagar and Varanasi Two ‘Seva Sankalp Bike Yatras’, covering around 1,300 km between Modi’s birthplace Vadnagar and his Lok Sabha constituency Varanasi, are being organised. One yatra is travelling from Vadnagar to Varanasi, while the other will set out from Varanasi for Vadnagar. In Varanasi, Yogi Adityanath and Rajnath Singh will flag off the yatra shortly. The journey will conclude on 7 October. See 5 photos-

stories.title: CM Yogi to remain key face for UP Assembly election:RSS tells BJP about ground realities, says, 'Set aside differences and focus on preparations'
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Assembly election will be fought under the leadership of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, with Yogi as the face of the election. This was made clear at a coordination meeting held in the presence of senior office-bearers of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS). The Sangh told the organisation, including BJP office-bearers, to “forget all differences and problems and now focus on election preparations.” Based on feedback received from organisations at the grassroots level, the Sangh also made several suggestions to the BJP and the government. A meeting of senior office-bearers of the Sangh and BJP was held at Dream World Resort in Lucknow on Wednesday. BJP National General Secretary (Organisation) BL Santosh and the party's Uttar Pradesh in-charge, Vinod Tawde, sought grassroots feedback from Sangh office-bearers about Assembly constituencies in their respective areas. Feedback was sought on the strengths and weaknesses of the constituencies. Uttar Pradesh BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary, general secretary Dharmpal Singh, the Sangh's regional pracharak Anil Kumar and all provincial pracharaks were present at the meeting. According to sources, the Sangh said Yogi's image among the public is good and there is no adverse narrative against him. However, there is an unfavourable atmosphere against MLAs in some places. People are unhappy with their working style, while relations between MLAs and party workers are also not good. The Sangh also gave feedback that the working style of police and administrative officials is not good either, and public-related work is not being carried out properly. Focus on Dalits and backward classes to increase; ways to counter anti-incumbency to be explored The meeting emphasised the need to bring Dalits and backward classes into the fold before the Assembly elections. Concern was expressed that both sections could shift towards the Samajwadi Party. The BJP would benefit electorally by bringing both sections on board. The meeting said the central leadership's position was clear: Yogi would remain the face of the election. The BJP will contest the Uttar Pradesh election with full force. Finding a way to counter growing anti-incumbency and the negative narrative at the grassroots level has emerged as the biggest challenge. The RSS made it clear that being active on social media does not simply mean uploading photographs. Leaders will have to go beyond posting birthday wishes and reposting other leaders' posts and instead build a narrative in their respective areas. Sangh coordinator Kripashankar raised issues related to the government and the BJP. According to sources, Tawde and BL Santosh will speak to BJP national president Nitin Nabin and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath after receiving the Sangh's feedback. They will try to resolve the issues that have been reported. Modi, Shah and Nitin Nabin to visit Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah and BJP national president Nitin Nabin will visit Uttar Pradesh in the coming days. Before the election is announced, Modi will hold one rally each in the Awadh, Kashi, Braj, western Uttar Pradesh, Gorakhpur and Kanpur regions. Major projects will be inaugurated and foundation stones laid during these events. Home Minister Amit Shah will also hold organisational meetings and rallies in all six regions, along with inauguration and foundation-laying programmes. Party president Nitin Nabin will hold conferences of booth presidents, Shakti Kendra in-charges and mandal presidents. BL Santosh and Vinod Tawde will also visit all six regions and hold organisational meetings. These meetings will be used to gather feedback on campaigning in Assembly constituencies, caste equations, the position of sitting MLAs and the Opposition's standing. Special focus on social media The meeting also discussed setting the narrative on social media. The government's achievements and the organisation's work will be taken to the public through reels and posts. Allegations levelled by the Opposition will also be countered. In particular, a strategy will be developed to reach Gen Z and Gen Alpha through social media and counter the Opposition among these groups. State Working Committee meeting soon The BJP's state executive committee will be formed soon. The meeting also discussed the appointment of members to the committee. Once the members are appointed, a meeting of the state executive committee will be held. BJP national president Nitin Nabin or Home Minister Amit Shah is likely to address it. The meeting also called for the appointment of the party's district in-charges at the earliest so that they can visit their allotted districts and take charge of the work there. BL Santosh also stressed the need to form the state teams of the Yuva Morcha, Mahila Morcha, SC Morcha, ST Morcha, OBC Morcha, Minority Morcha and Kisan Morcha soon. This will enable the teams of all frontal organisations to become active in election preparations. Close eye on 134 seats in Awadh and Kanpur In the 2024 general election, the BJP suffered significant losses in the Awadh region, which has 82 Assembly seats, and the Kanpur-Bundelkhand region, which has 52 Assembly seats. This is why the central leadership has turned its full attention to these two regions. Central leadership has been continuously camping in UP The BJP's central organisation has been closely monitoring every major and minor development in Uttar Pradesh for the past few months. 4 July visit: Nitin Nabin and BL Santosh held marathon meetings in Lucknow with the Chief Minister and both Deputy Chief Ministers. During the visit, a coordination meeting was also held with NDA allies, Apna Dal (S), the Rashtriya Lok Dal, the Nishad Party and the Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party. Review meeting on 5 September: State in-charge Vinod Tawde reached Lucknow for a two-day visit and reviewed the organisation with office-bearers at the regional and state levels. Meeting with the core group on 11 September: BJP Uttar Pradesh in-charge Vinod Tawde and National General Secretary BL Santosh held a meeting with the core group at the party headquarters in Lucknow. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath was also present. The meeting lasted more than two hours and focused on preparing the roadmap for Mission 2027.

stories.title: Storm, rain lash Kanpur-Bareilly; roads flooded in Sambhal:Gomti water enters temples in Lakhimpur; rain alert in 66 districts
stories.summary: The monsoon has begun withdrawing from Uttar Pradesh. Rain fell in 10 cities, including Meerut, Sambhal, Moradabad and Bareilly, on Thursday morning. Winds blew at a speed of 40 km per hour in Kanpur, followed by heavy rain. Trees and poles were uprooted in several places, cutting off power in many areas. Bareilly also experienced strong winds. It rained so heavily in Sambhal that the roads turned into ponds. Water entered people's homes, and motorcycles parked in the lanes were half-submerged. Meanwhile, the weather is clear in more than 40 cities, including Lucknow, Varanasi and Prayagraj. However, clouds continue to move across the sky. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for 66 districts today. Rivers are in spate because of the rain in the hills. Flood-like conditions prevail in 26 districts, affecting a population of 4 lakh. The water level of the Gomti river has begun rising in Lakhimpur Kheri. Sugarcane crops spread across hundreds of acres have been submerged. Water has entered the temple at Amri Ghat, and its stairs have been submerged. In Pilibhit, leopards have emerged from the forests. Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said- Over the next 24 hours, cloudy skies and rain are likely in several parts of the state. Light to moderate rain may occur, particularly in eastern Uttar Pradesh. Rainfall activity is likely to decrease in western Uttar Pradesh from 20 September. The weather will turn dry across the state from 22 September. See pictures of the rain and flooding…

stories.title: 2 festival special trains to run via Gorakhpur:Delhi-Gorakhpur-Bihar travel to get easier; check the full list
stories.summary: In view of the growing rush of passengers during the upcoming festivals, the railway has decided to operate two special trains via Gorakhpur. The first train will run between Anand Vihar Terminal and Muzaffarpur, while the second will operate between Delhi and Sitamarhi. Both trains will have reserved seating. The Anand Vihar-Muzaffarpur train will run twice a week, while the Delhi-Sitamarhi train will run once a week. This will provide additional convenience to passengers travelling between Delhi, Gorakhpur, Bihar and adjoining areas. 13 trips from Anand Vihar to Muzaffarpur Train 04028 Anand Vihar Terminal-Muzaffarpur twice-weekly reserved festival special will run from 13 October to 24 November every Tuesday and Friday. The train will make 13 trips during this period. The train will depart from Anand Vihar Terminal at 9:15 am. It will then reach Gorakhpur at 10:25 pm via Amroha, Moradabad, Bareilly, Shahjahanpur, Sitapur, Gonda and Basti. After departing from there, it will reach Muzaffarpur at 4:30 am the next day via Chhapra, Sonpur and Hajipur. Will run on Wednesdays and Saturdays on the return journey On the return journey, train 04027 Muzaffarpur-Anand Vihar Terminal will run every Wednesday and Saturday from 14 October to 25 November. The train will depart from Muzaffarpur at 6:15 a.m. and reach Gorakhpur at 12:55 p.m. via Hajipur, Sonpur and Chhapra. It will then reach Anand Vihar Terminal at 5:30 a.m. the next day via Basti, Gonda, Sitapur, Shahjahanpur, Bareilly, Moradabad and Amroha. Train to have 20 coaches The Anand Vihar-Muzaffarpur festival special train will have a total of 20 coaches. These will include one air-conditioned second-class coach, two air-conditioned third-class coaches, nine sleeper coaches, six general second-class coaches and two SLR coaches. Six trips from Delhi to Sitamarhi The second special train will be train 04010 Delhi-Sitamarhi weekly reserved festival special. It will operate every Thursday from 15 October to 19 November. The train will make six trips. The train will depart from Delhi at 11:05 p.m. It will reach Gorakhpur at 1:40 p.m. the next day via Ghaziabad, Moradabad, Bareilly, Shahjahanpur, Sitapur and Gonda. It will then reach Sitamarhi at 11:30 p.m. via Bagaha, Narkatiaganj, Sikta, Raxaul and Bairgania. Will run on Saturdays on its return journey On its return journey, train 04009 Sitamarhi-Delhi will run every Saturday from 17 October to 21 November. The train will depart from Sitamarhi at 12:45 a.m. and reach Gorakhpur at 7:50 a.m. via Bairgania, Raxaul, Sikta, Narkatiaganj and Bagaha. It will then reach Delhi at 8:30 p.m. via Gonda, Sitapur, Shahjahanpur, Bareilly, Moradabad and Ghaziabad. Sitamarhi Special to run with 21 coaches A total of 21 coaches will be attached to the Delhi-Sitamarhi Special train. These will include one LSLRD, four general second-class coaches, six sleeper coaches, four air-conditioned third-class economy coaches, two air-conditioned third-class coaches, two air-conditioned second-class coaches, one air-conditioned first-class coach and one generator-cum-luggage van. During the festive season, the number of passengers travelling on trains to Delhi and Bihar increases. The operation of these two special trains by the Railways will provide additional options to passengers travelling to Delhi and Bihar via Gorakhpur.

stories.title: Woman said, ‘We’ll break up, I need 2 months’:Old video surfaces of Lucknow woman run over by Shahnawaz
stories.summary: An old video has surfaced in the case involving a man allegedly running over his girlfriend with a car in Lucknow. The 36-second video shows the victim, Anamika Singh, with her boyfriend, Shahnawaz. The two can be seen talking, while Anamika is recording the video herself. However, it is not clear when the video was recorded. In it, she says: He is my boyfriend. He wants to leave me, but I don’t want that. I have told him to give me one or two months. I will leave him myself. If I don’t, then you can leave me yourself. Two separate videos of this conversation have surfaced. During the conversation, Shahnawaz talks about shaving his head, but the woman stops him. She says, “I went to him myself. It is not his fault. I asked for his number. I forcibly got his number from his phone. He was afraid that if he did not talk to me, I would beat him badly.” Police have also included these videos in their investigation. Regarding the ‘love jihad’ angle and the allegation that accused Shahnawaz befriended the woman while claiming to be Hindu, police said the videos suggest that the victim and Shahnawaz were in a relationship. The two knew each other. However, the two later had a dispute. Police are investigating whether the man had befriended the woman by concealing his religion. The woman will also be questioned. Meanwhile, Rachna Gautam, secretary of the Vishwa Hindu Raksha Parishad, said, “This is a case of ‘love jihad’. A high-level investigation should be conducted into accused Shahnawaz.” She said a memorandum would be submitted to the police in this regard. Earlier, Women’s Commission vice-president Aparna Bisht had said, Prima facie, this does not appear to be just a hit-and-run case. According to the victim, accused Shahnawaz was pressuring her to marry him. He had concealed his identity. The case appears to involve ‘love jihad’. Further investigation will be carried out. Attempted to run her over with a car The hit-and-run incident took place at around 6.30am on Wednesday (September 16) near Gate No. 4 of Janeshwar Mishra Park in Lucknow. A video related to the incident had surfaced. It showed Shahnawaz, who was driving the car, hitting the woman, causing her to become stuck on the bonnet. The woman kept screaming, but the accused did not stop the car. After driving another 20–25 metres, he increased the speed, causing her to fall onto the road. The accused then ran over her and fled the spot. Two versions have emerged about how the incident began First — Anamika had caught Shahnawaz with his new girlfriend. The two argued over this. When Shahnawaz tried to drive away in his car, Anamika stood in front of the vehicle to stop him. Shahnawaz then ran her over and fled. Second (as stated by the woman in the FIR) — “At around 6.30am, I had gone to have tea near Gate No. 4 of Janeshwar Mishra Park. During this time, Shahnawaz Ali arrived in a car with his friend Danish. Both of them asked me what I was doing there. They then started abusing me. Shahnawaz and Danish got into the car. Shahnawaz drove the car towards me with the intention of killing me and hit me. I was thrown onto the bonnet of the car. I held on to the windscreen wiper. Even then, I fell from the car. Shahnawaz then tried to run the car wheel over me. I lost consciousness after the incident. My younger sister, aunt and other people present at the spot picked me up. I was then taken to Dr Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital. Shahnawaz had also assaulted me several times in the past.” Eyewitness: She was screaming in pain An eyewitness had said that when the woman tried to stop the car, the accused hit her and fled. The woman suffered serious injuries and was screaming in pain. She was heard saying, “God, save me… I will die.” Family initially alleged he had posed as Yash Thakur Soon after the incident on Wednesday, the woman’s family had alleged that accused Shahnawaz had trapped her by introducing himself as Yash Thakur. They said he lived in the Dubagga area and worked as a contractor in Barabanki. However, police said the written complaint submitted by the victim does not mention this allegation. Shahnawaz tells police station: ‘I am being framed’ Shahnawaz told police, “I am being framed. The woman had been harassing me for the past 6–7 months and was following me. She had also taken money from me.” Police have also recovered the accused’s car. The word “Advocate” is written on its number plate. Police conduct Anamika’s medical examination Anamika, who was injured in the incident, underwent a medical examination on Wednesday evening. She was discharged after treatment at Dr Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital and returned home. After reaching home, she did not speak to anyone. Two videos key to the investigation Meanwhile, a case has been registered against Shahnawaz at the Gomti Nagar Extension police station based on her complaint, under charges including attempt to murder and other relevant sections. At present, the two videos have become key evidence in the investigation.
