stories.title: BL Santosh asks BJP-MLAs, ‘How will you win in 2027?’:Why did we lose 2024 LS polls, what is the solution; MPs, MLAs told not to fight each other
stories.summary: The BJP's concern has grown in Uttar Pradesh as Dalit votes have shifted towards the Samajwadi Party. The party will now launch a campaign to reconnect with Dalits. On Saturday, national general secretary (organisation) BL Santosh held a four-hour meeting with MPs, MLAs and district presidents from the Kanpur division. BL Santosh asked the MLAs, How many votes did the BJP candidate receive in your Assembly constituency in the 2024 Lok Sabha election? What was the reason for the defeat wherever the BJP lost? How will you make up for this in 2027, and how will you win the election? The MLAs said that in 2017 and 2019, a large number of Dalit votes that had moved away from the Bahujan Samaj Party came to the BJP. The BJP also received a substantial share of Dalit votes in 2022. However, in 2024, Dalit voters became alienated because of narratives such as the Constitution being changed and reservations being scrapped, and shifted towards the Samajwadi Party. Party leaders acknowledged that the Dalit vote is still shifting towards the Samajwadi Party. This could pose a major challenge for the BJP in the 2027 election. BL Santosh and Dharampal Singh urged party leaders to remain united and fight the Assembly election together. They said there should be no conflict between MLAs and MPs or between MLAs and district presidents. Read BL Santosh's three key points 1- People no longer like VIP culture B.L. Santosh said that people no longer like VIP culture. Convoys of vehicles, sirens and getting tolls waived send the wrong message. This harms the party as well as MPs, MLAs and district presidents. Launch campaigns to bring members of the Dalit community and Dalit leaders into the party. Implement the Ambedkar statue scheme. Organise Sant Ravidas Jayanti programmes effectively and use them to bring Dalits closer to the BJP. 2- Do not limit social media to a photo album B.L. Santosh said that social media is now the biggest political tool. Do not limit it to photographs and albums. Make full use of it in preparing for the elections. It can be used to convey the party's message to the public quickly and effectively. However, social media must not be misused. 3- Get the names of women deleted during SIR reinstated B. L. Santosh said that the names of a large number of voters had been deleted during SIR. This included voters who support the BJP ideology. B. L. Santosh said that the process of adding names was still under way. He directed party workers to have the names of those whose names had been deleted added again. He also raised the issue of the low gender ratio among women voters. He said that after marriage, the names of many women are deleted from the voter lists in their maternal homes but are not added to the lists in their marital homes. He directed party workers to have the names of such women added to the voter list, as women are a major vote bank for the BJP. Meeting lasted 4 hours, defeated candidates were also consulted The meeting lasted from 7 p.m. to 11 p.m. BJP office-bearers from Kanpur Nagar, Kanpur Dehat, Etawah, Kannauj, Auraiya and Farrukhabad attended it. State General Secretary Shankar Lal Lodhi and Kanpur Regional President Ram Kishore Sahu were also present. BL Santosh also spoke to candidates who had lost the 2022 election. He asked them how many votes they had received and by how many votes the victory or defeat was decided.

stories.title: Sumedha from Kashi wins silver for India:Silver medal at World Para Shooting after 18 years; Iran takes gold
stories.summary: Divyang shooter Sumedha Pathak from Varanasi delivered a stellar performance at the World Para Shooting Championships, winning a silver medal for India in the team event. Sumedha and her team will travel to Japan to participate in the Para Asian Games. Sumedha's team achieved this feat in the P-2 category of the 10-metre air pistol event. She was accompanied by Delhi's Bhakti Sharma and Ajmer's Srishti Arora. Sumedha dedicated the medal to Baba Vishwanath and her father. Sumedha said, Now we have to give our best at the Asian Games and win the gold medal for India. First medal in 18 years Brijesh Chandra Pathak, who was present with his daughter Sumedha in Changwon, South Korea, said, Sumedha and her team made history last night by winning a medal at the shooting championship for the first time in 18 years. The competition will continue from 7 September to 15 September. Iran won the gold Brajesh Pathak said, Iran gave India a tough fight in this event. The Iranian team won the competition's gold medal by a narrow margin. Sumedha succeeded in the 2-metre event for India and helped the country win the silver medal in the 10-metre air pistol team event. Dedicated to Baba Vishwanath Sumedha said, I dedicate this medal to Baba Vishwanath and my father. I hope we will aim for gold at the Asian Games. Brajesh Pathak said, Sumedha had already been selected for the Asian Games. She will now leave South Korea for Japan with her team.

stories.title: Tourists fold hands considering Taj Mahal a Shiv Temple:Entered after removing footwear, women say 'this is our Shiv Temple, Bhole Baba is below'
stories.summary: Some tourists who travelled to Agra to see the Taj Mahal are not willing to accept that it is a mausoleum. They believe it is 'Tejo Mahalaya', a temple dedicated to Lord Shiva. Driven by this belief, they were seen folding their hands and bowing their heads before the Taj Mahal. Some women from Mathura and Rajasthan's Dholpur said, "For us, this is not the Taj Mahal but 'Tejo Mahalaya'." As soon as they reached the main gate, they removed their slippers. They bowed their heads and paid their respects. The women also spoke about their faith and beliefs regarding the Taj Mahal. Read ahead to find out what they said and the reason for the controversy. See 2 pictures – Women said, 'This is our Shiva temple' Hindu Mahasabha has also raised the Tejo Mahalaya issue several times The Akhil Bharat Hindu Mahasabha has long claimed that the Taj Mahal is the 'Tejo Mahalaya' Shiva temple. On different occasions, the organisation has also tried to conduct prayers, perform jalabhishek and carry out other religious activities at the Taj Mahal. Dispute over the Taj Mahal has been pending in court since 2015 The dispute over claims that the Taj Mahal is the 'Tejo Mahalaya' Shiva temple has also reached the courts. A case was filed in an Agra court in 2015 in this connection. Lord Shri Agreshwar Mahadev Nagnasheshwar Virajman was made a party to the case. The petitioners demanded that the Taj Mahal be declared a Shiva temple and that Hindus be allowed to worship and offer prayers there. The Union government, the Ministry of Culture, the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) were also made parties to the case. Later, a demand was also made for the appointment of an advocate commissioner to conduct a survey of the Taj Mahal's closed rooms and premises. Demand for survey rejected in 2019 On 18 July 2019, Agra's Civil Court rejected the demand for the appointment of an advocate commissioner to conduct a survey of the Taj Mahal. The matter was subsequently challenged further. On 4 April, Agra's Additional District Court dismissed the revision petition. The petitioners then approached the Allahabad High Court. On 30 June 2026, a petition was filed in the Allahabad High Court challenging the order of the courts in Agra. It sought the appointment of an advocate commissioner to inspect, photograph and videograph the Taj Mahal. In July 2026, the Allahabad High Court sought responses from the central government and the ASI in the case. Citing 109 alleged historical and archaeological features at the Taj Mahal, the petitioners have claimed that they indicate it was a Hindu temple. Know when controversies arose over the Taj Mahal

stories.title: Encounter the killers just as they killed my father:Slain ex-CRPF jawan's daughter in Ballia says 'we are in terror, who will support us'
stories.summary: "My father deserves respect. He served the country; he did not steal anything. If he had been martyred at the border, he would have received respect. But here, he was killed like a coward." "What do we have left now? Everything we had is gone! My father is dead, and we do not know whether my uncle will survive. Those people will kill my younger brothers too. If they are not killed in a full encounter, we will set ourselves on fire too!" This is the pain of the daughters and family of a former CRPF serviceman in Ballia. Neighbours killed the former CRPF serviceman on Thursday (10 September). They also launched a fatal attack on his brother, who had come to save him. One brother died, while the other is battling for his life in hospital. Six women and two children remain at home. The family is terrified. Everyone has the same question: who will support us now? The funeral was held on the minister's assurance, but the family is angry because no action has been taken against the accused. The case concerns the Ubhawn area, 70 km from the district headquarters. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to the family to find out what caused the incident. Read the full report... See two pictures... First, understand the case... Amresh Bahadur Singh, 45, and his family live in Doth Sonadih in the Belthara Road area. At 9 p.m. on Thursday, neighbours suddenly arrived at his dairy farm. They knocked him down and beat him, then stabbed him several times in the abdomen. When his younger brother reached the spot after hearing the commotion, the attackers also stabbed him in the chest. Both brothers, injured, collapsed on the road. The family took both brothers to hospital, where Amresh, a former CRPF jawan, died. His brother's condition is said to be critical. Police conducted raids that night and detained three accused. Amresh's last rites were performed on Friday, 19 hours after the murder. The families of both brothers lived together in the same house Amresh Bahadur's wife, Kanchan Singh, and their three daughters-Kritika (21), Ritika (17) and Roshni (14)-live at his house. Kritika is in the final year of her graduation. She is due to get married next May. Ritika is in the first year of her B.A., while Roshni is in Class 7. The family of Amresh's brother, Manjesh (35), also lives with him. Manjesh's wife is Ranjana Singh, and they have two sons, Rudra Pratap (10) and Dhruv Pratap (nine). Rudra is in Class 5 and Dhruv is in Class 4. Amresh's badi mummy, Sharda Singh, also lives with them. Took VRS, returned to village and started a dairy with his brother Amresh took VRS on 31 March this year. He then returned to the village and began living with his family. Amresh and Manjesh ran a dairy farm near their home. The family of accused Girish Chandra (50) lived 50 metres from their house. His family comprises his wife Sheela (46), son Ram Karan Singh (25), daughter Khushi (21) and younger son Suraj (18). Ram Karan was released from jail only a month ago. He has a criminal history. Amresh's dairy farm is directly opposite Girish's house. According to the daughter, the story of the night of the incident... His daughter, Ritika Singh, said, "On the night of 10 September, our entire family was at home. Dad was sleeping at the dairy. Suddenly, our neighbour Girish came outside the house with his wife, two sons and daughter. They began hurling abuses. My father woke up and came outside. He asked, 'Whom are you abusing like this?' Girish replied, 'Mind your own business. I am abusing my enemies.'" At the time, the power had gone out across the entire village. It was completely dark. We also ran there. Dad said, "You cannot abuse someone's sister and daughter like this. Name whoever your enemy is." To this, he replied, "I am abusing you. Tell me, what will you do?" All five had come with the intention of murdering him. They were carrying knives and weapons. Uncle stabbed in the stomach while trying to save his nieces As soon as Dad opened the gate and came outside, these people attacked him. Dad was stabbed and fell. They tried to touch me inappropriately, so my uncle immediately stepped forward. Sheela plunged a dagger into my uncle's stomach. All of them were carrying weapons. We could not understand what was happening. When his uncle began shouting, Dad forgot about his own wound and stood up again to save him. He did not even tell them that I had been stabbed. The men stabbed him in the stomach again. His entire abdomen had already been ripped open. Dad collapsed in front of us. After that, my father never got up. Daughter said, "The accused should be killed in an encounter, and we should be provided security" The police have arrested only three accused. Our father had retired from the Army; he had not committed any theft. The accused should be killed in an encounter, and their houses should be demolished. We also need protection from the administration. I have so many younger brothers. These people will come in the future and kill them too. They left after saying that they would wipe out our entire family. The elder daughter is to be married next year These people stole from our house in 2022. There was no major enmity. Our family was doing well, and they were jealous of that. There were two guardians in my home. One of them-our father-is gone...my uncle is on a ventilator. We have nothing left now. My mother is ill, and my elder sister is to be married next year. Who will take on all these responsibilities now? We want all of them killed in an encounter...we want all of them killed in an encounter. Just as my father's and uncle's blood has been spilled, just as my father was killed... we want all of them killed in an encounter. ASP Northern Dinesh Kumar Shukla said ... Three of the five accused-Sheila, Suraj and Khushi-have been arrested. Four police teams are working to arrest the remaining two accused. They too will be arrested soon.

stories.title: ₹100 crore scam in UP government medicines, equipment supply:Former Congress MLA accused; ED probing 7 years of records
stories.summary: An investigation has begun into an alleged ₹100 crore scam in the supply of government medicines and medical equipment in Uttar Pradesh. The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has sought 7-years of records from the UP Medical Supplies Corporation Limited (UPMSCL). The scale of the case can be gauged from the fact that the document seeking the records is marked ‘most urgent’. However, instead of providing the records, the Supplies Corporation has sought permission from the Principal Secretary (Health) to share them. ED officials allege that the department is deliberately delaying the submission of information to allow evidence of the alleged scam to be destroyed. FIRs have already been registered in three districts of Uttar Pradesh, naming former Congress MLA Mukesh Srivastava as the main accused. While the Supplies Corporation has not yet provided the records, the ED already has documents that formed the basis of the FIRs. Read the full report… 5-point year-wise details sought On 13 July, L.K. Verma, Assistant Director of the ED’s Lucknow Zone, wrote to Health Department Director General Dr Pawan Kumar Arun. Citing the FIRs registered in Shravasti and Balrampur, the ED sought five sets of information for 2019-20 to 2025-26: The ED has also sought details of funds released to government hospitals in Shravasti, Bahraich, Gonda and Balrampur from 2013-14 till now, their utilisation and medical reimbursement records. On 16 July, the Director General wrote to the UPMSCL managing director seeking the information. However, instead of providing the records, UPMSCL sought clarification from the Principal Secretary (Health) on whether the purchase- and payment-related documents could be shared. UPMSCL was set up to curb corruption Earlier, government medicines and equipment were purchased at the district level, leading to complaints of corruption and irregularities. To address this, the state government set up UPMSCL in 2018. Since then, most procurement has been carried out through the corporation. The Centre provides funds to states for rural and urban healthcare services through the National Health Mission (NHM). UPMSCL uses these funds to float tenders, purchase medicines and equipment, and supply them to districts. ED entered the case after Mukesh Srivastava’s arrest Former MLA Mukesh Srivastava, alias Gyanendra Pratap Srivastava, has already been arrested in the case linked to the medicines and equipment procurement documents sought by the ED. The agency began its investigation after his arrest. Around 9 companies linked to his family and relatives were found involved in the supply of medicines, equipment, furniture and maintenance work in Bahraich, Balrampur and Shravasti. These companies received contracts worth more than ₹18 crore in these districts. What did the UP Vigilance probe found? According to the allegations, the former MLA allegedly set up fake and unnamed firms and construction companies in the names of family members, relatives and close associates, including the RP Group. These firms allegedly secured contracts worth crores without valid tenders or on the basis of forged documents. The probe alleges that in the Health Department in Balrampur, Shravasti and Gonda, funds for hospital maintenance, medicines and medical equipment were released in full against work that had either not been completed or existed only on paper through fake bills. Mukesh Srivastava is also accused of conspiring with senior Health Department officials, including then CMOs, medical superintendents and clerks. The investigation also found allegations that his companies directly used the department’s GeM portal ID. The former MLA allegedly accumulated assets worth crores, including hotels, farmhouses and plots, during and after his tenure as an MLA from 2012 to 2017, far exceeding his known legitimate sources of income. The Vigilance probe also found that under the Supportive Supervision Scheme, funds meant to operate one vehicle were allegedly withdrawn for three vehicles. The role of then CMO Dr. Ghanshyam Singh also emerged during the investigation. The probe found several instances where tender procedures were allegedly not followed. Printing work was carried out without a tender, while in other cases, despite tenders being issued, the then CMO gave exemptions to Medical Officers In-Charge (MOICs), allegedly violating financial rules. The then CMOs Dr. Ghanshyam Singh, Dr. Satyadev and Dr. Praveen Kumar, along with junior engineer Ram Manohar Maurya, have since retired. Vigilance has registered a case against them and continued its investigation. Sources say the alleged scam followed a pattern similar to the ₹5,000-crore NRHM scam reported in 2011.

stories.title: Rohini to enter politics to take revenge on Chandrashekhar:Writes ‘Switzerland to power’ on X; Ghavari working to unite the Valmiki community
stories.summary: It is said that everything is fair in love and war. Something similar appears to be unfolding between Azad Samaj Party president Chandrashekhar Azad and his former girlfriend Rohini Ghavari. Rohini once gave up everything to help establish Chandrashekhar in politics. Now, Ghavari is preparing to enter politics herself to take revenge on him. Having already drawn up a ‘Switzerland to power’ roadmap, Rohini is working to unite the Valmiki community. Her first test will come in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. She may be seen aligning with the Samajwadi Party at the time. What is the reason behind her dispute with Chandrashekhar? What roadmap has Rohini prepared to enter politics? What did she discuss with SP chief Akhilesh Yadav? Read the Sunday Big Story… Rohini had already drawn up her political roadmap… Rohini Ghavari, the daughter of a sanitation worker from Indore, went to Switzerland to pursue her studies 6 years ago on a state government scholarship. Along with completing her PhD in Switzerland, she was also running the Janpower Foundation. On 11 September, Rohini left Switzerland and returned to India. Soon after returning, Rohini first visited the Valmiki Ashram at Bhagwan Valmiki Mandir Marg in Pachkuinya. She sought blessings there. This clearly signals that she plans to launch a nationwide campaign to unite the Valmiki community. She will begin with Uttar Pradesh, the country’s most populous state. Rohini has made her political goal clear. She aims to have the country’s first chief minister from the Valmiki community within the next five years. She says that a person from a community that has been confined to sanitation work for years must be placed in the highest position of power for true freedom to be achieved. Rohini said that if everyone in the country has had the opportunity to become a chief minister, why should the Valmiki community not have the same right? She said she wants to build political leadership and confidence among people from her community. According to Rohini, her next goal is to have a Valmiki community member become chief minister of a state within five years. Senior journalist Syed Qasim says that whether or not Rohini succeeds in becoming a chief minister, she has certainly attempted to awaken political ambition within the Valmiki community through this campaign. To politically mobilise a community, it is also important to give it a big dream. Rohini appears to be moving forward in the same direction. Rohini preparing to build political presence in 4 states, including Delhi Rohini Ghavari received a grand welcome in Delhi after returning to India. Karni Sena president Surajpal Singh Ammu, along with Hindu leaders Daksh Chaudhary and Akku Pandit, attended the event. She later met members of the Valmiki community. On 12th September, Rohini reached Gurugram, Haryana, where she again interacted with community members. On 13th September, she is scheduled to visit Meerut in Uttar Pradesh. The city is part of western UP, where her biggest political rival, Azad Samaj Party chief Chandrashekhar Azad, is strengthening his political base. Rohini will be in Lucknow on 14 September and may meet SP chief Akhilesh Yadav. She will stay there for two days and hold meetings with members of the Valmiki community. She will then travel to Indore on 16th September. Her itinerary indicates a strategy to mobilise the Valmiki community across Delhi, Haryana, UP and Madhya Pradesh. Rohini’s UP plan Rohini says she will raise issues of representation and social justice for Dalits, with a special focus on the Valmiki community. She is also questioning political representation and rights for the Jatav and Valmiki communities. She claims Dalits account for around 21% of Uttar Pradesh’s population, of which the Valmiki community makes up about 3.19%. She questions the community’s representation in government jobs and politics, saying Valmikis are still largely viewed only as sanitation workers. According to the information cited by Rohini, Valmiki voters have a significant influence in around 21 Assembly constituencies, including Agra Cantt, Etmadpur, Jasrana, Firozabad, Meerut Cantt, Meerut City, Ghaziabad, Loni, Lucknow Central, Lucknow North, Lucknow West, Sisamau, Arya Nagar, Kidwai Nagar, Aligarh, Kol and Khair. Rohini plans to be more active in these constituencies, most of which are in western UP. She will also hold meetings in areas where Chandrashekhar has influence and share her account of the alleged betrayal with the Jatav community. Rohini may be seen with the SP Rohini says Akhilesh Yadav was the only politician who supported her in her dispute with Chandrashekhar. According to her, Akhilesh heard her concerns and assured her of support. She is expected to meet him during her Lucknow visit, with discussions on her political roadmap also likely. On whether she will join the SP, Rohini says her primary aim is to fight for the rights of sanitation workers and give the Valmiki community a political identity. She says she is ready to do whatever is required for this. There is also speculation that Akhilesh could consider making her a candidate from a constituency. Plans to bring upper-caste communities into the campaign Rohini’s campaign appears to extend beyond the Valmiki community. She has openly challenged the Jatav community, saying she will see how many Jatavs support her movement. She has also spoken about bringing people from all communities together. Rohini says the Valmiki community does not insult anyone’s faith or Hindu gods and goddesses and claims that the community has always worked towards keeping the country united. Her welcome by Karni Sena members and the Valmiki community after returning to India is also being seen as a possible sign of her political expansion. Rather than limiting herself to Dalit politics, she appears to be seeking wider support across communities. Her support for reservation based on economic criteria is also being viewed in this context. Rohini has also spoken openly about what she calls the misuse of the SC/ST Act. She says casteism divides society, while justice unites it. She has called for a separate law to address caste discrimination and injustice within the Dalit community, while also supporting reservation for upper-caste communities on economic grounds. What is behind Rohini Ghavari’s dispute with Chandrashekhar? Rohini has accused Chandrashekhar of lying to her and promising marriage despite being married and having a child. She alleges that he physically and mentally exploited her. According to Rohini, she also provided financial support to help establish Chandrashekhar in politics. She says they had shared a dream of securing dignity for the Dalit community, but she learnt his “true face” after he became an MP. She further claims that she later learnt that Chandrashekhar had behaved similarly with several other women. She says she approached the National Commission for Women and Delhi’s Rohini police station, but alleges that no FIR was registered. Rohini has linked her campaign to the issue of caste-based justice. In a social media post, she questioned why an FIR was registered in the case of a Jatav woman when the accused was a Brahmin and several leaders, including those from the Congress and AAP, supported her, while no one stood by Rohini. She argued that in her case, the victim belonged to the marginalised Valmiki community, while the accused, Chandrashekhar, belonged to the Jatav community. Before returning to India, Rohini also wrote on social media that Chandrashekhar and the Bhim Army would be directly responsible if she was attacked. She said she would travel across different states, hold social meetings, and continue her campaign despite opposition.

stories.title: Tawde gives 3 mantras for 2027 victory:District chiefs must submit political, social and organisational analysis report
stories.summary: Formal preparations for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections have begun in the Gorakhpur region, with BJP national general secretary and Uttar Pradesh in-charge Vinod Tawde holding a series of meetings with party functionaries and elected representatives. The meetings are part of the party’s broader organisational exercise ahead of the polls. The main responsibility has been placed on organisational office-bearers. Tawde outlined three areas of analysis namely political, social and organisational and asked district presidents from 12 districts to focus on detailed ground-level assessment rather than relying only on data. The political analysis has been asked to be completed by October, with reports to be submitted thereafter. Political analysis to cover candidates, caste equations and BJP prospects The political analysis will cover every Assembly constituency in the districts. District presidents will assess potential strong contenders from each party, the candidates the Opposition may field, and which candidature could benefit the BJP. They will also study the caste equations in each area. The exercise will also identify influential local leaders whose entry could benefit the BJP during the election. Their names and the potential advantages of bringing them into the party will have to be included in the report. A similar assessment will be carried out at the booth level. District presidents have also been asked to compare the BJP’s position in their Assembly constituencies in the 2017 and 2022 Assembly elections and the 2024 Lok Sabha election. Where the BJP’s victory margin has narrowed compared with 2022, where the party has lost a seat, or where its margin of defeat has increased, the reasons will have to be analysed in detail. The broader Gorakhpur-region exercise is focused on assessing the party’s grassroots organisation, booth-level position and local political equations ahead of the 2027 polls. Tawde starts political outreach soon after reaching Gorakhpur Although Tawde’s formal meetings began on the second day of his visit, he started gathering political feedback soon after reaching Gorakhpur. He first met some senior leaders at his hotel to understand the local situation. He later visited the residence of Dr Radha Mohan Das Agrawal, a former BJP national general secretary and Rajya Sabha member who had represented Gorakhpur City as an MLA four times. The two held a detailed discussion over dinner on the political situation in Gorakhpur and neighbouring districts, including the strengths and weaknesses of the organisation. The meeting also gave Tawde an opportunity to draw on Agrawal’s two decades of experience as an MLA in Gorakhpur. ‘Do 100 tasks, but highlight only one’ At a meeting with regional and district office-bearers, Tawde stressed that merely creating an impression of work would not be enough. He said, “Office-bearers should not publicise one piece of work as if they had completed 100 tasks. If they have 100 responsibilities, they should focus on actually completing them rather than highlighting each one.” Tawde also asked every office-bearer to assess what contribution they would make to the election campaign. Responding to a question frequently raised by workers, he said that if a worker complained about not being heard at a police station, he should also consider whether he would be able to continue in the same position if an Akhilesh Yadav-led government returned to power. Tawde holds discussions with seven of 12 district presidents The BJP has 12 organisational districts in the Gorakhpur region, and Tawde held discussions with district presidents from seven of them. During the meeting, the district presidents stood up and briefed him on preparations in their respective districts. Most of them shared details such as the number of booths, the formation and verification of booth committees, and the status of Shakti Kendras. Tawde told them that providing data on organisational structures would not be enough and that the focus now had to shift towards detailed analysis. He outlined three areas of analysis, political, social and organisational. The BJP's Gorakhpur region comprises 12 organisational districts and covers 62 Assembly constituencies. As part of the social analysis, Tawde said office-bearers would have to understand the role and influence of social and religious organisations. Referring to factionalism in some districts, he said, “Avoid it. If you have any problem with someone, tell me privately.” ‘Analyse influential organisations and remain connected with people’ The exercise will include analysing which organisations have influence among people, which direction they are moving in, and what their internal meetings and public statements indicate. At the same time, party workers will have to maintain direct contact with people at the grassroots level. Explaining organisational analysis, Tawde said, “Every office-bearer from the booth level to the mandal and district levels must remain active. The party will also have to keep track of the activities of other political parties.” The district presidents with whom Tawde interacted included those from Deoria, Basti, Siddharthnagar, Kushinagar, Gorakhpur City and Gorakhpur district. ‘Turn difficult seats into triangular contests’ The meeting discussed a strategy for Assembly constituencies where the BJP may face a difficult direct contest. It was suggested that, at the local level, efforts should be made to create a three-cornered contest wherever possible. Similar electoral dynamics have previously affected contests in the region, where a divided opposition vote has influenced the outcome. The meeting also assessed that the Samajwadi Party’s position could be stronger than in the previous election and estimated that the party could begin the contest with more than 30% support. Focus on social media, young voters and local caste equations The meeting stressed that the BJP’s social media team should remain fully active. Any rumour or misleading information should be countered quickly with a factual response. The party was also advised to focus on young voters and study the local influence of Brahmin, Sainthwar and Nishad communities. The meeting also discussed reminding voters of past political experiences associated with Yadav-led governments.

stories.title: Suspended Jal Kal EE in Varanasi blames civic body:Minister suspended him over waterlogging; says pumps stopped due to flood
stories.summary: Varanasi Jal Kal's suspended executive engineer (EE) has questioned the action taken by Urban Development Minister AK Sharma. He said the waterlogging was caused by the Municipal Corporation's negligence, but he was made the scapegoat. The pump was shut down on 20 August after correspondence. This is done every year because of flooding. If everyone knew about this, how could it be my fault? Following his claim, Dainik Bhaskar visited the 140 MLD pump house in Chaukaghat to understand how it operates. It also tried to find out where the negligence occurred and whether the Jal Nigam or the Municipal Corporation was more responsible. Read the report... Pictures of the pump house Now read what suspended Executive Engineer (EE) Pawan Kumar Gupta said and what questions he raised... Pawan Kumar Gupta, who was posted at the 140 MLD pumping station in Chaukaghat, has now been attached to Kanpur. An inquiry is under way against the Jal Nigam EE. Speaking over the phone from Kanpur about his suspension, he raised a major question and said, Why is action being taken against a Jal Nigam engineer for the Municipal Corporation's negligence? The grounds for the suspension are not valid EE Pawan Kumar Gupta said, The grounds on which I was suspended are not valid. The reality is something else, but the issue has been diverted elsewhere. Sewers in the city are clogged, which is causing waterlogging. They do not have the resources to prevent waterlogging. Action was taken against us to conceal this fact, even though we operated the pumps. Chaukaghat pumping station built near the Varuna river Pawan Kumar Gupta said, The pumping station at Chaukaghat is near the Varuna river. This time, the Varuna's water level reached 71 metres. The entire area was waterlogged. Several times, Varuna's water has also entered the pump house. In such a situation, when we run the pumps, will we be able to pump out Varuna's water? Why has the water level of the Varuna risen? In such a situation, no matter how much we pump, it will not make any difference. So how will the sewage water be pumped out? They are accusing us to conceal their own shortcomings The suspended executive engineer said, All the sewers of the municipal corporation are choked and full. This is causing waterlogging in the city. To hide their own shortcomings, they have blamed us and said that the pump is not working. But when the Ganga's water level has risen, the pump cannot do anything. A large pumping station and a retaining wall should be built here. This is meant for sewage pumping, but they are making us pump floodwater. Find out what Ajay Kumar Sinha, the site in-charge of the Chowkaghat pumping station, said, Sewage from several parts of the city goes to the STP from here Ajay Kumar Sinha said, This is a 140 MLD sewage pumping station (urban). It mainly handles sewage collected from several places. Sewage lines from Phulwaria, the Cantonment, Lahurabir and several other parts of the city have been connected here. We pump it from here, separate the garbage and pump it to the STP. Primary treatment is carried out here before the sewage is sent for treatment. The garbage is then separated, after which it goes directly to the STP. Pumping stations are shut down during floods Ajay further said, This pumping station is related to river pollution. It was built to prevent the river from being polluted. The water from the city's drains and sewers used to flow into the rivers. It has to be intercepted and sent to the STP from here. This area lies along the Varuna, and when flooding occurs, the water level rises and the river merges with the drains. In such a situation, pumping is stopped so that no problem is caused in the river. We will not be able to treat that water because treating the river water and releasing it back into the river would serve no purpose. Letter issued on 20 August itself Ajay said that all pumping stations along the riverbanks are shut during floods. This station is operational. It is shut during floods, but when there is no flooding, it is not shut. This time, when the Ganga's water level rises above 68 metres, the line to this 140 MLD pump station is closed because of the reverse flow from the Varuna. Water from the Varuna then begins flowing into it. This year too, as in the past, our executive engineer received an order from the Dinapur STP stating that the river and drain had met on 20 August. It should therefore be shut and maintenance work carried out. It should be restarted once the water level falls. Heard of this for the first time in six years According to Ajay, this is the first time in six years that it has come to light that the closure of the SPS has caused waterlogging somewhere in the city. This is a new issue for us as well, so it is impossible to say anything at this stage. According to the documents and records available to us so far, whenever floodwater has arrived, not only this station but all pumping stations along the Ganga in the city have shut down.

stories.title: UP MLA Pooja Pal duped of ₹1.55 lakh:Money withdrawn via PhonePe; says personal data also at risk
stories.summary: Around ₹1.55 lakh was fraudulently withdrawn from the bank account of Pooja Pal, MLA from the Chail constituency in Kaushambi and BJP State Vice-President. The amount was deducted in multiple transactions between 22 August and 13 September via PhonePe and UPI. The MLA came to know about this on 14 September. Upon inspecting her bank account statement, several transactions were uncovered that had been executed without her knowledge. Following a complaint lodged by the MLA, an FIR was registered at the Dhoomanganj police station in Prayagraj on Friday at 2 pm. Money withdrawn multiple times over 22 days The MLA, Pooja Pal, holds an account with the Union Bank of India branch in Dhoomanganj, Prayagraj. She informed the police that money was fraudulently withdrawn from her account multiple times between 22 August and 13 September. The MLA suspects that someone hacked her iPhone 17 Air and misused her banking and personal data. The police, with the assistance of the cyber cell, are examining the mobile device, PhonePe, UPI, and bank account details. Demand for investigation into transactions and mobile device The MLA has requested the cyber crime police to conduct an investigation into all PhonePe and UPI transactions made between 22 August and 13 September. She has urged for a technical audit of her mobile phone, along with a review of all transaction IDs and bank account details. Furthermore, the MLA has demanded that future unauthorized withdrawals from her account be prevented and that the stolen sum of approximately ₹1.55 lakh be recovered. Copies of the complaint have also been submitted to the Cyber Crime Police Station in Prayagraj, the Dhoomanganj Police Station, and the manager of the concerned bank branch. The police are currently investigating the matter.

stories.title: SP MP’s car pelted with stones, windows smashed:Chaos during Ganesh immersion in Sant Kabir Nagar; people angry over DJ's detention
stories.summary: In Sant Kabir Nagar, a crowd vandalised the vehicle of SP MP Laxmikant alias Pappu Nishad during the immersion of a Ganesha idol. The mob surrounded the vehicle and smashed its window. Police safely evacuated the MP from the crowd. The incident occurred on Friday night at around 11 pm. The immersion procession had reached the Amardobha crossing. Meanwhile, the police began taking the DJ to the police station. Outraged by this, people sat on the road in protest. Just then, the MP's vehicle was passing through the area. The angry crowd surrounded his vehicle and vandalised it. Following the incident, a heavy police force was deployed in the area. Additional Superintendent of Police Sushil Kumar Singh and the Additional District Magistrate arrived at the spot and reasoned with the people. The incident took place within the jurisdiction of the Bakhira police station area. The MP stated, “All three of my vehicles were vandalised and stones were pelted. The miscreants are protected by the ruling party. They attacked after seeing the party flag and because I belong to a lower caste. Upper-caste people cannot tolerate how a man from a lower caste became an MP. A life-threatening attack was made on me.” A DJ was accompanying the immersion procession According to local residents, the Ganesha idol immersion procession had set off from Bakhira town. The procession was heading towards Dhodhaya Canal via Amardobha. Just then, Mehndawal CO Sarvdaman Singh arrived at the spot. It is alleged that the CO took photographs of the DJ vehicle accompanying the procession and spoke of taking it to the Bakhira police station. Outraged by this, the people participating in the procession sat on the road in protest. It was during this time that the mob attacked the MP's vehicle. Following the attack on the MP's vehicle, the occupants inside it were also enraged. They sat on the road and raised slogans against the police and administration. Officers from the police and administration reached the spot and brought the situation under control. The MP stated: Stones were pelted after seeing the party flag The MP said, "I was returning after meeting flood victims and other people. I was stuck in a traffic jam at the crossing. Just then, slogans of 'Pappu Nishad Murdabad' started being raised. Seeing the party flag, people began hurling bricks and stones at the vehicle. I got out of the car and ran towards the market to save my life. When the police saw the vehicles being vandalised, they resorted to a lathi charge. I somehow reached the police station and went home from there."

stories.title: Lucknow’s Papermill Colony has cleanest air in India:70 parks; residents formed groups, planted trees with own money
stories.summary: An unique initiative by residents of Lucknow's Paper Mill Ward has made the entire city proud. The residents formed groups, raised funds and created gardens in every home. The ward is numbered 70 in the municipal corporation. Working with the municipal corporation, they built 70 parks across the area. The project took around 20 years. But the results have now emerged. Paper Mill secured the number one rank in the Ministry of Environment's Air Survey 2026. This means its air is the cleanest in the country. The residents have created vertical gardens in the parks and planted trees using the Miyawaki method. Waste in the ward is collected only using electric vehicles. As a result, air pollution here is nearly zero. The ward has a population of around 60,000. Residents here say, The title of having the cleanest air in the country was not achieved in a single day. We worked hard for years to achieve it and paid attention to cleanliness. This result has come from caring for the ward together. How is the air in the ward so clean? To find out, a Bhaskar reporter surveyed the neighbourhoods. The survey found that the ward has remarkable greenery. It has beautiful parks, trees along the roads and no piles of rubbish anywhere. Homes of all sizes have gardens. The drains are clean, and the roads are free of dust. Five pictures of the ward with the cleanest air in the country- Extent of Papermill Colony Ward: Residents said: Prabha Chaturvedi also contributed to this recognition Prabha Chaturvedi, a resident of the ward, is no longer alive, but people are now praising her work after the ward received the honour. Residents say Prabha had launched a campaign to increase greenery in the ward. Shekhar Malviya said people here had developed the area using their own money. Prabha Chaturvedi was among them. Her efforts transformed the condition of the parks. People became aware of environmental issues. The ‘Greenery in Every Home’ campaign was launched. Work was undertaken on rainwater harvesting and making compost through kitchen-waste management. She initiated these efforts along with providing training. She also worked with women on cleanliness. She died in 2021 during the coronavirus pandemic, but people are now remembering her work. Her family currently lives abroad. 3 major reasons behind the country's cleanest air title Vertical gardens and Miyawaki gardening reduced air pollution Vertical gardens, plantation along roads and riverbanks, and forests developed using the Miyawaki method are being created in the ward to reduce air pollution. Urmila Van and Shakti Van are among the prominent ones. Encroachments and garbage are being removed along the Kukrail river, after which plants are being planted using the Miyawaki method. These forests have improved the air quality in the ward. They have also enhanced the beauty of the area. The parks have been landscaped properly. Better maintenance has further improved their appearance. This has increased the greenery in the area and cleaned the air. Water is sprayed every day to prevent dust from becoming airborne Water is sprinkled daily in the ward to prevent PM-10 pollution particles generated by road dust. As part of efforts to raise awareness, nets are installed at construction sites to contain construction and demolition waste. These nets are later removed properly. Roads within the ward are cleaned more effectively. All major roads are cleaner. In addition, the drains and smaller open drains are covered. PNG lines have been installed for clean fuel in large parts of the ward, including Nehru Enclave and Vishwas Khand. LPG is also used in homes across the ward. Electric vehicles collect waste, with real-time tracking through GPS Electric vehicles (e-auto tippers) have been introduced in place of the old diesel waste-collection vehicles. GPS has been installed in all the vehicles, and a control command centre has been set up for their real-time monitoring. This has improved waste collection in the ward. Waste is no longer piling up inside homes or on the roads. It is not dumped in the open. Waste is collected at only two compactor stations. These are located at Mithaiwala Chauraha and Metro City police outpost. Dustbins have also been placed at various locations in the neighbourhoods. Sewer and water pipelines have been laid throughout the ward, providing convenience to residents. What residents of the ward with the cleanest air have to say- The councillor heeds the elderly, while residents contributed their own money Shekhar Malviya said that for the past several years, elderly residents have been sitting on chairs by the roadside with the councillor from the morning and informing him about the work that needs to be done. Local councillor Rajesh Singh Gabbar implements it. There is greenery around every house here. The colony is old. Its residents have improved it with their own money, so work has continued to be carried out. This is not a one-day effort. Residents work themselves to keep the ward clean Girish Chandra Tiwari said that our ward ranked number one in the country. The biggest reason for this is the parks in our area. They are all clean and well-maintained. People here keep the areas around them clean and tidy. They work towards this themselves. The parks have facilities ranging from exercise equipment to other amenities, which help people stay close to nature. People are called out when they make mistakes; the change did not happen in a day Swati said that the people in her ward are hardworking. No other ward has as much greenery as this colony. The reason the colony is clean and beautiful is that everyone is working towards this with awareness. If anyone makes a mistake, they are stopped from doing so. Residents are also partners, but sanitation workers deserve praise Hemendra Singh Rawat said, I have been living in the colony for 60 years. Relentless efforts have been under way for 20 years. Work has been carried out for the ward since Rajesh Singh became the councillor. The public also contributes to these efforts. Construction and demolition waste is being stored properly. Besides us, we congratulate the workers who work from morning to keep the city clean. Councillor says - made possible by public awareness Rajesh Singh Gabbar, councillor for the Papermill Colony ward, said, Under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP), the Papermill Colony ward has been ranked No. 1 in the country among wards with a population of more than 30,000 in the Swachh Vayu Survey 2025-26. This has been made possible by the cooperation and awareness of the people in the area. It was my dream for our ward to become the most beautiful ward in the country, with clean air and cleanliness. That has now become possible. I am grateful to all the people for this. For the past 20 years, the people have been guiding me. We have all continued to work together accordingly. This is why we have received this distinction. Congratulations to everyone. Three more pictures of the ward-

stories.title: Ayush says, ‘I will marry Chandni at any cost’:Court approves marriage; her family says they were framed in Shamli
stories.summary: Ayush Malik, a resident of Shamli, told the Allahabad High Court that he had embraced Islam of his own free will. Ayush also expressed his desire to marry his girlfriend, Chandni Qureshi. The court permitted him to do so and said, An adult cannot be prevented from making decisions regarding their religion, residence and choice of life partner solely on the grounds of family opposition. Ayush's father is a prominent medicine trader in the city. A photograph of Ayush wearing a skullcap and offering namaz had gone viral. Hindu organisations protested after this. Ayush's father accused Chandni Qureshi of forcing him to convert. The police also sent several people, including Chandni and her father, to jail. After the court's ruling, Dainik Bhaskar spoke to Chandni's family. Read the report... Chandni's aunt's sons were also sent to jail Our team reached the home of Chandni Qureshi, who lives in Azad Chowk. We met Chandni's sister there. She said their father had gone to the market and that her elder sister was in Noida. Chandni's aunt's house is 100 metres from their home. Her aunt's son Mohammed Salim, her brother Tausif and some neighbours were sitting there. Tausif was also sent to jail in this case. Mohammad Salim said, Chandni is my maternal uncle's daughter. The Bharat Medical Store is 2 km from her home. Devraj Malik's son, Ayush Malik, used to sit there. There is a hospital next door where Chandni worked as a physiotherapist. Ayush used to bring his mother there. Ayush was the one who tried to trap Chandni. Maternal cousin said: Ayush trapped Chandni Mohammad Salim said that Chandni had made it clear from the outset: ‘We are Muslims. You are Jats. We have nothing to do with you and no relationship with you. Nor do we want any ties with you.’ Despite this, Devraj Malik had us framed as part of a conspiracy. He used Chandni as a pawn. He had us falsely implicated and sent to jail. He dragged not only us into the case, but also the family's elder paternal uncle, younger paternal uncle, maternal aunt's sons and the entire family. What is our fault? If we had even the slightest role or fault in this case, they could have shot us at a crossroads. Salim said - If she had wanted to frame him, she could have had a court marriage Salim said that if Chandni had really wanted to frame Ayush, she could have had a court marriage with him, but she did not do so. The boy had been converting to Islam and growing a beard for 12 years - did his father and family not know about it? Even the brothers and paternal aunt's sons have been framed in the case. How could people who cannot sign arrange a nikah? We have been rendered homeless. The locks on our house were broken and the police and administration were let inside; people entered the house by jumping from the roof. This is outright oppression against poor people like us. If the same oppression had happened to someone else, what would they have gone through? Shamli SP Narendra Pratap Singh said that the matter is before the court. The police are not intervening in the matter at present. Action will be taken if any complaint is received. Now, know the full story Devraj Malik, a resident of Dayanand Nagar, is the president of the Chemists Association in Shamli district. He owns a house in the city's upscale area and two well-known medical stores in the city. His two daughters are married. His son, Ayush Malik, ran a medical store after completing a BPharm. On 6 June, Devraj Malik lodged a report at the Kotwali police station. He alleged that Chandni Qureshi had lured his son into a relationship and had him converted. She had his name changed to Mohammed Ali. Ayush had suddenly started changing his appearance. He first grew a beard and then began going to the mosque. A photograph of Ayush also surfaced, showing him offering prayers at a mosque. He was seen sitting at the medical store wearing a skullcap and a kurta-pyjama. FIR filed after protests by Hindu organisations Swami Yashveer, the mahant of Yog Sadhana Ashram, released a video. He said that Chandni Qureshi had trapped the only son of the owner of Bharat Medical Store. Under pressure, the entire family had converted to another religion. After the matter came to light, Hindu organisations began protesting and threatened to stage a sit-in outside Chandni's house. Police had registered an FIR against eight people in the case, including Chandni Qureshi, her father Islam Qureshi and three maulvis. On 7 June, police arrested three accused, including Chandni Qureshi and her father. After spending one and a half months in judicial custody, the father and daughter were granted bail by the court on 24 July. He became a Hindu again after performing religious rituals just 15 days later About 15 days later, Ayush released a video. He said, Mother, seeing your distress, I have returned of my own accord to my original religion, Hinduism. Please forgive me. On 9 September, Ayush's friend Mohammad Sultan filed a petition in the Allahabad High Court. He alleged that Ayush was being forcibly confined at home. The court ordered Ayush's father to produce him before the court on 16 September. Expressed desire to convert to Islam before the court On 16 September, Ayush Malik was produced before a bench of the Allahabad High Court headed by Justice Sandeep Jain. Ayush said, I am around 31 years old. I have studied up to BPharm. I converted to Islam of my own free will in 2014. I want to marry Chandni Qureshi. My father and family do not approve of this decision. Ayush alleged that he had received threats and had been kept under house arrest since June 2026. His father, Devraj Malik, rejected all his son's allegations outright. He said that some people had ‘brainwashed’ his son. As a father, he is deeply concerned about his son's future. Court says Ayush has the right to make his own decisions The court said Ayush Malik is an adult and fully capable of making decisions about his own life. It said he had converted his religion of his own free will, without any pressure or threats, and had decided to marry Chandni Qureshi. The court acknowledged that it was natural for Devraj Singh Malik to be concerned as a father. However, this concern cannot override the constitutional rights of an adult citizen. Therefore, Ayush has the independent right to live with a person of his choice according to his wishes, practise his religion and make decisions regarding marriage in accordance with the law. Father says-he will remain my son After the High Court's order, father Devraj Malik said that Ayush Malik is and will remain his son. He cannot live without his son. The High Court's decision is acceptable to him. ‘I want Ayush to live with his family.’ However, no statement from Ayush Malik has emerged in the matter so far.

stories.title: Lohia Trust becomes important for Akhilesh before polls:Took control after staying on sidelines since 2016
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav was recently elected president of the Lohia Trust, which owns the Samajwadi Party’s headquarters, district offices and several other properties and has a fund of around ₹800-1,000 crore; the trust also played an important role in the formation of the Samajwadi Party. During the 2016-17 feud, when then state president Shivpal was pushing Team Akhilesh out of the party, Akhilesh formed the Janeshwar Mishra Trust, while, as the dispute intensified, Mulayam Singh removed his cousin Ram Gopal Yadav, who was supporting Akhilesh, from the Lohia Trust and made his own brother Shivpal its secretary. Mulayam remained its president until his death. After his death, Shivpal became its head, and now the reins are in Akhilesh's hands. There is also discussion that his elder daughter, Aditi Yadav, could become part of the trust. Today, in the UP Explainer, read what changed in the trust's funds, properties and politics from the 2016 family battle to the present. What message is behind handing over its reins to Akhilesh? Question 1: What is the history of the Lohia Trust? Why is it important for Akhilesh? Answer: Let's understand the entire story of the Lohia Trust, from its formation to the present, in three parts... (A) The situation before its formation (B) Lohia Trust became the vehicle for the formation of the SP (C) Mulayam's Lohia Trust vs Akhilesh's Janeshwar Mishra Trust Question 2: How much property does the Lohia Trust have? Answer: There is no official figure available for the trust's bank accounts. As a non-governmental charitable trust, its balance sheet is not made public. After Akhilesh became the SP chief, the importance of the Janeshwar Mishra Trust increased. Funding has also shifted towards it. Question 3: What is the strategy behind changing the Lohia Trust president before the election? Answer: It is being viewed as an attempt to bring family coordination and Mulayam Singh's legacy under one roof ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. The strategy can be understood as follows...

stories.title: Will UP Congress president be removed?:‘Chair’ tussle between 2 senior leaders; Rahul Gandhi to take final call
stories.summary: Political activity over the organisational leadership of the Uttar Pradesh Congress has intensified ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. There are two possibilities being discussed: First: State Congress president Ajay Rai could be removed. Second: He could remain in the post, with three to four working presidents sharing responsibility with him. Discussions are reportedly underway over this formula. State in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam claims that the party leadership is considering the options and that major decisions could be taken by September 30. On the other hand, Ajay Rai says he has no information about any organisational change at the state level. Read the full report... Why the discussion about changing the president is gaining momentum UP in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam is reportedly presenting social equations before the high command. The argument being put forward is that Ajay Rai belongs to the Bhumihar community, whose population in the state is very small. To win the 2027 election, it is being argued that the Congress needs a face with a larger and broader vote base. Gautam himself belongs to the Dalit community. His strategy is reportedly to target Uttar Pradesh through a Dalit-Brahmin or Dalit-OBC combination. In this proposed change, the name of Pramod Tiwari's daughter and MLA Aradhana Mishra is gaining momentum. Both want to distribute tickets according to their own preferences Party insiders claim that the entire battle is not about the organisation but about retaining control over ticket distribution in the upcoming election. If an alliance is formed with the Samajwadi Party, Ajay Rai wants his close associates to get as many tickets as possible. Meanwhile, state in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam is trying to field candidates of his choice. However, both leaders have publicly denied any such factionalism. When did the differences between the two leaders become visible? 1. Different claims over alliance with SP and seat-sharing Discussions about Ajay Rai's future began after the Congress replaced Brahmin leader Avinash Pandey with Dalit leader Rajendra Pal Gautam as its UP in-charge. Ajay Rai has been the state president for around three years. During this period, he visited different districts of the state to strengthen the organisation and focused on building the organisation at the grassroots level. After Gautam's arrival, his involvement in the Congress's strategy for seat-sharing with the Samajwadi Party also increased. Gautam advocated negotiating for an equal number of seats with the SP, while Ajay Rai continued to emphasise preparing the organisation across all 403 Assembly seats in Uttar Pradesh. 2. Rai unhappy over attempt to meet Mayawati In May 2026, Rajendra Pal Gautam suddenly reached BSP chief Mayawati's residence to meet her. Some other Congress leaders and MPs were also with him. However, Mayawati did not meet them. At the time, it was described as an attempt to initiate dialogue among Dalit leaders. Ajay Rai openly expressed his displeasure over this. He said he had no information about whose permission Gautam had taken before going to Mayawati's residence. 3. Differences intensified after district presidents' list emerged Although Rai and Gautam were seen smiling together at the 'Lok Hunkar' programme in Lucknow on September 2, discussions about differences intensified within a week. According to party sources, Gautam objected to the list of district presidents prepared under the 'Sangathan Srijan' campaign. There is discussion that he sought greater representation for Dalit, OBC and minority communities. 4. Separate joining programmes by both leaders on the same day On September 9, three prominent leaders were inducted into the Congress at the party headquarters. State in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam merged the Jan Sardar Party of Siddharthnagar leader Hemant Chaudhary with the Congress. BJP leader Manoj Kumar Chauhan and Harvansh Singh Chauhan were also inducted into the Congress. On the same day, at 11 am, state president Ajay Rai himself inducted retired IAS officer Dr Rakesh Verma and South Indian film actress Firdaus Bano, also known as Zara Khan, into the Congress. Three options before the high command, which one will be approved? Rajendra Pal Gautam travelled to Delhi on September 10-11 and held a lengthy meeting with Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi and organisational general secretary KC Venugopal. There are now three options before the high command: First: Remove Ajay Rai and hand over the state leadership to a Brahmin, OBC or Dalit face. Second: In view of the party's performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, retain Ajay Rai as state president. The strongest argument in Rai's favour is that the party won six Lok Sabha seats under his leadership. He himself gave Prime Minister Narendra Modi a tough contest in Varanasi and led at different stages for a total of seven rounds during counting. Third: Instead of taking the risk of changing the president just four months before the election, retain Ajay Rai but appoint three to four working presidents alongside him to maintain a balance. These could include Brahmin, Dalit, OBC and Muslim faces. Will the 'experiment' in Bihar and Jharkhand weigh on the decision? In March 2025, around seven months before the Bihar Assembly elections, the Congress changed its state president. The party replaced Akhilesh Prasad Singh with Dalit leader Rajesh Kumar as state president. In the election results, the Congress fell from 19 seats to six. Similarly, in August 2024, around three months before the Jharkhand Assembly elections, the Congress replaced Rajesh Thakur with OBC leader Keshav Mahto Kamlesh as state president. In the election, the Congress retained its 16 seats. If Ajay Rai is removed as Uttar Pradesh Congress president, the change would mark the Congress's third major experiment with organisational leadership ahead of an Assembly election.

stories.title: 'Mohammed Shami's brother lives with me as husband':Says he promises marriage after IPL selection; now refuses relationship
stories.summary: A Lucknow woman has accused Indian cricketer Mohammed Shami’s younger brother, Mohammed Kaif, of rape. Kaif is also a cricketer and plays domestic cricket. An FIR for rape has been registered against him at Ashiyana police station. The woman said: “Before filing the FIR, I called Kaif for the last time from outside the police station. I wanted to know if there was still any possibility of us getting married. But now, I will never become part of his family… They should understand what a woman’s dignity means.” The woman spoke to Dainik Bhaskar about how her relationship with Kaif began, her conversations with Shami’s family and the entire dispute. Read the full interview… Question: Where did you first meet Kaif? How did the marriage talks begin? Woman: I met Kaif in 2020 through a common friend. He liked me, so we started talking on social media. Our meetings increased in 2023, and he told me that he wanted to marry me. He often said, “I will marry you once I get selected for the IPL.” When he was not selected, I asked him whether he would still marry me. After that, his behaviour changed and he started avoiding the issue. Question: Were you in touch with Kaif’s family? Did you ever speak directly to Mohammed Shami? Woman: When we were in a relationship, I also spoke to Mohammed Shami and other members of his family. But when his family refused to agree to the marriage, Mohammed Shami spoke to me using his elder brother’s phone number. He clearly said that the marriage could not happen. Question: Did you ever have a dispute with his family over your relationship with Kaif? Woman: I had mentioned my relationship with Kaif on a podcast on a sports channel. After that, I spoke to Kaif’s elder brother, Mohammed Haseeb. In May 2026, Kaif told me that he would marry me if I got the podcast deleted. After this, I met Kaif’s mother and his brother Haseeb at the home of his coach Badruddin in Moradabad. During the meeting, they said many hurtful things to me. It felt as though they had a problem with our relationship. Question: How often did you meet Kaif during your three-year relationship? Woman: I worked in the aviation sector, so I travelled to different states for work. Kaif would also call me to places where he travelled for his matches. We stayed together in several cities, including places in Uttar Pradesh, Kolkata, Hyderabad and Delhi. Our relationship was like that of a husband and wife. He never made me feel that he would betray me like this. Question: Why did you leave your job? Was there any pressure from Kaif? Woman: Kaif did not like me working as cabin crew at all. Later, after a lot of difficulties, I started working in Dubai, but he had problems with that too. I then started living under mental stress and could not focus on my career. Question: What did you speak to Kaif about just before filing the FIR? Woman: I last spoke to him on May 30, 2026. After that, when I went to Ashiyana police station in Lucknow to file the FIR, I called him one last time while standing outside the police station. I asked him if there was still any possibility of us getting married. But he clearly refused. Question: If Kaif or his family now agrees to a settlement and offers to marry you, what would your response be? Woman: I will never go to speak to him myself again. They should understand what a woman’s dignity means. I have neither any forgiveness left for him nor any possibility of living with him in the future.

stories.title: Elderly man stabbed to death outside Lucknow police station:Deceased had confronted a street vendor for driving on the wrong side
stories.summary: An elderly man was stabbed to death in front of Madiyaon police station in Lucknow on Saturday afternoon. His grandson was taking him on a bike to pay a bill when a handcart vendor came towards them from the wrong side. As soon as the grandson asked him, "Where are you coming from on this side?" the vendor became angry and attacked him with a knife. The grandfather, who was seated behind his grandson on the bike, got off to save him. The handcart vendor stopped attacking the grandson and began stabbing the grandfather instead. He stabbed the elderly man five times in the stomach and chest with full force, causing chunks of flesh to protrude. He collapsed and died at the scene. The incident took place at 1 pm under the flyover in front of Madiaon police station. See 2 pictures- Retired from the municipal corporation 16 years ago The elderly man was Magan Bihari Tiwari of Bharatnagar. He had retired from the municipal corporation around 16 years ago, in 2010. He had been a supervisor in the RR department. At around 1 p.m. on Saturday, he was heading to the power house with his grandson, Sankalp Tiwari, to pay a bill. On the way, Sankalp got into an argument with a scrap dealer who was arriving on a three-wheeled cart, in front of Madiyaon police station. During the argument, the scrap dealer attacked Sankalp with a knife. Magan Bihari stepped forward to save his grandson. The scrap dealer repeatedly stabbed him as well. The knife penetrated several places in his abdomen and chest. Chaos broke out at the scene. People informed the police. The scrap dealer fled before the police arrived. Eyewitnesses said Rajkumar alias Malai committed the murder Madiyaon police said eyewitnesses reported that 40-year-old Rajkumar alias Malai stabbed the grandfather and grandson. He currently lives around Markandeya Dharamshala in Keshavnagar and buys scrap from neighbourhoods. According to police, teams have been deployed to apprehend the scrap dealer. He will be arrested and questioned about the motive for the murders. Pradeep Tiwari, the son of Magan Bihari, is also a supervisor in Zone 2 of the municipal corporation. He said, "I was in the office when my mother called and told me that my father was unwell. She asked me to come to Highway Hospital. When I reached the spot, I learnt that someone had stabbed my father. He had gone out with his son, my nephew, to pay the electricity bill." Injured Grandson Is Studying in Intermediate, Daughter Reached Hospital Magan Bihari's family includes his wife, Maya Tiwari, son Pradeep Tiwari, daughter-in-law Pushpa, and three grandchildren. At the time of the incident, his eldest grandson, Sankalp Tiwari, was with him. He is currently studying in intermediate. The family has been inconsolable since the incident. After receiving the information, his elder daughter Poonam also reached the hospital. She broke down after seeing her father's body there.

stories.title: Ajay Rai picked up on way to meet trader’s family:He questions why Dhananjay was not arrested in the codeine case
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai was stopped by police while travelling to Gonda to meet the family of businessman Vinod Sahni, who was killed. He was travelling with a convoy of six vehicles on Saturday afternoon. Police stopped him beyond the Shahabpur toll plaza at the Barabanki border and did not allow him to proceed. Ajay Rai became angry and argued with the police. Angrily, he said: "If there is a written order, show it. Why are you stopping me from meeting the family? I am going to share the family's grief. What have you done to the strongman Dhananjay Singh in the codeine cough syrup case? You have not been able to arrest him to this day. You are stopping me." Ajay Rai remained adamant about proceeding. The police then detained him and brought him to Masoli police station. As soon as he reached the station, he sat on a sit-in protest. On learning this, around 200 Congress workers from Gonda and Barabanki also reached the police station. Congress workers continued the sit-in for around one and a half hours. At 3:30 p.m., Ajay Rai ended the protest after the police persuaded him and returned to Lucknow. See 3 pictures- Congress leader says - We will definitely meet the family Ajay Rai had announced on Friday that he would travel to Gonda. The police became alert after this. Barricades were put up at the Shahabpur toll plaza and 100 police personnel were deployed. When Ajay Rai's convoy arrived at 1:20 p.m., Circle Officer Colonelganj Narendra Pratap Rai and Kotwal Narendra Pratap stopped it. In addition, several Congress leaders in Gonda were placed under house arrest. Pramod Mishra, former Gonda Congress district president, said, "We will meet the family, but before that, the police have started harassing us. Under no circumstances will we be prevented from visiting the victim's family home." Now, understand the full matter Videos and photos of Dhananjay with a drug smuggler had emerged Photos and videos of strongman former MP Dhananjay Singh with drug smuggler Amit Tata, who was arrested in Lucknow around nine months ago, had surfaced. However, Dhananjay Singh later issued a clarification, saying that a conspiracy was being hatched against him and that the CBI should investigate the smuggling of codeine-mixed intoxicating syrup. Ajay Rai has targeted Dhananjay over this case.

stories.title: Man hung upside down and beaten after visiting girlfriend:Saharanpur attackers tied him to a pole for 12 hours, freed him after taking ₹5 lakh
stories.summary: In Saharanpur, the family members of a man who had gone to meet his girlfriend caught him. They tied him up with a rope and hung him upside down. They beat him for around half an hour, then tied him to a pole. His family learnt about the incident in the morning and reached the spot. A village council was then held. The council took ₹5 lakh from the man's family in exchange for releasing him. A video of the incident emerged on Saturday. It shows the man hanging upside down from a rope, with several people standing nearby. The man repeatedly tries to hide his face. The incident took place in the Mirzapur police station area. Based on the video, police are trying to identify and arrest the accused. See 2 pictures... Now, the sequence of events in detail... The young man went to meet someone on the night of 9 September The young man is from the Mirzapura police station area. He is married. On Wednesday night (9 September), he went to the nearby village of Kasimpur to meet his girlfriend. During this time, the girl's family members caught him. The young man was first tied up with a rope and then beaten while being hung upside down. Someone recorded a video of the entire incident. Family began searching when he did not return home overnight The young man's family became worried when he did not return home overnight. They began searching for him. During this time, they learnt that the young man was in Kasimpur village and was being beaten. The young man's family then reached the spot. Discussions began to pacify the situation between the two sides. During this time, money is reportedly said to have been discussed in the name of releasing the young man and ending the dispute. The victim's family claims that ₹5 lakh was demanded. Of this, ₹3 lakh was taken by the girl's family and ₹2 lakh by intermediaries. Case reaches senior police officials Despite talks and a settlement, the young woman's family handed the young man over to the police. The police then began questioning him. It is alleged that despite a video emerging of the young man being hung upside down and beaten, a case was not immediately registered against the accused. Senior police officials have been informed about the entire sequence of events. On the officials' instructions, the victim has been called to Saharanpur and details of the entire matter are being gathered. Mirzapur police said the man is being questioned. Further action will be taken if a written complaint is received and the allegations are found to be true during the investigation.

stories.title: Supporters climb trees to see MP Chandrashekhar in Lucknow:Says ‘I won’t fill anyone’s maang until brothers’ demands are met’
stories.summary: The protest by panchayat assistants at Lucknow's Eco Garden continued on Saturday. Protesters arrived at the sit-in carrying umbrellas to protect themselves from the harsh sunlight. Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad also reached the protest site to support the panchayat assistants. Some of his supporters climbed trees to see him. Chandrashekhar Azad said, "Until my brothers' demands are met, I will not marry anyone." Panchayat assistants from different districts across the state have been sitting in protest over their demands for a week. They are seeking an increase in their honorarium and the fulfilment of other service-related demands. The panchayat assistants said they handle online and administrative work at the gram panchayat level. In return, they receive an honorarium of ₹6,000 per month. They are demanding that it be increased to ₹30,000 per month. They alleged that despite the low honorarium, they are being made to do more work and are being exploited.
