stories.title: Mayawati to promote niece Deepika, not nephews, in politics:Says she stands against dynastic politics like Kanshi Ram; 50% tickets for Gen Z in 2027
stories.summary: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) supremo Mayawati may hand over the reins of the party to her niece, Deepika Anand. Mayawati herself said this on Saturday. She stated that neither of her nephews, Akash and Ishan, will hold any political post in the party. In the future, her nephews' children will not receive any posts either. If her brother Anand Kumar requires a member's assistance, he can take the help of his only daughter, Deepika Anand (Mayawati's niece). Based on her honesty, loyalty, and competence, she may be entrusted with responsibilities in the party in the future. Mayawati said that, like Kanshi Ram, she will remain firm against dynastic politics. Deepika is currently studying law. Playing the Gen-Z Card to Counter the Fallout from Akash To hedge against potential losses from Akash Anand's expulsion, Mayawati announced plans to allocate up to 50% of tickets to Gen-Z in the 2027 Assembly elections. Mayawati stated that in the upcoming Assembly elections in UP, Uttarakhand, and Punjab, priority will be given to dedicated, young, and capable candidates from all sections of society. Mayawati said—BSP's objective will be to rapidly strengthen Ambedkarite politics and constitutional values in the country through the new generation. She appealed to party workers to prioritize the youth along with worthy individuals from all sections of society while selecting candidates, emphasizing representation for both women and men. If the Daughter is Unwilling, Responsibility Will Go to a Dalit Missionary Worker Mayawati clarified that if Deepika is not ready for this responsibility, her brother Anand may hand over the charge to another missionary worker from the Dalit community with the party's general consensus. However, this responsibility will not be given to his sons or their future children. "If I were not a woman, I would not have kept even my brother with me" Mayawati said—If I were not a woman, I would not have kept even my brothers and sisters with me. Due to being a woman, to avoid safety and other issues and to work in the party with dignity, I had to keep my youngest brother Anand with me. However, despite the circumstances now emerging regarding my brother's family members, I will not fall into any attachment. I will not let the party suffer any loss. "Like Kanshi Ram, I too stand firm against dynastic politics" Mayawati linked herself to Kanshi Ram's political legacy. She said—Just as Kanshi Ram stayed away from dynastic politics, I too stand firm on this principle. In the BSP, an individual may be given an opportunity based on their merit. However, under that pretext, other members of their family will not be given political benefits. The purpose of this is to keep the BSP free from dynastic politics and to connect as many people from all sections of society as possible with the movement for social change and economic liberation. Focus on Gen-Z and Gen-Alpha for 2027 Mayawati has indicated plans to increase the participation of youth in the party organisation as well as prioritize young faces in the Assembly elections. In this, particular emphasis has been placed on keeping the needs of Gen-Z and Gen-Alpha at the centre of politics. She also referenced the tenures of previous BSP governments. She stated that along with roads, electricity, water, education, health, government jobs, employment, schools, hospitals, and urban and rural development, work was also done on the needs of the youth. Mayawati claimed that during BSP governments, facilities such as schools, colleges, universities, hostels, training centres, and parks were expanded. As a result, forced migration was also largely curtailed. Blamed Rivals for Not Returning to Power in 2012 Mayawati also referred to the 2012 Assembly elections. She stated that owing to the alleged casteist attitude of opposition parties, the BSP could not form the government for a 5th time in 2012. People across all sections of society still regret this today. Following the BSP government, 'rule of law by law' could not be established in the state. People's lives remain full of hardships. Questioning the government's claims of development, Mayawati said that merely blowing the government horn does not fill people's stomachs. Advised Caution Against Social Media Propaganda Mayawati asked party workers to remain cautious of propaganda running across opposition parties, organisations, and media-social media. She alleged that tactics such as persuasion, bribery, division, and force (Saam, Daam, Dand, Bhed) could be employed to prevent the BSP from forming a government in UP. She appealed to the workers to remain dedicated to the Ambedkarite mission with their complete body, mind, and resources. Dismissed Reports of Expelled Leaders' Return as ‘Fake News’ Mayawati also rejected discussions circulating on social media regarding the return of leaders expelled from the party. She stated that for the past few days, propaganda has been spread claiming that individuals expelled due to indiscipline and anti-party activities would be taken back into the BSP. Such people will not be readmitted into the BSP.

stories.title: Bus crushes child to death in front of mother:Was waiting for school bus in Gorakhpur; female teacher held hostage, 3-hour uproar on road
stories.summary: A school bus ran over a five-year-old child in front of his mother in Gorakhpur on Saturday morning. The mother was waiting for the bus to drop her child at school. The speeding school bus then arrived and, after running over the child, continued on out of control. Family members took the child to CHC Pipraich, where doctors declared him dead. Meanwhile, after the accident, the driver tried to flee with the bus. When villagers chased him, he stopped the bus around 200 metres away and fled. Angry villagers held the schoolteacher travelling in the bus hostage and vandalised the vehicle. The commotion continued for around 3 hours. The people calmed down after officials who reached the spot assured them of action. The accident took place at 8 a.m. in Naiyapar Buzurg village, under Pipraich police station limits, 20 kilometres from the district headquarters. See the pictures... Read the full story now... Soni lives with her family in Naiyapur Buzurg in Pipraich. Her in-laws also live with her. Soni's husband lives in Mumbai, where he works in painting and polishing. Soni, the child's mother, said, "My five-year-old son Himanshu studied in Class 1 at SD Public School in Chauri. He woke up on Saturday morning to go to school. I prepared his lunch and then began waiting outside the house for the school bus to arrive." At 8 a.m., an SD Public School bus (UP52T0177) suddenly arrived at high speed. It ran over my child right in front of me and drove away. I raised the alarm. The villagers nearby then surrounded the bus from the front and stopped it around 200 metres away. The children also began shouting. The villagers held the teacher who was sitting in the bus hostage, while the driver fled the spot. The villagers smashed the bus windows and began creating a commotion. Pipraich police, who arrived after receiving the information, tried to pacify the people. When the police arrived around three hours later, they took the teacher to the police station along with the bus. Family demands ₹1 crore and a government job After the accident, SDM Gyan Pratap Singh, Tehsildar Dr Bhagirathi Singh and Naib Tehsildar Anu Singh reached the spot. During the commotion, the family members handed a memorandum of demands to the SDM. The mother, Soni, said, "A compensation of ₹1 crore should be paid, and one family member should be given a government job." CO Chauri Chaura Kundan Singh said: “We received information about the accident at around 8:30 a.m. today. A five-year-old boy, Himanshu, was waiting for a bus to go to school when the accident involving a school bus occurred. A case is being registered in this matter.”

stories.title: Woman dies six months after love marriage in Ghaziabad:Footage shows her falling from roof; brother alleges husband pushed her for Scorpio
stories.summary: A woman died in Ghaziabad six months after her love marriage. Her brother has alleged that her husband beat her for not receiving a Scorpio as dowry and then pushed her from the second floor. She died on Friday after undergoing treatment at a hospital for four days. As soon as they learned of the woman's death, her husband, parents-in-law and two sisters-in-law fled. Police have registered an FIR against all five and begun searching for them. A video of the incident also emerged on Saturday afternoon. It shows the woman suddenly falling from the roof at night. People nearby can be seen taking her to hospital. The incident took place in the Muradnagar police station area. The deceased has been identified as Akriti Singh. Her husband, Gaurav (25), works at a factory in Noida. Two images of the woman falling from the roof... Now read the full case in detail... The accused, Gaurav, owns a three-storey house in Muradnagar. He lives there with his parents and two sisters. Prabhat, the brother of Aakriti, a resident of Bhangel, said, "My sister's marriage to Gaurav was fixed on 20 February. At the time, Gaurav had demanded ₹30 lakh in cash and a Scorpio as dowry." "We could not afford to give such a large dowry, so we refused. The two sides also reached a settlement at Muradnagar police station in the matter. The marriage was subsequently called off, but Gaurav and Aakriti continued speaking on the phone." Brother said Sister had married against the family's wishes The brother said, "Two months later, the couple married at a temple against the family's wishes. Gaurav then brought Aakriti to his home. The family was initially upset but later accepted the marriage." Everything was fine between the two for a few days. Gaurav then started demanding a Scorpio from Aakriti again. He would ask her to get a Scorpio from her family. When Aakriti refused, he would assault her. Brother said: Sister told him over the phone, ‘All these people are beating me.’ Prabhat said that Aakriti called him on 7 September and said, "All these people are beating me." Shortly afterwards, Gaurav called and told him that Aakriti had fallen from the roof. He asked them to reach a hospital in Ghaziabad quickly. When they reached the hospital, Aakriti was in a critical condition. After four days of treatment, she died on the night of 11 September. Case registered against five, including husband After Aakriti's death, her family lodged a case at Muradnagar police station against her husband, Gaurav; father-in-law Ramesh, mother-in-law Saroj, and sisters-in-law Soni and Neha. Police reached the spot, conducted an investigation and sent the body for post-mortem. DCP (Rural) Surendranath Tiwari said that police were investigating the circumstances surrounding the woman's death. An FIR had been registered against her in-laws on the basis of the complaint.

stories.title: Three-star hotel gutted in Meerut fire:People flee to save lives, 2 cars parked outside burn; flames reach Indian Bank
stories.summary: A fire broke out at a three-star hotel in Meerut around 11.30am on Saturday (12 Sept). The blaze started in the parking area of Abika Hotel under the Partapur police station area and quickly spread to the hotel, engulfing 12 rooms. The sight of flames and thick smoke triggered panic among people in the surrounding area. As the fire began spreading towards the adjoining Indian Bank branch, chaos also broke out there. Six fire brigade vehicles reached the spot after receiving information about the incident, and firefighters began efforts to bring the blaze under control. The entire hotel was evacuated and everyone inside was brought outside. Hotel furnishings and two cars gutted in blaze The fire completely destroyed the hotel’s luxury furnishings and two cars parked in the parking area. A short circuit is being cited as the immediate cause of the fire. No casualties have been reported so far. See three pictures of the fire... Hotel fire spreads towards Indian Bank, eight fire tenders deployed Avika Hotel, located on Delhi Road under Partapur police station limits, is owned by advocate Arvind Bhati, who had rented it to Kumari Nandwani aka Bunty. Around 11.30am, a fire suddenly broke out in the hotel’s parking area. Fire spreads from cars to hotel rooms and party hall The fire initially reached the cars parked in the parking area. An Eon and a Brezza were gutted in the blaze. The fire then spread rapidly, with flames reaching the first floor from the ground-floor party hall. Within a short time, the entire hotel was engulfed. All 12 rooms and the belongings inside were destroyed. Thick smoke and flames could be seen from a distance, triggering panic among people in the surrounding area. Flames move towards adjoining Indian Bank branch During the blaze, flames also began spreading towards the Indian Bank branch adjoining the hotel. Panic broke out as the fire moved towards the bank. Preventing the flames from spreading to the bank became a major challenge for firefighters. Eight fire tenders bring blaze under control Eight fire brigade vehicles reached the spot after receiving the alert. Firefighters began operations from different sides and managed to prevent the flames from spreading towards the bank. The blaze was brought under control after around 30 to 60 minutes of efforts. No major damage to the bank has been reported. Short circuit triggers fire, flames spread from sofas to upper floors Hotel guard Ratan Pal Singh said the fire started in the parking area due to a short circuit. The fire first broke out in the sofas before the flames spread upwards. The tin sheets above also caught fire, after which the blaze spread to the vehicles parked in the parking area. Guard and owner suffer burns while trying to douse fire Ratan Pal said he and the hotel owner were the only people present when the fire broke out. Both tried to extinguish the blaze but suffered burns to their hands in the process. When they failed to bring the fire under control, they alerted the fire brigade. Six fire tenders rushed to the spot Six fire brigade vehicles reached the hotel after receiving the alert and began efforts to control the blaze. No customers at hotel, estimated loss of nearly ₹1.75 crore He said no customers or other people were present at the hotel when the fire broke out. The hotel has 25 rooms, including three store rooms. At present, only 12 rooms are being rented out. According to Ratan Pal, property and other belongings worth nearly ₹1.75 crore were damaged in the fire. It took around two hours to bring the blaze under control. Police confirm no one was trapped inside SP City Vinayak Gopal Bhosle said police reached the spot as soon as they received information about the fire. The hotel has 12 occupied rooms, and all staff members and guests were evacuated in time. He said all the rooms were checked. There were rumours that some people were trapped inside the hotel, but the search found no one trapped. No casualties were reported in the incident.

stories.title: Youth murdered in public, accused’s house bulldozed:Meerut father sits with son’s body on road; married 4 months ago
stories.summary: The family has staged a sit-in after their only son was murdered in broad daylight in Meerut. They are raising slogans against the police and administration. They say they will not perform the last rites until the alleged killers are killed in a police encounter. On Friday, six attackers who arrived on two motorcycles shot dead 22-year-old Nitin in broad daylight, 200 metres from Hastinapur police station. He was shot in the leg and collapsed, bleeding heavily. He died after losing a large amount of blood. The father's health deteriorated after he saw his son's body, and he collapsed unconscious. His wife was inconsolable. When the police arrived at the scene to take the body into custody, the family refused to hand it over. Police personnel tried to persuade them throughout the night, but they did not agree. From 7 a.m. on Saturday, around 500 people joined the family in blocking the road at Ganeshpur Tirahe in Hastinapur, with the body placed there. They said, "We will not leave this place until bulldozers are used at the accused's homes and they are killed in a police encounter." After receiving the information, Hastinapur MLA and Minister of State Dinesh Khatik reached the spot and began trying to persuade the family members. He assured them that strict action would be taken against the accused. Immediately afterwards, the police began demolishing one of the accused's houses with a bulldozer. At present, police forces from five police stations, including Rural SP Abhijeet Kumar, are present at the spot. See three pictures... First, let us understand the entire case in sequence- Nitin killed in friend Prince's dispute His family members said Nitin's friend Prince lived in Hastinapur. Two days earlier, he had a dispute with his neighbour, Vivek Vardhan alias Pinky Chaudhary, over a route. The two sides had fought. A settlement was then reached in the presence of the police. On Friday, Pinky's elder brother Satya alias Miththu attacked Prince along with his associates. Prince escaped, but Nitin was killed. The police are searching for the killers. The father of accused Miththu is reportedly a clerk in the Education Department. Meerut SSP BBGTS Murthy said: “Four teams have been deployed to arrest the accused. The attackers will be arrested soon. The reason for the murder appears to be a two-day-old road-rage incident. The accused have been identified. Police teams are conducting raids to trace them.”

stories.title: Wife and daughters refuse last rites of former CRPF jawan:Say 'will immolate if killers not gunned down'; sit with petrol cans
stories.summary: After the murder of former CRPF jawan Amaresh Bahadur Singh in Ballia, his wife and three daughters have refused to perform his last rites, keeping his body at home for 16 hours while demanding action. His eldest daughter, Kritika Singh, is sitting beside the body with a can filled with petrol. She said the killers should be killed in an encounter and their house demolished with a bulldozer. "If the bulldozer is not brought in by 12 noon today, all three of us sisters will pour petrol on ourselves and self-immolate alongside our father." SDM Sharad Chaudhary and police personnel are trying to persuade the family. The wife said- "Blood must be avenged with blood. My husband was brutally murdered in front of my eyes. The accused fled. The police have not been able to arrest them yet. My husband was the family's only breadwinner. The family is now facing a financial crisis. We should be provided financial assistance." In fact, neighbours murdered former CRPF jawan Amaresh Bahadur Singh (45) on Thursday night. His brother, who came to save him, was also attacked in an attempt on his life. He is in a critical condition. The body arrived home from Mau on Friday evening. The family then began protesting, demanding action. Amaresh had taken VRS from the CRPF on 31 March this year. The incident took place in the area under the jurisdiction of Ubhaon police station, 70 km from the district headquarters. See three pictures – Daughter says, "There is no one left in my family to perform the last rites" The elder daughter, Kritika Singh, said, "It was dark at the time of the incident. My sister Ritika and I kept screaming. Our father fell to the ground injured right in front of our eyes. The accused also beat my uncle Manjesh Singh so severely that he is fighting for his life. There is no one left in my family to perform the last rites." Kritika said around 24 hours had passed since the incident, but there had been no update on the action taken so far. Two of the accused are still absconding. If the accused are not being arrested, their house is right here-why is it not being demolished with a bulldozer? "I saw my father get injured and collapse before my eyes" The younger daughter, Ritika, said her father was attacked in front of her. She demanded strict action against the accused. Ritika said she could not save her father. The accused also assaulted her and threatened that they would return and harm the family. Neighbours had torn open the abdomen of the former CRPF jawan Former CRPF jawan Amresh was a resident of Doth Sonadih village in the Belthara Road area. His family comprises his wife, Kanchan Singh, and three daughters: Kritika (21), Ritika (18) and Roshni (16). His brother, Manjesh Singh (35), also lived with them. The two brothers ran a dairy farm near their home. Amresh was at the dairy farm on Thursday. His neighbour Girish Singh then arrived with his wife, Sheila, their two sons, Karan and Suraj, and daughter Khushi, and began hurling abuses. When he objected, the entire family attacked Amresh. They knocked him down, beat him and stabbed him, leaving him seriously injured. Brother on ventilator support, 3 arrested, 2 still absconding When Mangesh went to save him, he too was attacked. Amresh died in hospital. Mangesh is undergoing treatment on ventilator support at BHU in Varanasi. After the murder, police arrested Khushi, the daughter, Sheela Singh, the wife, and Suraj, the son of named accused Girish. Girish and his son Karan are absconding. Three police teams have been formed to arrest the two absconding accused. The teams are conducting raids at likely hideouts. SP meets family, says strict action will be taken SP Omkar Singh went to the family's home to meet them on Friday evening. He said strict action would be taken against the accused. He added that he would speak to the SDM to arrange financial assistance from the Chief Minister's Discretionary Fund for the family's upkeep.

stories.title: IIT engineer’s body lay in flat for 4 days:Lived alone in Gorakhpur; younger brother in US, father was irrigation department officer
stories.summary: The body of a 45-year-old IIT engineer was found on the sofa in his flat in Gorakhpur on Friday morning (11 Sept) after neighbours alerted police when a foul smell began coming from the flat. Police broke open the door and found the body, which they said was three to four days old; however, the post-mortem examination also failed to establish the cause of death. The incident took place at Malhar Apartment in Sahara Estate. As soon as he learnt of engineer Abhishek Tripathi's death, his younger brother Ambreesh set off for Gorakhpur from the United States. The last rites will be performed after he arrives. Abhishek lived alone in the flat. He had lost his job four years ago and had been struggling with mental health issues since then. His younger brother, who lives in the United States, supported him financially. He had not married. His father, Sabha Tripathi, had retired as an executive engineer from the Irrigation Department. Their parents are dead. Their younger brother, Ambreesh, is an IT engineer in the United States. Their elder brother, Ashutosh, was a security guard for former Bihar Chief Minister Rabri Devi. He died of an illness in Chennai in 2014. Their sister, Gudiya, lives in Gorakhpur with her husband. Lost his job at a multinational company and slipped into depression Archana, who reached the spot after the incident, said, "Our father was originally from Mahason village in Kushinagar, but he was posted in the Irrigation Department in Gorakhpur. That is why we all studied here. Our father died 16 years ago. Three years later, our mother also passed away." Abhishek was academically bright. He studied engineering at IIT and worked for a multinational company in Noida. During the COVID-19 period, he moved to Gorakhpur because of work from home. He lost his job four years ago. After that, he began to remain distressed and gradually slipped into depression. His family arranged treatment for him in Lucknow, but the problem did not go away completely. His illness changed his behaviour, prompting people to distance themselves The sister said that Abhishek's behaviour had changed because of his illness. At times, he would speak to people in abusive language. This affected his relationships, and visits from relatives and acquaintances became less frequent. His younger brother, Ambareesh, used to send him money, which covered Abhishek's expenses. Ambareesh and I would visit him from time to time. Neighbours said he had become isolated and spent most of his time in his room According to neighbours, Abhishek had become isolated. He spent most of his time in his room and did not speak much to anyone. He had not been seen for three to four days. On Friday, the neighbours informed the police after a foul smell began coming from the flat. When the police broke open the door, they found his body inside. CO Keerti Nidhi Anand said- Abhishek had not left the flat for three to four days. The door was locked from the inside. The cause of death has not yet been established. The post-mortem report and other evidence are being examined. The room was found in disarray. The mobile phone is locked, and attempts are being made to unlock it.

stories.title: Programme held to ensure youth participation:Students take part in Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue in Varanasi
stories.summary: The Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue (VBYLD) quiz was organised at Jagatpur PG College in Varanasi on September 11. The programme aimed to connect as many young people as possible with the campaign and encourage their participation. College students enthusiastically registered for the quiz during the event. Focus on youth participation The programme encouraged students to understand the role of young people in building a developed India and participate actively in the campaign. Organisers stressed the need to involve more young people in the quiz, while student registrations were also conducted on the college campus. Faculty members encourage students Dr Sanjay Pradhan, Lieutenant Dr Suresh Kumar Singh, Dr Chandrashekhar Pandey, Dr Ankur and Dr Anamika, among other faculty members, attended the programme. They encouraged students to participate enthusiastically. Students also showed keen interest in the quiz during the event.

stories.title: Azam Khan’s close aide, SP leader Dakku left isolated:Raids underway to trace close aide, city president; he writes letter detailing his pain
stories.summary: Jafar Amin, aka Dakku, never held a major post in the Samajwadi Party, but his political stature remained significant because of his close ties with the party’s Muslim face, Azam Khan. Although he never appeared to stake a claim to the posts of district president or city president, Dakku remained influential whenever the SP was in power, with his influence clearly visible within the party. He is currently in jail. Azam Khan is also in jail. This close aide of Azam has now been left isolated within his own party. A letter he wrote from jail has gone viral, and it also reflects his pain that his party is not standing by him. His close aide, Shabbir Qureshi, is the city president and is absconding in the same case; police are conducting raids in search of him. The matter is also within the knowledge of the SP national president, but no public statement has yet been issued by him either. In Dakku's letter, current district president Brajesh Kumar Gautam is in the crosshairs. Taking a sharp swipe at his efforts, he even said that Gautam should not come to meet him in jail. He also said that three councillors should not come either. One of them is considered his opponent. Dakku now wants to somehow manage the matter and get out of jail. For this, he has been knocking on the doors of some BJP-linked leaders from time to time. The Samajwadi Party's district president has also hinted at this. First, find out the case in which Dakku is in jail Dakku is in jail for allegedly attempting to seize land and threaten his opponent. However, he claims that he purchased the land in question through a registered sale deed and has the documents to prove it. Even on the day the incident took place and the video went viral, he remained unconcerned until 9:30 p.m. The police had also summoned both sides in the case with their documents. Until then, there was no indication that any action would be taken. Then, suddenly, an FIR was filed late at night, and Dakku was arrested from his home at midnight. Ten days have passed, but he remains in jail. Samajwadi Party city president Shabbir Qureshi had accompanied him in the same case. Shabbir is also named in the case but is absconding. Raids are continuing to locate him. On the first day, he was searched for in every corner of his house, including the fridge, cooler and wardrobe. Why has the SP been unable to speak out? Both leaders caught up in this case are prominent faces of the Samajwadi Party. Dakku is a senior SP leader, while Shabbir is the current metropolitan president. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav is aware of the matter and has been kept informed at every stage. He has also been informed about the letter sent by Dakku from jail on Thursday. The SP leader also knows that someone had gone to Gorakhnath Temple with a recommendation on his behalf. The SP leader has returned after meeting the SP chief in Lucknow, but no instructions were issued from his side. If there had been any instructions, they would have been visible on the ground. A senior Samajwadi Party leader explained the reason. He said the party considers the matter a personal issue involving Dakku. Secondly, while he remained influential, his relations with most leaders were strained. Because of his outspoken image, he no longer had good relations with several leaders. The most important reason is that the family involved in the dispute is also Muslim. Akhilesh Yadav, who is conducting his entire political campaign around PDA, is staying away from the issue for this reason. He has not issued any statement regarding his metropolitan president either. SP leaders say the organisation fears that if the matter is given too much publicity, it will give the BJP an opportunity. It will not be easy for the party to respond to allegations such as grabbing a Muslim's land. The party has therefore maintained silence for now. What did the SP district president say? After the letter went viral, the SP district president reacted sharply. In an emotional outburst, he had said that Dakku had not gone to grab land after asking either him or the party. By Friday evening, his tone had softened, but the sting of the letter remained. Describing Dakku as his elder brother, he said that if he was instructed not to visit him, he would follow that order. He said he had not spoken to the metropolitan president either. Every possible effort has been made for the party leaders. He said the matter was in the knowledge of the national president. The person with whom there is a dispute is also from the Muslim side. This is Dakku's personal matter. However, a leader named Janardan Chaudhary has criticised the SP district president on social media over the issue. He called the district president's statement childish. Dakku has contested elections twice Dakku is a heavyweight leader. In 1991, he contested the Assembly election from Gorakhpur City on a Janata Dal ticket and received 20.10 per cent of the vote. Shiv Pratap Shukla won the election, held amid the Ram temple wave, after securing more than 55 per cent of the vote. Dakku contested the election from the newly formed Gorakhpur Rural Assembly seat in 2012 and received 22.27 per cent of the vote. BJP candidate Vijay Bahadur Yadav won that election. Dakku was highly influential in the Samajwadi Party government from 2012 to 2017. Azam Khan was the Urban Development Minister, and Dakku held sway over Gorakhpur Municipal Corporation and the municipal councils in the district.

stories.title: LIC agent shot at repeatedly in Lucknow, condition critical:Bullet grazes head and hits hand; attackers flee scene
stories.summary: Two youths allegedly surrounded an LIC agent and opened rapid fire at him in Malihabad, Lucknow, leaving him seriously injured. The attackers fled after repeatedly firing at the insurance agent outside a shop in front of a petrol pump near Dhendhemau village; one bullet grazed his head, while another struck his hand. LIC agent Samendra Yadav (36) is a resident of Saifalpur village. He had gone to a mobile shop in Dhendhemau, 10 km from his home. The two youths, who were lying in wait there, surrounded him and opened fire. After receiving information about the shooting, the agent's family members also reached the spot. They took Samendra, who was found injured by the roadside, to the Malihabad CHC. After providing first aid, doctors referred him to the trauma centre. See 3 pictures- CCTV footage related to the incident has also emerged. In one clip, the attacker is seen shooting Samendra in the forehead and fleeing on foot, while in another, he is seen fleeing on a motorcycle with an accomplice. Police reach the scene after being informed of the incident; atmosphere of fear The firing in the middle of the road has created an atmosphere of fear among local residents. As soon as the police were informed of the incident, personnel from the Malihabad police station reached the scene. After inspecting the site, the police launched a search for the attackers. ACP Malihabad Gyanendra Singh said that the youth had sustained a gunshot wound. His family was with him. The family members were being spoken to. Legal action was being taken after obtaining a complaint from them. The person seriously injured in the shooting is married. Link being drawn to the death of a brother-in-law's pregnant wife On 25 May, Rupanshi Yadav, the wife of Samendra's brother-in-law Sudhir Yadav, died under suspicious circumstances. She was three months pregnant. The police are also linking the firing at Sumendra to that incident. It is suspected that after Rupanshi's death, her maternal family may have developed an enmity not only towards her in-laws but also towards Samendra. The investigation is under way. It may be noted that Samendra's brother-in-law's in-laws' home is near Dhendhemau, close to the scene of the incident. Today, Samendra had gone there from his home, around 10 km away. This gave those holding a grudge an opportunity, and they fled after shooting him. CCTV footage of the incident also emerges Some CCTV footage related to the incident has also emerged. In one clip, the attacker is seen shooting Samendra in the forehead and fleeing on foot, while in another he is seen fleeing on a bike with an accomplice. In the first clip, the attacker shoots Samendra in the forehead. A youth was waiting for him some distance away. After the firing, the attacker ran away, and the other youth also fled with him. The attacker youths had parked their bikes some distance away. They ran there, mounted the bike and fled the scene of the incident. Married five years ago, has a four-year-old son Insurance agent Samendra is one of three brothers. Amarendra is the eldest, the injured Samendra is the middle one and Narendra Yadav is the youngest. Samendra married Neha Yadav of Bhulbhula village around five years ago. They have a four-year-old son. After the incident, Samendra's father Umashankar Yadav, his wife Neha and his brothers have been inconsolable. Liquor shop salesman was murdered in the same village on 11 May On 11 May, Ajay Kumar Jaiswal, aka Rinku Jaiswal (35), a salesman at a country liquor shop in the same Dhendhemau village under the jurisdiction of Malihabad police station, was beaten to death with an iron rod. Exactly four months later, on 11 September, an LIC agent was shot in the same village.

stories.title: BJP to build narrative against SP, Congress in UP:BL Santosh, Vinod Tawde meet in Lucknow; Mission 2027 roadmap prepared
stories.summary: BJP Uttar Pradesh in-charge Vinod Tawde and national general secretary BL Santosh held a meeting with the party’s core group at the BJP headquarters in Lucknow on Friday (11 Sept). Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath was also present at the meeting. It was decided that the BJP would complete the first phase of its election campaign through the Seva Sankalp campaign, which will begin on Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday on September 17. The campaign will continue until October 17, with the government and party organisation reaching out to people with the achievements of the Modi-Yogi government. Ground situation to be assessed during campaign The party will assess the ground situation in Assembly constituencies during the campaign and mobilise workers for the upcoming election. The meeting, which lasted more than two hours, also focused on preparing a roadmap for Mission 2027. The BJP and its organisation will work together to form the party’s government in Uttar Pradesh for a third consecutive term. BJP plans counter-narrative against Opposition Two key issues were discussed during the meeting. The party plans to build a narrative against the Samajwadi Party and Congress among young people, Dalits and backward communities during the campaign. A strategy was also discussed to target the Opposition over issues including the alleged theft of offerings at the Ram temple, the UGC and the Gen-Z movement. Tawde, Santosh on two-day Uttar Pradesh visit BL Santosh and Vinod Tawde are in Lucknow on a two-day visit. This is Tawde’s second visit to Uttar Pradesh in the past seven days. Deputy Chief Ministers Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak, BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary and Organisation General Secretary Dharampal Singh were also present at the meeting. Modi, Shah and Nitin Nabin to visit Uttar Pradesh Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah and BJP national president Nitin Nabin will visit Uttar Pradesh in the coming days. Before the elections are announced, Prime Minister Narendra Modi is expected to hold one rally each in the Awadh, Kashi, Braj, western Uttar Pradesh, Gorakhpur and Kanpur regions. Major projects will also be inaugurated and foundation stones laid during these events. Amit Shah will also hold organisational meetings and rallies across all six regions, along with inauguration and foundation-stone-laying programmes. BJP president Nitin Nabin will hold conferences with booth presidents, Shakti Kendra in-charges and mandal presidents. Santosh, Tawde to assess ground situation Before this, BL Santosh and Vinod Tawde will visit all six regions and hold organisational meetings. Feedback will be gathered on election campaigning in Assembly constituencies, caste equations, the performance of incumbent MLAs and the position of the Opposition. The feedback will be used to strengthen the party’s strategy for the upcoming Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. BJP plans focused social media strategy for Gen Z, Gen Alpha The meeting also focused on shaping the party’s narrative on social media. The government’s achievements and the organisation’s work will be highlighted through reels and posts, while allegations raised by the Opposition will also be countered. A specific strategy will be developed to reach Gen Z and Gen Alpha and corner the Opposition on social media. State working committee meeting likely soon The BJP’s state working committee will be formed soon, and the appointment of its members was also discussed during the meeting. Once the members are appointed, a meeting of the state working committee will be held. BJP national president Nitin Nabin or Home Minister Amit Shah is likely to address the meeting. District in-charges, frontal teams to be appointed The meeting also stressed the need to appoint district in-charges soon so they can visit their assigned districts and take charge of organisational work. BL Santosh also emphasised the early formation of state teams for the Yuva Morcha, Mahila Morcha, SC Morcha, ST Morcha, OBC Morcha, Minority Morcha and Kisan Morcha. This will enable all the party’s frontal organisations to become active and strengthen preparations for the upcoming elections. BJP discusses election strategy for Uttar Pradesh BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary said the core group meeting focused on reaching every household through the Seva Sankalp campaign and communicating the government’s achievements to the public. It was also decided to convene the state working committee meeting soon. Preparations for the 2027 Assembly elections were discussed, with emphasis on strengthening the organisation at the grassroots level, reaching out to young voters and increasing the party’s presence on social media. BJP focuses on 134 seats across Awadh and Kanpur The BJP has shifted its focus to the Awadh and Kanpur-Bundelkhand regions, which together account for 134 Assembly seats. The party suffered significant losses in these regions during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, prompting the central leadership to give them greater attention ahead of the 2027 Assembly polls. Santosh, Tawde to visit Kanpur on Saturday BL Santosh and Vinod Tawde will travel to Kanpur on Saturday for a two-day visit. They will hold meetings with MLAs, MPs, Lok Sabha candidates, district presidents, district in-charges and regional office-bearers from the Kanpur region. They will also address a conference of booth presidents from the Govind Nagar Assembly constituency. Central command continues to camp in UP The BJP's central organisation has been keeping a close watch on every major and minor development in UP for the past few months-

stories.title: 24 gay men blackmailed with obscene videos, robbed:AMU student helps catch one accused; app-based gang active in Aligarh
stories.summary: A gang allegedly involved in blackmailing and robbing young men through a dating app has been busted in Aligarh, with the police investigation so far finding that 24 young men were targeted. Police have arrested one suspect, whose mobile phone contained obscene videos of 10 young men. The case came to light on Friday when a 19-year-old BBA student of Aligarh Muslim University (AMU) filed a complaint. The student alleged that he was assaulted in a hostel and blackmailed after an obscene video of him was recorded. Meanwhile, another victim also approached the police. As the modus operandi in both incidents was found to be similar, the police suspected that a gang was active. The police arrested one suspect based on the identification by the victims. Obscene videos of 10 young men were recovered from his mobile phone. The police are investigating the case. Now read the details... The student says, 'Friendship on app', then called to AMU hostel According to the BBA student, he received a friendship request on his Grindr app account. After they spoke, he was called to Vikar-ul-Mulk Hall at Aligarh Muslim University (AMU) to meet. The student alleges that after he reached the room, he was held captive and assaulted. An obscene video of him was also recorded. The accused blackmailed him by threatening to make the video viral and extorted ₹5,600 from him. Police have registered an FIR at Civil Lines police station on the student's father's complaint and begun an investigation. Another young man also fell victim through the app While the investigation into the student's complaint was under way, another young man from the Bannadevi area also approached the police. He too reported being blackmailed after coming into contact through the Grindr app. In both cases, the method was found to be the same: first contacting the young men through the app and then luring them to meet on the pretext of a meeting. The police subsequently expanded the scope of the investigation. So far, the police have obtained the names and addresses of 10 young men who were victims. First friendship, then a VIDEO... this is how the blackmailing was carried out How did the gang reach the AMU hostel? The biggest question in the case concerns how the gang gained access to the AMU hostel. According to the complaint, the BBA student was called to a room in Vikrarul Mulk Hall, although he himself lives in G.M. Hall. The police are therefore investigating how outsiders gained access to the hostel and with whose help the room was used. The police are also finding out whether the gang received assistance from any student or another person. The role of some outsiders and people linked to AMU is also being investigated. The investigation has been expanded to determine whether the gang's activities were limited to a single hostel room or whether its network extended further across the university campus. CO Sarvam Singh said: One accused has been arrested. Videos of 10 victims were found on his mobile phone. Digital evidence is being examined in the case.

stories.title: Daughter-in-law drank heavily on night of father-in-law’s murder:Danced with husband for 1.5 hours while drunk; Kanpur hotel owner says they ate grilled fish, mutton tikka
stories.summary: In Kanpur, the daughter-in-law and son of millionaire pharmaceutical businessman Vineet Minocha drank heavily on the night of his murder. While contract killers were allegedly murdering the businessman inside his home, his accused daughter-in-law Shalu was partying at a lounge with her husband Subrat. The lounge manager and waiter told Dainik Bhaskar that the couple spent around five hours there. After drinking, Shalu danced with her husband on the DJ floor for around one-and-a-half hours. She also ate grilled fish and mutton tikka. The staff said Shalu and Subrat appeared normal and happy throughout the party. When they learnt about Vineet’s murder the next day, the lounge staff were also shocked. Here is what else emerged from the conversation. Shalu told waiter to make food less spicy Pharmaceutical businessman Vineet Minocha was found murdered inside his flat on the night of September 5 after his throat was slit. Police said his daughter-in-law had allegedly hired domestic worker Vishal Gautam, a resident of Harbans Mohal, and his associate Rajkishore to carry out the murder. While the alleged contract killers were murdering the businessman at home, his daughter-in-law and son were partying at Cosmojin Lounge in Tilak Nagar. Lounge general manager Saurabh Tripathi told Dainik Bhaskar that Subrat had booked a couple’s party there for the first time on September 5. A regular customer of the lounge had introduced him to Subrat. The party was scheduled to begin at 11.30 pm, but Subrat and Shalu arrived an hour early at 10.30 pm. They then went to the first floor of the lounge, where they ordered starters to check the taste. The waiter served them Hariyali kebab, veg seekh kebab, grilled fish and mutton tikka. Shalu reportedly praised the grilled fish and asked for the food to be made less spicy. Shalu and Subrat danced to songs from the 1990s General manager Saurabh said Subrat’s guests began arriving at around 11.15 pm. Around 35 guests attended the party. After the party began, Shalu and Subrat started playing games with their guests. Drinks were also served during this time. Shalu and Subrat also drank heavily while playing the games. At around 1 am, everyone moved to the DJ floor and requested songs from the 1990s. Shalu and Subrat were seen dancing enthusiastically. Saurabh said the couple continued dancing on the DJ floor until around 2 am. As it got late, the staff told them that the food was getting cold. However, Shalu said she wanted to dance for some more time and asked the DJ to play her favourite songs. They began eating after around 2.30 am and left the lounge at around 3.30 am. Waiter said Shalu did not appear to be plotting father-in-law’s murder Sam, a waiter from Shuklaganj, was responsible for looking after all the guests at the party. He said he had been working at the lounge for the past four years. Both vegetarian and non-vegetarian dishes were served at the party. Sam said Shalu and Subrat particularly liked the grilled fish and chicken tikka and praised the food. He said the couple appeared very happy throughout the party. “Looking at Shalu, it did not seem at all that she was allegedly having her father-in-law murdered,” he said. The lounge staff were shocked when they learnt about the incident the next day and wondered what had happened. Domestic worker allegedly offered ₹6 lakh to carry out murder According to police, Vishal had been unemployed since 2022 and had a debt of ₹2 lakh. Around 20 days earlier, he had gone to Subrat’s house looking for work. Police said Shalu told him that she was troubled by her father-in-law’s behaviour, claiming that he constantly interfered in her affairs and had CCTV cameras installed in the house. She allegedly asked Vishal to either kill her father-in-law or arrange for his accident. He was a wholesale pharmaceutical trader and ran the business with his son Businessman Vineet Minocha lived with his family in flat C-104 on the first floor of Ratan Arbit Apartment. He ran a pharmaceutical firm named Pharma Traders on Birhana Road. Vineet managed the business along with his son Subrat. The firm had an annual turnover of ₹50-60 crore. His family includes his wife Puneeta, son Subrat, daughter-in-law Shalu and six-year-old grandson Shrijay. Puneeta is a marriage counsellor. Shalu and Subrat got married seven years ago. Police said Vishal initially did not agree to arrange an accident. Shalu allegedly then suggested that he should suffocate Vineet with a pillow while he was asleep so that people would believe he had died of a heart attack. She allegedly promised to give Vishal a job after the act and also offered him ₹6 lakh for carrying out the murder. Vishal then allegedly agreed to kill Vineet Minocha. Police said Vishal offered his friend Rajkishore ₹30,000 to join him, following which the two allegedly murdered Vineet Minocha on the night of September 5.

stories.title: Elections to be fought more on mobiles than on ground:BJP, SP devise strategies to expand reach in UP; Mayawati has better X strike rate
stories.summary: This time, the Uttar Pradesh Assembly election will be fought more on mobile phones than on the ground. People are understanding issues through reels, short videos and social media posts rather than long speeches by political leaders. The political power of social media became even more visible after the Gen-Z protests held in Delhi from June 6 to July 25. This is why BJP, SP and BSP have put their full strength into social media. Here are three reasons behind it: After SIR, the state has a total of 13.39 crore voters. Of these, 12.28 crore have smartphones. According to mobile network companies, around 90% of voters in urban areas and 65% in rural areas have smartphones. An average voter spends around 4-5 hours a day on social media. 1. BJP (UP): More followers, but low reach on routine posts X (Twitter): Looking at data from July 26 to September 10, normal posts from the @BJP4UP handle generally receive between 5,000 and 40,000 views. However, posts targeting Akhilesh Yadav and Rahul Gandhi perform better. A ‘The Priest King’ video posted on September 6 received 7.49 lakh views. Facebook and Instagram: The Facebook page generally receives between 100 and 300 reactions. On Instagram too, more than 90% of posts remain below 1 lakh views. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath is BJP’s biggest and most influential digital face. 2. SP: Strong reach despite fewer followers X (Twitter): Posts featuring press releases and government statements remain limited to 4,000-12,000 views, while videos related to Akhilesh receive 15,000-45,000 views. These figures are from July 26 to September 10. Facebook and Instagram: Clips of Akhilesh’s speeches on Facebook receive between 9,600 and 36,000 likes. On Instagram, SP has fewer followers than BJP, but its average likes per post are higher. 3. BSP: Mayawati’s direct hold on X X (Twitter): The @bspindia handle only retweets Mayawati’s posts. Its reach does not even cross 100. Facebook and Instagram: We could not find BSP’s official Facebook page. However, it posts on Instagram around once every seven days on average. Posts related to Akash Anand and Mayawati receive between 5,000 and 15,000 likes. Akhilesh has strong engagement, Mayawati has hold on X 1. Yogi Adityanath: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s social media accounts appear to have the highest reach among the three leaders. His posts on political statements, development projects and cultural issues receive lakhs and even crores of views. An Instagram post on September 7 received more than 1.2 crore views and over 10 lakh likes. 2. Akhilesh Yadav: Most posts by SP president Akhilesh Yadav are getting more than 1 lakh views. However, photo posts and short updates receive only 3,000-18,000 views. On Instagram, his reels and videos are reaching lakhs and crores of views. 3. Mayawati: BSP supremo Mayawati’s strongest hold is visible on X. Between September 1 and 10, most of her posts featuring statements received more than 1 lakh views. An Instagram post on September 6 received more than 10 lakh views. How BJP and SP are increasing their reach, what is their strategy BJP focuses on 30-second reels On September 10, BJP IT Cell national coordinator Deepak Mhaskey held a major meeting with the state team in Lucknow. BJP’s future strategy is as follows: People no longer watch entire speeches. Therefore, selected and sharp excerpts from leaders’ speeches will be turned into reels and made viral. BJP has prepared a large team of digital influencers. They are being paid according to their reach and number of followers. The party has acknowledged that the opposition was getting ahead in setting the narrative. New IT teams are now being formed at district level, which will respond to SP and Congress in their own style without using abusive language. SP focuses on real-time response SP’s social media team operates from the party headquarters in Lucknow, with office-bearers posted in every district. Whenever an incident takes place anywhere in the state, the local team immediately sends information and videos to the Lucknow team. SP leaves no opportunity to target the government. Through Akhilesh’s official pages, it directly sets an aggressive narrative. Social media is not just publicity, but also a test of claims Social media expert Anup Mishra says, “Digital content will play the most decisive role in the 2027 UP Assembly election. Gen-Z is checking the reality of every promise and claim on social media. If an issue gets support on digital platforms, it becomes an agenda for television channels and newspapers.”

stories.title: Why HC released properties of Mukhtar’s relatives:Is UP Gangster Act weak; what changes can govt make to law?
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court has released properties of Mukhtar Ansari’s relatives that were attached under the Gangsters Act. In a ruling in another case, the Supreme Court described the Act as ‘stillborn’, meaning a ‘dead law’ that died at birth. Comparing the Gangsters Act with Maharashtra’s MCOCA and Gujarat’s GCOCA, the court pointed out the legal shortcomings of the Gangsters Act. Read in today’s UP Explainer why the properties were released, what legal loopholes make the Gangsters Act weak, and what changes the government can make to the law… Question-1: Why did the Allahabad High Court release the properties of Mukhtar’s relatives? Answer: We will understand this in two parts. First, let us know which properties were released and in whose names they were… 1. September 2026: A bungalow worth around ₹2.5 crore in Dalibagh, Lucknow. It was in the name of Farhat Ansari, Mukhtar’s sister-in-law and wife of SP MP Afzal Ansari. The then Ghazipur DM had attached it in October 2022. 2. August 2026: Around 25 bighas of agricultural land, orchards, and a farmhouse in Machha and Shakarpur mauzas of Ghazipur, worth around ₹12 crore. These properties were in the names of nieces Nusrat, Nooria, and Maria, and sister-in-law Farhat Ansari. They were attached in 2022. 3. March 2026: 18 shops in Ghazipur worth around ₹28 lakh. These were in the name of cousin Mansoor Ansari and were attached in March 2023. Now, let us understand why the properties were released… Under Section 14 of the Gangsters Act (UP Gangsters and Anti-Social Activities Prevention Act, 1986), the DM can attach property even without a case being decided or the crime being proved, on the basis of a preliminary inquiry and police report. According to the Act, the DM must have ‘reason to believe’ that the movable or immovable property has been acquired with money obtained through crime. What constitutes ‘reason to believe’ has not been clearly defined. However, in court, it has to be proved that there is a direct link between the date of the crime, the illegal income generated from it, and the money used to purchase the property. This is called the ‘money trail’. In all these cases, the police could not establish this link. Question-2: What kind of legal loopholes did the SC point out in the Gangsters Act? Answer: In a judgment in a case on 21 August, 2026, the Supreme Court made several serious observations about the Act. It also explained why the law is technically weak… Definition of crime is not clear: The Supreme Court said the offences mentioned in this law are already punishable under the IPC and BNS. Therefore, the law does not define any separate offence; instead, it declares a person a ‘gangster’ and punishes them. This is its biggest shortcoming. A law made in the name of preventing violence appears, in several cases, to promote violence and repression against innocent people. Treating a person as guilty without a verdict: The court said that once provisions of the Gangsters Act are imposed, the process of arrest, prolonged judicial custody, trial, and punishment begins. In such a situation, the trial appears to become a mere formality, and the verdict seems to have been decided in advance. The person is defamed, and people begin to consider them guilty. Against the general legal principle: According to Supreme Court lawyer Virag Gupta, under MCOCA and other central laws, action to attach property is taken after the crime has been proved. However, under the Gangsters Act, property can be attached even before the trial begins, merely on the basis of the Act’s provisions being added to an FIR. The accused or property owner is not given a notice before the attachment. At the same time, the owner has to prove that the property is not ‘illegal’. This goes against the general principles of law. Loose standard for proving a crime network: Maharashtra-Gujarat laws continuously monitor the illegal activities of a crime network (gang). In contrast, the Gangsters Act is also imposed on petty or individual offenders. This takes the law away from its basic objective of dealing with ‘organised crime’. The Supreme Court had given a judgment in a similar case on August 21. Question-3: How is the Gangsters Act weaker than the Maharashtra-Gujarat laws? Answer: A comparison with Maharashtra’s MCOCA (Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act, 1999) and Gujarat’s GCOCA (Gujarat Control of Terrorism and Organised Crime Act, 2019) shows… Question-4: What changes can the government make to the Gangsters Act? Answer: No official draft for amendments to the law has been presented yet. However, considering the recent court judgments, Supreme Court lawyer Virag Gupta suggests that the following changes could be considered… Shortcoming 1: Clear definition of crime Technical point: The law needs to clearly specify which ‘act’ constitutes an offence. Sections 2(b) and 2(c) of the Gangsters Act only explain ‘gang’ and ‘gangster’, meaning they describe a ‘status’, not an act. Impact: Police can register an FIR by declaring the accused a ‘gangster’, even if there is no concrete or provable allegation. Possible reform: Section 2 could be amended to clearly specify (a) which acts constitute offences, and (b) how many incidents/FIRs are required at minimum to establish ‘continuity’. Shortcoming 2: Standards for property attachment Technical point: Under the existing procedure, the DM can attach property by declaring it ‘benami’ or ‘acquired through gangster activities’. Impact: According to the legal principle, the burden of proving that property is criminally acquired lies with the prosecution (police), not with the accused to prove their innocence. The existing procedure works in the opposite manner. Possible reform: (a) Before issuing an attachment order, the DM could be required to record a ‘preliminary evidence report’ showing a direct financial link (money trail) between the property and the crime. (b) If concrete evidence is not found within a specified time limit, a provision could be added for the attachment to be automatically cancelled. Shortcoming 3: Using only a family relationship as a basis Technical point: The Allahabad High Court has clearly said that property cannot be attached merely on the basis of an allegation or the owner’s relationship with a criminal. Possible reform: Mafias often purchase properties in the names of their drivers, employees, or relatives. A new amendment could create a legal mechanism for coordination with the Income Tax Department and the Benami Property Act to seize such ‘benami’ properties.

stories.title: Russian police ties up Kanpur engineer and abducts him:Threaten to kill him; tortured him for 48 hours, he says he will never go abroad again
stories.summary: A Russian police officer in Moscow detained a Kanpur-based engineer for 48 hours and tortured him. The engineer returned home to Kanpur with his wife and 10-year-old son on Thursday night. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, engineer Chandan Gupta said, “The police tied my hands and my friend’s hands and took us away in a police van. The officers abused us and threatened to kill us. “They took my friend to a separate room and beat him with sticks. We were not allowed to speak to our families. They did not provide us with a phone or a translator. The police falsely accused me of breaking the glass of an ambulance while drunk. Chandan said, “After this incident, I have no intention of going back to Russia for work. In fact, I will not go abroad for work again. I have been living in Moscow with my wife and son since 2023. Before that, I had also lived in Moscow for two years.” His wife, Sneha, said, “If the ambulance’s glass was broken, then where is the evidence?” Read the special report based on Dainik Bhaskar’s conversation with the engineer and his wife… Police tied my hands and took me away, seized my passport Engineer Chandan Gupta was working in Moscow on a high-qualified visa through a polyfilm company based in Noida’s Sector 62. He is a resident of Yashoda Nagar in Kanpur. His wife, Sneha, has studied LLB. Chandan said that on September 5, he went out for a walk with his friend Ashish and another friend after dinner. They were heading towards Kitay-Gorod Metro Station via the Hanging Bridge and Red Square when the police caught Ashish and him. Their other friend was a little farther away and managed to escape. The police then tied one hand of each of them and took them to a police vehicle parked around 400 metres away. During this, they also took Chandan’s mobile phone, passport, and other documents. Chandan said they repeatedly asked the police why they were being detained, but the policemen did not give them any answer. Police said I was drunk and had broken an ambulance window Chandan said that after making him sit in the vehicle, the police told him that he had broken an ambulance window. The policemen repeatedly said, “You broke the ambulance glass.” He asked them when and where he had broken the ambulance window. He was not shown any video or other evidence. The police also claimed that he was drunk, but he said he had not consumed alcohol. “The behaviour of the policemen was extremely inappropriate. They pushed me and threatened to beat me when I asked questions. My friend, who was detained with me, repeatedly asked the policemen why we had been arrested. He was then taken to a separate place and beaten several times with sticks.” No phone or translator provided until we went to court Chandan said the police vehicle carrying the two of them drove around for about an hour. On the way, the policemen stopped at one place and spoke to an officer. After this, they were taken to the Basmanny police station. Until around 1 a.m., they did not know what action was being taken against them. Chandan said they were not allowed to speak to anyone over the phone at the police station. They did not have their phones, and no translator was provided. He said they were not allowed to meet anyone until they went to court. According to Chandan, the language barrier made the situation even more difficult for them. However, he was confident that his family and company would be trying to help them. Police made us write and sign documents as they wanted Chandan said that before releasing them, the Russian police made them sign some protocols and documents. “The policemen said we had to write exactly what they told us. The police threatened me that if I did not cooperate, I would be released for now, but they could detain me again and seek a long remand.” “I was afraid that if I stayed in Moscow, I could be implicated in another case. That is why I decided to return to India with my family.” Chandan said he had been hearing about incidents of Indian nationals being harassed by police in Russia for around the past five months. His acquaintances and people from his company had told him that police stopped Indians, made them sit for several hours, and took their documents and money. Chandan says Indian Embassy did not even speak to him Chandan has also questioned the Indian Embassy in Moscow. He said that during the nearly 48 hours he was in custody, no official from the Indian Embassy contacted him. His wife, Sneha, had appealed to the Indian government for help through social media. Despite this, neither did any embassy official come to meet him nor did anyone speak to him over the phone about the incident. “What hurts me the most is that the Indian Embassy issued information based on the Russian police’s statement without even hearing my side.” Sneha asks: Where was the evidence before issuing the statement? Chandan’s wife, Sneha Gupta, has also questioned the Indian Embassy. She said that before issuing a statement about her husband, the embassy did not seek complete information about the incident from either her or her husband. “If Chandan had consumed alcohol, was he medically examined? If he broke the ambulance window, where is the video or photograph? What was the ambulance’s location and what was my husband’s location?” She said these questions should be answered. Sneha said that if Chandan has been accused of breaking the ambulance window, the evidence should be made public. She demanded that the Indian Embassy issue a clarification on the entire matter. Sneha said, “I want this matter to be investigated.”

stories.title: Class 4 student in UP made sister nude:Drew teacher’s dirty picture after watching porn; BTech student said, ‘Make me a girl’
stories.summary: A fourth-grade student undressed his seven-year-old sister, showed her pornography, and began sexually abusing her in Gorakhpur. Meanwhile, his mother entered the room and was shocked to see this. One day, the student also drew an obscene picture of a teacher at school. The principal then complained to his family, and the student's name was struck off the school register. The principal had advised the student's family to seek treatment for him. The family took the child to a psychologist, who told them that he was suffering from borderline personality disorder. He is currently undergoing treatment in Shahpur. In a similar separate case, an engineer also began insisting to his father that he be made into a girl. Child became addicted to mobile phone during online classes The student studied in Class 4 at a famous school in Civil Lines. According to his mother, he was given a mobile phone during online classes. He would play games for a while during his studies. For the past six months, he had been insisting on getting the mobile phone. He would start crying when he was not given it. The child gradually began taking the mobile phone to the bathroom and would sit inside for hours. When stopped, he would become irritable and angry. The child's family members said that one day he was found naked in the room with his sister. Classmates said: The boy talks obscenely to everyone When the family checked the mobile phone, a pornographic video was playing. The site was open, after which they explained to the child that such things were wrong. About two months ago, they received a call from his school. The principal asked them to come in. When they went to the school, they found out that their son had drawn an obscene picture of one of his teachers. The principal called the children who studied with him and asked them about his behaviour. The other children said that the boy spoke obscenely to everyone. Following this, the school management struck the child's name off the rolls and advised his family to get him treated. He would sit in the bathroom for hours watching pornographic videos Dr Aakriti Pandey, the psychologist treating the child, said that timely treatment is essential. Otherwise, the child could go on to pose a major threat to society. This is not the first such case to come to us. Numerous cases have been seen in which children want to become adults from an early age. They do not even know their own gender. Children develop this illness for various reasons. Their reactions also differ. In another case, a 27-year-old man from the Gularihya area wants to marry his male friend. His father says that the son's marriage had been arranged. However, he wants to marry a man. He has attempted suicide several times and has been undergoing treatment for a year. Engineering student in Gorakhpur wants to become a girl In a third case, a 21-year-old engineering college student is also suffering from borderline personality disorder. His home is in the Shahpur area. His parents are troubled by his behaviour. He repeatedly cuts his legs, leaving deep marks on them. The young man always remains silent. He suddenly becomes angry. He repeatedly tells his parents, "I want to become a girl. Get me operated on and change my gender." A psychologist counsels him every day.

stories.title: Explosion on BJP leader’s plot in Chitrakoot:3-ft-deep crater formed; leg and burnt clothes found 200 metres away
stories.summary: An explosion at a vacant plot owned by a BJP leader in Chitrakoot created a hole about 3 feet deep and 4 feet wide. Human body parts, burnt clothes and machine parts were found in the plot and nearby areas. A human leg was found in a field about 200 metres from the site. The incident took place on Saturday (12 September), but came to light at 2 p.m. on Monday. It is believed that a person was blown to pieces in the explosion. BJP leader Jagdish Gautam informed the police about the incident. Expert teams from Banda and Lucknow were then called in to investigate. The NIA and bomb disposal squads have also been involved in the investigation. The incident occurred in the Pahadi police station area. Read the full story... BJP leader owns a 10-bigha plot Jagdish Gautam owns a plot measuring around 10 bighas along the Karwi-Rajapur Highway in Assoh village. He is the president of the Disaster Relief Cell for the Bundelkhand-Kanpur province of the BJP. The plot is surrounded by a high boundary wall and has a gate. Shyam Sundar Yadav, a villager, looks after it. Shyam Sundar said that at around 6 p.m. on Saturday, he and his wife were grazing goats nearby. During this time, they heard a loud explosion. The sound could be heard up to around 3 km away. He and the villagers thought lightning had struck or that someone had set off an explosive to hunt wild boar. Therefore, no one paid much attention at the time. Severed leg found in a pigeon Pea Field When Shyam Sundar reached the plot late on Sunday evening, he found a severed and burnt human leg lying in the pigeon pea field. He informed BJP leader Jagdish Gautam. On receiving the information, police reached the spot, cordoned off the area and began an investigation. During this, charred and torn pieces of clothing were found on a tree around the plot. Shepherds said that another leg was lying in a field on the other side of the road, about 200 metres away. The police conducted an investigation there as well. Boundary and walls damaged in explosion On Monday, SP Arun Kumar Singh, Rajapur CO Fahad Ali and Pahari police station in-charge Nishikant Rai, along with SOG in-charge MP Tripathi and a forensic team, reached the spot. The investigation confirmed that an explosion had occurred at the site. The SP said, "The plot's boundary was found damaged. Clumps of human remains were found stuck to the walls and in the surrounding area. Some machine parts were also recovered along with burnt and torn clothing. However, other parts of the deceased's body have not yet been identified." Accident suspected during the use of explosives SP Arun Kumar Singh said, "The blast is suspected to have occurred while the explosive material was being stored or used. The explosion was very powerful, sending human body parts flying over a wide area. Police are also investigating the possibility that more than one person was present at the scene when the incident occurred. Information has also been gathered from police stations nearby about anyone reported missing over the past two days. However, no clear information has emerged yet." Police searching fields for human remains Some parts of the human body have not been found after the explosion. Police are searching for them in the surrounding fields. Officials believe that other body parts may also have been thrown far from the site of the explosion. The dense grass in the fields is making the search difficult. An investigation is under way to identify the human remains found at the site and determine the actual cause of the explosion. Jagdish Gautam contested the Assembly election on a Bahujan Samaj Party ticket in 2017, but suffered defeat. He later joined the Bharatiya Janata Party in December 2021. Jagdish Gautam currently serves as the regional convener of the Cooperation, Disaster Relief and Service Department in the BJP's Kanpur-Bundelkhand region.

stories.title: Minister Nishad targets ‘seasonal leaders’ carrying wads of cash:Says they are misleading fishing community; battle for Nishad votes intensifies
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh minister Sanjay Nishad launched a fierce attack on Vikassheel Insaan Party (VIP) national president Mukesh Sahni on Monday. However, Nishad did not name Sahni. He said, "Some 'seasonal leaders' have still not decided whether they will do business in Mumbai, roam around laying mats for others or continue brokering the votes of the fishing community, as they have done in their own state." For the first time since Independence, the fishing community in Uttar Pradesh has emerged as a political force. The Assembly election season has now begun. In such a situation, the community needs to remain cautious of leaders coming from outside. Someone who has been notorious in Bihar for buying and selling the votes of the fishing community; who eclipsed the political rise of fishermen there; and who is not capable of winning even a single Assembly election. Such a person has set out to mislead Uttar Pradesh's Nishad community by keeping bundles of currency notes in his pocket and wearing a red cap and blue uniform. Sanjay Nishad said: The fishing community is not a people that can be bought Sanjay Nishad said, "The fishing community is not a people that can be bought with money. Before teaching politics to fishermen in Uttar Pradesh, it must be understood that politics is in their blood. The fishing community may be poor, but it is not the son of a traitor. It is a community that fought the British and the Mughals, defeated them, helped free the country, and got the Constitution written. It also got reservation written into the Constitution." He said that the community's reservation had been plundered because of certain people and was still being plundered. The community is not being allowed to unite. Divisions are being created within it in the name of Kevat, Mallah, Bind and Kashyap. Anyone who takes money from other parties and distributes it within the community, while labelling people as "saleable" or "Piaau", is not truly a Son of Kevat but a "traitor son". Know the reason behind Sanjay Nishad's anger Tensions escalated after the Gonda incident The killing of Vinod Kumar Nishad, a member of the Nishad community, in Gonda is considered to be a key reason behind Sanjay Nishad's attack. Sanjay Nishad is reportedly angry with Mukesh Sahani over his activism in the case. After the incident, Sahani had reached out to members of the Nishad community and tried to turn it into a political issue. He had reached Lucknow with his family to stage a sit-in. In fact, Mukesh Sahani has been increasing his outreach among the Nishad community in Purvanchal for some time. He has been continuously raising issues related to the fishing community in an effort to strengthen his political base in Uttar Pradesh. Talk of an alliance with the SP is also making Sanjay uneasy Mukesh Sahani's increased activity ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections is considered significant because there has been speculation about an alliance with the Samajwadi Party. Sahani's party has been trying to establish its political identity among the fishing community and the Extremely Backward Classes vote bank in Bihar. In addition, a large number of Assembly seats in eastern Uttar Pradesh have a significant presence of the Nishad, Mallah, Bind, Kevat and Kashyap communities. In such a situation, Sahani's activism could become a direct political challenge for the Nishad Party. On the other hand, Sanjay Nishad has long been working to consolidate the Nishad community as his political base. He therefore sees any attempt by an outsider to make inroads into the same vote bank as a challenge to his political influence. Battle for the Nishad vote is now head-to-head On the one hand, Sanjay Nishad is projecting his party as the Nishad community's biggest political voice within its alliance with the BJP. On the other, Mukesh Sahani is becoming active in Purvanchal and trying to bring the same social base over to his side. Against this backdrop, the political activity of both leaders among the Nishad, Mallah, Bind, Kewat and Kashyap communities could increase in the coming days. Sanjay Nishad's statement today is being seen as an open indication of this growing political rivalry.
