stories.summary: The government will now provide treatment to more than 5 lakh registered lawyers in Uttar Pradesh. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath announced at an Allahabad High Court Bar Association event on Monday evening that lawyers will get cashless treatment of up to ₹5 lakh. He also made two other major announcements. The CM reached the event at 4 pm. Advocates welcomed him by chanting ‘Jai Shri Ram’. Association vice-president Amit Singh ‘Sonu’ first touched the CM’s feet and then prostrated himself before him. 6 key points from Yogi’s speech… See 3 pictures… 5.14 lakh registered lawyers in UP The CM symbolically handed over the key to the advocates’ chamber building to the association. The building, constructed at a cost of around ₹700 crore with 2,400 chambers, was inaugurated on May 31, 2025. However, the chambers have not yet been allotted. The allotment process will begin after the handover of the key. There are currently 5,14,439 active registered lawyers in Uttar Pradesh. This figure came to light recently during a hearing in the Allahabad High Court related to the backgrounds of lawyers. The figure was mentioned in reports submitted by the Uttar Pradesh Bar Council and the Director General of Police. Before this, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath had provided cashless treatment of up to ₹5 lakh to teachers, anganwadi workers and helpers, PRD personnel and cooks.

stories.title: Pilot says, ‘My ear hurts, I won’t fly’:Refuses to operate IndiGo flight in Varanasi; passengers protest
stories.summary: A pilot refused to fly a flight at Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport in Varanasi on Monday. The pilot declined to board the aircraft, saying that he had ear pain and was unwell. Meanwhile, all 178 passengers had boarded the aircraft. When they learnt that the pilot would not fly the aircraft, they became angry and started creating a disturbance. The airport authority tried to pacify the passengers and told them they would be sent on the next flight. The passengers calmed down after this. Flight was scheduled to depart at 11:55 am IndiGo Airlines flight 6E 6559 was scheduled to depart from Varanasi for Bengaluru at 11:55 a.m. After completing the security checks and boarding pass formalities, all the passengers had boarded the aircraft. Meanwhile, the pilot categorically refused to report for duty, saying he had suddenly developed severe pain in his ear. As soon as the passengers learnt of this, they began protesting against the airline administration. As the situation worsened, the CISF QRT team and senior officials deployed for airport security reached the spot. They pacified the passengers, escorted them off the aircraft, and seated them in the terminal building (deboarded). Flight finally took off at 5:45 p.m. During this time, the passengers also had a heated altercation with airline staff. As the situation escalated, the airline management began making alternative arrangements. A pilot was brought to Varanasi on another flight arriving from Delhi. The flight was subsequently sent to Bengaluru at 5:45 p.m. The passengers were inconvenienced for around six hours. Second incident in a week This is the second incident involving IndiGo Airlines at Babatpur Airport this month. Earlier, on Thursday, the pilot of an IndiGo flight to Mumbai had also refused to operate the flight, citing a sudden deterioration in his health. On that occasion too, the aircraft could depart for Mumbai after a delay of around four hours, once another pilot from Hyderabad took charge. What are the rules on rest for pilots and crew? stories.title: Jayant Chaudhary threatens to expose Akhilesh:SP leader hits back, ‘Leader of a one-and-a-half-district party is ungrateful’
stories.summary: Rashtriya Lok Dal chief and Union Minister of State Jayant Chaudhary delivered a sharp response to Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav on Monday. Speaking to the media in Delhi, he said, "The flippant way Akhilesh Yadav speaks is not right. Before the NDA, I had an alliance with Akhilesh Yadav. There are many things that are not disclosed. If I reveal all of them, Akhilesh Yadav will have nowhere to stand in Uttar Pradesh." SP leader Fakhrul Hasan Chand hit back at Jayant's statement. He said: "In western Uttar Pradesh, there is a party with a presence in one and a half districts, whose leaders are ungrateful. They enter the Rajya Sabha on the strength of SP MLAs and join the BJP alliance as soon as they reach the Rajya Sabha. They enjoy the perks of power. They used to say, 'Am I some chavanni [25-paise coin] who will switch sides?' It turns out they were a chavanni-they switched sides." In fact, Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav had sarcastically claimed last month that the Rashtriya Lok Dal would get 73 seats in the NDA. Without naming RLD chief Jayant Chaudhary, Akhilesh had said, "I turned a four-anna coin into a rupee, but even he ran away." Since then, leaders of both parties have been attacking each other. Now read Jayant's full account in 10 questions and answers... Your wife has responded to Akhilesh for the first time. Will she contest the election too? Jayant Chaudhary: Charu ji's speech outdid me too. She made a precise point. She said a great deal in a short time. That reflects her emotions. There was no beating about the bush; she put forward what was in her heart. You should ask her whether she wants to contest the election. If she does, she will have to apply to our parliamentary board. How many seats is the RLD planning to contest this time? Jayant Chaudhary: Uttar Pradesh has 403 seats. Along with Uttar Pradesh, we will also contest in Uttarakhand. But on all 403 seats in Uttar Pradesh, the NDA is fighting jointly. All constituent parties have the same aim: the path of development must not be obstructed. Election symbols and party names keep changing. During the time of Chaudhary Charan Singh and Chaudhary Ajit Singh, too, there were different symbols and names. Regardless of whose party name or symbol it is, we must fight our battle with strength. You are not speaking clearly about your seats, but Akhilesh Yadav is? Jayant Chaudhary: I am speaking about the NDA's seats with full authority. Tell me, is that statement more important, or is Akhilesh's statement? Akhilesh Yadav has already made your seats clear on social media? Jayant Chaudhary: When we were in an alliance with him, not everything was made public. This is my seriousness, which is why I am not revealing those things. If I reveal them, he will not find anywhere to stand in Uttar Pradesh. He is saying today, with such casualness, that they should get so many seats for there to be any respect. Chaudhary Charan Singh's respect will not be determined by the number of Assembly seats. He is respected in everyone's hearts and always will be-even if the Rashtriya Lok Dal does not win a single seat. Akhilesh is very aggressive. He first made the "chavanni" remark, and then his leaders made the "haveli" remark? Jayant Chaudhary: There should be issues in politics. The issue is not about a chavanni. The issues concern farmers, the education system, and development. Ask the people of Saharanpur how long it takes to reach Delhi on the highways being built today. They get there in two to two and a half hours. And how long did it take earlier? It took no less than 6 hours. These people want progress and employment, and that is what we are working towards. You spoke about Gen Z and said G stands for ganna. Is this, in a way, an attempt to bring Gen Alpha over to your side? Jayant Chaudhary: I believe that young people do not think in the same way that I do or that our ancestors did. Nor should they; their world is entirely different. There is no benefit in entangling them in caste divisions. That is why we need to rise above caste. There is not much time left before the Assembly elections. Has the Samajwadi Party begun its campaign from western Uttar Pradesh? Jayant Chaudhary: No, where did it begin? He is not SP; he is PC. He is doing nothing except PC. He will not hold a public meeting. He will tweet there. He has not led any movement, nor has he come out onto the streets, but he is engaging in opposition politics. Are Akhilesh's rallies in western Uttar Pradesh being postponed because of the 'chavanni' remark? Jayant Chaudhary: I do not know why they are being postponed. I know that the rallies are not taking place. What will your party's stand be on the UCC? Jayant Chaudhary: Look, this is for the states to do. The Home Minister has made a statement on the issue. From the perspective of women's rights, the common law is progressive. In fact, Home Minister Amit Shah said in Mumbai on 13 September that the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) would be implemented in all 21 BJP-NDA-ruled states before the 2029 Lok Sabha election. The UCC has already been implemented in several states. It will be implemented in the remaining states as well. Will there be a decision on the UCC in Uttar Pradesh before 2027? Jayant Chaudhary: No. That was the last question, and I have given the last answer. SP leader Fakh­rul Hasan Chand hits back at Jayant's statement SP leader Fakhrul Hasan Chand hit back at Jayant Chaudhary's statement. He said, "It is a party of one and a half districts in western Uttar Pradesh, whose leaders are ungrateful. Today, they are talking about development when potato farmers are in distress." Paper leaks continued, young people were beaten in the streets, farmers remained troubled, and stray animals kept grazing on farmers' crops, but Jayant Chaudhary remained silent. Why? Because he sees development only when farmers appear distressed. Therefore, the leader of a party confined to one and a half districts should remember that the people are supreme and the people give their answer. Whenever the Samajwadi Party holds a rally in western Uttar Pradesh, it will be held with full force and will be historic.

stories.title: Prayagraj man jumps from Naini Bridge, leaves suicide note:‘My wife liked this place, see, I can die’; gets rescued by police personnel
stories.summary: A young man in Prayagraj jumped off the Naini Bridge, the same bridge his wife liked. He mentioned this in a suicide note before taking the step. Seeing him fall into the river, water police personnel immediately rushed towards him in a motorboat. With the help of divers, the man was safely pulled out of the river. He was given initial treatment and is said to be in stable condition. Police questioning revealed that the man is a resident of Jaunpur district. See 3 pictures… He left his bag aside and climbed onto the bridge railing Alok Singh (32), a resident of Ahmadpur Gariyanv village in Mungra Badshahpur, Jaunpur district, reached the Naini Bridge over the Yamuna at around 9 am today with a bag. He placed the bag on one side, then climbed onto the bridge railing and jumped into the river. Water police personnel rescued him with the help of divers. ‘My wife thinks I cannot die’ When police checked the man's bag, they found his Aadhaar card along with a suicide note. It said that his wife should be informed by phone after his death. If she did not answer the call, she should be sent a message and a video should be made and sent to her. The note said his wife did not believe that he could die. After being informed about the incident, police from the Keedganj police station reached the spot. They traced the man's family and informed them about the incident. He was taken to hospital by ambulance, where he received initial treatment. Based on the suicide note, a dispute with his wife is being considered the likely reason behind his step at first glance. However, police are investigating the matter. The situation is expected to become clearer after questioning the man. Water police rescue three people in three days The rescue operation was carried out by the water police team under the supervision of in-charge Ravindra Nath and team leader Devanand Barnwal. Constables Sanjay Kumar and Anil Kumar Kotarya, who were on duty, immediately reached the river in a motorboat and played a key role in rescuing the man. Notably, the water police have rescued three people in the past three consecutive days.

stories.title: Rape FIR filed against cricketer Mohammed Shami's brother:Lucknow woman says he made false marriage promise, forced her to quit job
stories.summary: A rape FIR was registered late on Sunday night at Lucknow's Ashiyana police station against Mohammad Kaif, brother of cricketer Mohammed Shami. A divorced woman had accused him of having sex with her several times after promising to marry her. She had said: "Mohammad Kaif had sex with me several times after promising to marry me. After he assured me that we would marry, I even quit my job. Whenever I raised the subject of marriage, he would call me over and have sex with me again. I am now fighting for justice. He cannot silence my voice by using his influence and position." The woman told Dainik Bhaskar, “Before entering into a relationship, I had made it clear that I was divorced and had a son. Mohammad Kaif had said, 'I have no objection to your past or your son. I will marry only you.'” At his insistence, I quit my job. I worked as a member of the cabin crew for an airline company in Delhi. We would meet on flights while travelling. As we grew closer, I reminded him of his promise to marry me. After that, he would call me to whichever city he was in. He would have sex with me for several days. The woman submitted written complaints at Lucknow's Ashiana police station on 31 August and at Vibhuti Khand police station on 2 September. When no case was registered, she went to the DCP East's office on 5 September. She submitted a complaint there, seeking the registration of an FIR against Mohammad Kaif and legal action. Finally, a case was registered against Mohammad Kaif on 13 September on charges of rape and issuing threats. The woman said she had informed Mohammad Kaif that she was divorced. Despite this, he entered into a relationship with her. He has now left her. Charges filed under which sections, and what punishment is possible? A case has been registered against Mohammad Kaif under Sections 69 and 351 of the BNS. Section 69: This section applies in cases where someone has sexual relations by making a false promise of marriage or employment. If convicted, the accused may face up to 10 years in prison and a fine. Section 351: This section applies in cases involving threats to kill or cause harm. If convicted, the accused may face imprisonment ranging from 2 to 7 years or a fine. They first met in 2023 The woman told Dainik Bhaskar, "I was introduced to Mohammad Kaif on Instagram in 2020. At the time, he was not even playing domestic cricket. In August 2023, he expressed his wish to marry me. When I told him that I was divorced, he said he had no objection to my past." “We met for the first time in Ghaziabad on 11 September 2023. After that, we continued meeting. He called me to hotels several times while playing in Delhi. I stayed with him in Delhi for several days. A few months later, when I reminded him about marriage, he called me to Kolkata. There, he had sexual relations with me at a hotel.” Invited me to Lucknow's Hotel Hyatt, said he would marry me after the IPL auction The woman alleged that the cricketer had said he would marry her after the IPL auction. He had also sworn on the Quran to this effect. On 11 October 2024, Bengal's Ranji team came to Lucknow. Mohammed Kaif also came with the team. There, too, he invited me to Hotel Hyatt in Gomti Nagar and had sexual relations with me. Mohammed Kaif and his elder brother are threatening me today. If I am standing on the streets and raising my voice today, it is because I have been wronged. I want to tell the police to register my complaint. If the investigation finds me guilty, I should also be punished. Said-Quit job on promise of marriage The woman said that she was working as cabin crew for an airline company in Delhi at the time. She alleges that the cricketer asked her to quit her job and promised to marry her. The woman claims that she quit her job after trusting the cricketer's assurances. They still did not marry. She had hoped they would marry after the IPL auction in December 2025, but that did not happen. When she pressured the cricketer to marry her in January 2026, he began distancing himself from her. He also stopped speaking to her. Called to Kolkata after making allegations on a podcast The woman said that when she spoke to Mohammed Kaif's elder brother, Mohammed Haseeb, about marrying Kaif, he initially said he would speak to Kaif and let her know. Later, he began calling me a honey trapper. After being harassed continuously, I spoke about my ordeal on a sports channel on 29 April 2026. Ten days after the channel's podcast, on 9 May, Mohammed Kaif called me and asked me to get the podcast removed. He assured me that he would speak to his family and marry me. He called me to Kolkata again. There, after once again promising to marry me, he had sex with me several times. The woman has been visiting police stations and police officers in Lucknow in recent days, seeking justice. Called to Amroha and threatened with claims of influence at the highest levels Mohammad Kaif had sex with her on 18 May. The next day, 19 May, she was called to a man's house in Amroha to discuss marriage. Kaif's elder brother, his mother and others were present there. She was threatened during the conversation. His elder brother Haseeb said they had influence at the highest levels and that she could not harm them in any way. The woman said, "On 30 May, I told Kaif about the entire incident in Amroha. He did not help me and also refused to marry me." These incidents left her under considerable mental distress. Appealed to senior officials after visiting one police station after another The woman says she previously lived under the jurisdiction of Ashiyana police station. Therefore, she submitted a written complaint at Ashiyana police station. However, the police said the matter did not fall under their jurisdiction. She then submitted a written complaint at Vibhutikhand police station because the hotel where she had stayed with the cricketer falls under the jurisdiction of Vibhutikhand police station. After she received no response from either police station, the woman submitted a written complaint to the DCP East, Lucknow. Following her complaint, the investigation into the entire matter has been assigned to the ACP, Vibhutikhand. The woman has recorded her statement in the case.

stories.title: Life convict kills wife with trishul in Mahoba:Sat beside her body for 3 hours; serving sentence for granddaughter’s murder
stories.summary: Life convict who had come out on parole in Mahoba stabbed his wife to death with a trident. She fell to the ground covered in blood and died at the scene. Convict Kallan Raikwar suspected that his wife was feeding him poisoned food. After killing her, he sat beside the body for around three hours. He then told his family and the police himself that he had committed the murder. As soon as the information was received, police reached the scene and arrested Kallan. He was already serving a life sentence in Madhya Pradesh's Satna jail. He had killed his 10-month-old granddaughter. The incident took place late on Sunday night in the area under Kulpahar police station. See 2 pictures... Now read the full story in detail Kallan Raikwar, 50, lives in Ragaulia Buzurg village, around 38 km from the district headquarters. His elder son, Santosh, died by suicide four years ago after hanging himself. His younger son, Munna, 30, works as a labourer in Delhi, while his daughter, Vissa, 25, is married. Kallan is serving a life sentence at Satna jail. In 2014, he killed his 10-month-old granddaughter by smashing her against a stone in Naogaon, Madhya Pradesh. The court sentenced him to life imprisonment in 2017. Kallan would return to Ragaulia Buzurg every three months on parole. This time, Kallan came home on 1 September on 14 days' parole. He suspected his wife, Champa, 48, of mixing a poisonous or intoxicating substance into his food. This led to an argument between the couple. During the quarrel, Kallan repeatedly struck Champa on the head and neck with a trident kept inside the house. She died on the spot. Nephew said, ‘Uncle himself informed them about the murder’ Jayram said, "Uncle killed aunt at night. We found out in the morning when uncle himself told us about it. He did not flee after the crime. We called the police, who arrived and took uncle into custody. Uncle is serving a life sentence and had come out on parole." Additional Superintendent of Police Vandana Singh said, “After receiving information from the PRV, a police team reached the spot. The accused has been taken into custody. A case has been registered against him. Further action is under way.”

stories.title: AMU students protest over food:Proctor falls during pushing and shoving as girls shout, ‘We find insects in our food, we won’t tolerate it anymore’
stories.summary: More than 100 female students of Aligarh Muslim University (AMU) took to the streets on Monday morning and began raising slogans, alleging that they had been served poor-quality food in the hostel. The proctorial team arrived after learning about this. An argument first broke out between the team and the students, followed by a clash and pushing and shoving. During the incident, a deputy proctor fell to the ground. As the commotion escalated, the proctorial team called the police. The police formed a human chain to separate the students and the proctorial team. The students were then counselled. The commotion continued for four hours. The incident took place at the university's Abdullah Hall. The students alleged that the proctorial team assaulted and misbehaved with them. They said the matter should be investigated impartially and action should be taken against those responsible. The students shouted: We are continually being served poor-quality food. Worms are found in the food. We will not tolerate this any longer. Whenever a complaint was made, we were always assured that the matter would be resolved after a meeting. Four meetings have been held so far. Still, no solution has been found. This is why we had to take to the streets. See three pictures of the female students' protest... Students say they were warned of action over complaint Students living in Abdullah Hall said they went to the university administration at 7 a.m. on Monday with their complaint. They told the authorities that they were being served poor-quality food continuously. The administration did not listen to them and instead warned that action would be taken against them. They were told, "Leave this place, otherwise action will be taken against everyone." After this, they began raising slogans. Meanwhile, the proctorial team arrived. The dispute escalated during the discussions. The team manhandled them. The men behaved indecently with them. The university administration then called the police. Proctor says process of improving food quality is also under way Proctor Prof. Naved Khan said that three to four meetings had been held with the students over the past 10 days regarding the quality of the food. The process of improving the food is also under way, incorporating the suggestions received from the students. He said that students at Abdullah Hall are charged ₹1,400 every month for food. In an era of inflation, providing extremely high-quality food for this amount is challenging. The university does not receive sufficient separate funding for this purpose. The proctor said that one of the students' complaints was that dogs and cats roam around the hall premises. The district administration is being contacted regularly about this. Several drives have also been conducted to catch stray dogs, but the problem has not been resolved. Serious action is being taken on all the students' legitimate complaints. Examinations for Classes 1 to 5 cancelled amid the uproar Examinations for Classes one to five at Abdullah School and AMU Girls' School were also affected by the students' protest. Several girls were unable to reach the examination centre. As a result, the examinations were cancelled.

stories.title: Massive factory fire breaks out in Moradabad:Smoke plume visible from 2km away, nearby area evacuated
stories.summary: A massive fire broke out at a timber factory in Moradabad on Monday afternoon. Within moments, the entire factory was engulfed in flames. The fire leaped nearly 20 feet into the air, with a plume of smoke visible from almost 2 kilometres away. The smoke was so intense that people in the vicinity began to suffocate, prompting the police to evacuate the surrounding area. Chief Fire Officer (CFO) Dr Rajeev Kumar Pandey stated that owing to the severity of the blaze, fire engines had to be summoned from Rampur. Large quantities of thinner, paint, chemicals, and dry wood were stored in the factory, causing the fire to spread rapidly. A team of approximately 30 firefighters and 15 fire engines were deployed to tackle the inferno. The blaze was brought under control after nearly three hours of intense effort. Extinguishing the fire proved particularly difficult due to the vast amount of wooden goods stored inside. The fire broke out at around 11 o'clock at the RH International factory, located near Rampur Doraha in the Katghar police station area. The factory is owned by a man named Tasleem. The unit manufactures lamps, premium curtain rods, designer furniture, and metal handicrafts, which are also exported abroad. Photographs of the fire- Eyewitnesses' account: Suspected short circuit behind the fire According to eye-witnesses, smoke was suddenly seen billowing from the factory around 11 o'clock, after which the fire spread rapidly. A short circuit is suspected to be the cause of the blaze. All employees present in the factory are safe. However, the exact cause of the fire has not yet been confirmed, and teams from the police and fire brigade are currently investigating the matter.

stories.title: ‘Forget taking the trophy, won’t even accept gifts’:Cricketer Deepti Sharma's mother says Indian team refused Asia Cup trophy
stories.summary: Cricketer Deepti Sharma's mother, Sushila Sharma, said the family would not only refuse to accept the Asia Cup trophy from Asian Cricket Council (ACC) president and Pakistan Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi but also reject any gift from Pakistani representatives until Pakistan ends terrorism. India won the trophy after defeating Sri Lanka in the Asia Cup final at the Dubai International Stadium, with Agra's Deepti playing a key role by taking three wickets for 19 runs in four overs after scoring five runs before being run out; India posted 183/5 in 20 overs, while Sri Lanka were bowled out for 111 in 19.6 overs, with Sri Charani taking four wickets and Deepti three. Celebrations in Agra after Deepti's victory After Deepti won the Asia Cup, celebrations broke out at her home in Agra and in the neighbourhood. Her family and people from the colony watched the final together. As soon as India won, people congratulated one another and extended their best wishes to Deepti's family. After India's victory, the entire family, including her father Bhagwan Sharma, celebrated by feeding one another sweets. Family members spoke to Deepti over the phone and congratulated her on the victory. The family and people in the neighbourhood are proud of Deepti's achievement. Deepti's coach and brother, Sumit Sharma, said her performance throughout the Asia Cup had been outstanding. Along with taking three wickets in the final, she also performed well in the other matches. He said Deepti had brought glory not only to Agra but to the entire country. Most wickets in the tournament Deepti Sharma took the most wickets in the tournament, with 14 in total. She bowled in five matches at an economy rate of 3.84. Sri Charani ranked second with 12 wickets. Shafali-Mandhana give India a strong start India won the toss and elected to bat first. Openers Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana put on a 129-run partnership for the first wicket. Shafali scored 68, while Smriti made 59. Their innings helped India post a total of 183. Now read about Deepti Sharma... Deepti would insist on going to the stadium Deepti's elder brother, Sumit Sharma, used to play cricket and went to the stadium every day for net practice. Watching him, Deepti's interest in cricket also grew. Initially, she began training at home with her brother. After that, whenever her brother went to the stadium, Deepti began insisting on accompanying him. However, she was not given a chance to play there. So she would sit on the sidelines and watch net practice for hours. When the ball hit the stumps directly One day, Deepti arrived at Agra's Eklavya Sports Academy with her brother. She was sitting on the sidelines, watching the other players practise in the nets. Just then, after a shot was played, the ball rolled to a stop near Deepti. She picked it up and threw it towards the stumps, which were about 50 metres away. The ball hit the stumps directly and the bail flew off. Selector Hemlata Kala, who was standing at a distance, witnessed the entire scene. Kala realised that the girl had exceptional cricketing talent and should make it to the Indian team. She recommended Deepti's name. Hemlata Kala herself had been part of the Indian women's cricket team. Deepti was given the post of DSP in the Uttar Pradesh Police Two years ago, Deepti was appointed Deputy Superintendent of Police in the Uttar Pradesh Police. The Yogi government also awarded her ₹3 crore for her outstanding victory in the Asian Cup. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath presented Deepti with the honour at an event held in Lucknow. Deepti won a gold medal for India in the women's cricket event at the Asian Games held in China. She also won a silver medal with the Indian women's cricket team at the Commonwealth Games held in Birmingham in 2023.

stories.title: BJP MLA fumes over toll collection on damaged Jhansi highway:Threatens to shut toll booth after witnessing accident
stories.summary: Jhansi BJP MLA Jawahar Lal Rajput lashed out at an NHAI officer after seeing the damaged road on the highway. He called the project director and said: "Accidents have occurred because of the damaged road. We will have an FIR registered against all of you. We will also get your toll plaza shut down. When the road is in such poor condition, why are you collecting toll? Why should people pay, and what are they paying for? I will complain to the Chief Minister about this. We will not allow the public to be troubled." The MLA had reached the accident site on Sunday night after a woman was killed in a road accident. Another accident took place right in front of him. A father and his son were injured after falling from a motorcycle. The incident angered the MLA. The matter concerns National Highway 27 between Jhansi and Kanpur. See two pictures Now read the full account in the MLA's own words MLA Jawahar Lal Rajput said, "There are potholes at several places on the Jhansi-Kanpur highway. The road is damaged. I raised this issue at the core committee meeting three days ago. I have already filed a written complaint as well. It was because of the highway's poor condition that Ramdevi died in a road accident near the Moth bypass on Sunday afternoon." The MLA said, "We reached the accident site at night. Deepak, a resident of Erich, and his father were injured after falling from a motorcycle right in front of me. After this, I called NHAI Project Director P D Singh. I said, 'Two accidents have taken place near the Moth bypass today.'" He said, "No vehicle hit anyone in either accident. Both accidents occurred because of the damaged road. This is negligence in one way or another. We believe that action will definitely be taken in this matter. Officials have been asked to repair the highway so that people in the area do not face difficulties and road accidents can be prevented." MLA tells official: This will not do A 2.04-minute video has emerged showing a conversation between the MLA and the project director of the NHAI (National Highway Authority of India) at the scene. In it, the MLA says, "Does this fall within your area or not? Tell me the name of the person whose area this concerns. We will have an FIR registered." "This will not do. If the road is in such poor condition, why are you collecting money? Tell me, you cut up the road and left, and accidents are now taking place here. We will speak to the DM and SSP and everyone else. This will not do – the road is in such poor condition, yet people are expected to pay you toll." MLA had reached the Assembly in a bullock cart Jawahar Lal Rajput is the MLA from the Garautha Assembly constituency in Jhansi and has been elected for a second consecutive term. His father was a farmer. Jawahar Lal Rajput practised law. He is known as a farmers' leader. During his legal practice, he continued to raise farmers' issues. He was elected MLA for the first time in 2017 after defeating veteran Samajwadi Party leader Deepnarayan Singh Yadav. He reached the Assembly in a bullock cart for the first time. After being elected MLA for the second time in 2022, he took his oath in Bundeli.

stories.title: Murder accused claims police told him to kill:Murders village head's son in Raebareli, says victim forced meeting with his wife
stories.summary: A man and his wife allegedly killed the village head's son in Raebareli's Khairhani village on Saturday after the accused claimed the man had been harassing his wife, with a video of the incident emerging late on Sunday evening. In the video, the accused is heard saying, "Call the lawyer; I have killed him. I had filed a complaint at the police station three times. The police had said, 'Kill him'; I have killed him.' According to the accused, the village head's son arrived by car on Saturday to meet his wife despite being warned several times, refused to return home when told to do so, and was killed by the couple after an argument, in an incident that took place 27 kilometres from the district headquarters. Read the complete sequence of events... She divorced her first husband because of an affair Surendra is a salesman. He lives in Khairhani village with his wife, Soni, and their children. Soni's first marriage was to Amit of Chhataiya village in 2010. They have a son and a daughter. During this period, Soni met Ramakant (35), the son of village head Ganesh Prasad. The two began having an affair. As a result, Amit and Soni divorced seven years later. Their son began living with Amit, while their daughter went with Soni to her parental home in Bachhrawan. Soni married Surendra in 2017. They have a son. Soni says that even after her marriage, Ramakant continued to pursue her. He would often arrive at her in-laws' home to meet her. He did not stop despite being told several times. Soni had also filed a complaint against him at the Bachhrawan police station. Arrived at the house on Saturday, killed after an argument Soni said that Ramakant reached Khairhani in a Swift Dzire car at 1:30 p.m. on Saturday. Surendra parked his car 200 metres before the house. My husband, his brother Virendra and I reached the spot. Surendra told Ramakant not to come to the house, but he did not listen. The two began fighting. Virendra was also injured in the incident. Surendra became angry after his brother was injured. Ramakant was then seriously injured and died some time later. Father of deceased weeps uncontrollably; three sent to jail Ramakant's father, who reached the spot after receiving the information, broke down upon seeing his son's body. Station House Officer Shyam Kumar Pal said that police reached the spot and took the accused into custody. On Sunday, Surendra, his brother Virendra and Soni were sent to jail.

stories.title: BJP Mahanagar list being repeatedly edited:Names kept expanding in executive committee list while several dropped
stories.summary: The list of the Gorakhpur BJP metropolitan unit's executive committee, released after noon on September 7, 2026, has undergone several amendments, with more than a dozen new names added and one name removed, although it was made public only once. The name of a senior leader was hurriedly included in two lists before being removed from the first list after it was edited, causing considerable turmoil within the BJP metropolitan unit; while no one is prepared to speak openly about the issue, questions are being raised internally. The changes being made to the list do not concern key posts. They are limited to the names of executive committee members and special invitees to the executive committee. If the original list that was released is considered correct, the metropolitan team should have 91 members, including the president. However, according to the changes made by 12 September, the number has risen to around 104. There is speculation that further amendments may be made in the future. First, find out when each list was released The metropolitan president first announced the office-bearers of the main body. These included vice-presidents, ministers and the treasurer. However, no changes were made to this list. Then, at around 4 p.m. on 7 September, the metropolitan president posted a four-page list on his Facebook page. It included the names of the district assistant treasurer, media coordinator, two assistant coordinators, the social media coordinator, three assistant coordinators to assist them, the district IT coordinator, two assistant coordinators to assist them, two district assistant office ministers and 57 executive committee members. Following this, a list of 17 special invitee members of the metropolitan executive committee was released on 11 September. It included Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and other senior leaders. However, questions soon began to be raised about it. On Sunday morning, senior BJP leader Chiranjiv Chaurasia posted a list on his Facebook page, writing that it had been sent to him by the metropolitan president. The list he posted contained 18 names instead of 17, with his own name listed as the 18th. After that, some more people posted a list on Facebook, in which their names had been added as executive committee members. Business leader Madan Lal Gupta (Agrahari) shared a screenshot of a list from his Facebook account. The number of executive committee members in it had increased by 13 from the list dated 7 September. The name of one member had also disappeared. Now, find out what changes were made First, let us look at the list of special invitee members, as this was the subject of public questions. A BJP worker posted on Facebook after not finding Chiranjeev Chaurasia's name on the list. Chiranjeev Chaurasia's name was subsequently added to the list of executive committee members, and some people also received that list. However, it was later revised, and he was placed at the bottom of the list of special invitee members. As for the working committee members, the names of Vinod Dubey, Umesh Srivastava, Bhola Agrahari, Madan Agrahari, Ganesh Verma, Durgesh Bajaj, Rohit Sawant, Ankit Gupta, Somu Nigam, Jitendra Gaud, Pashupatinath Nigam, Awadhesh Agrahari and Vishal Nishad were added. In the list issued by the metropolitan president on 7 September, Anil Singh was the last name. The name was written in bold letters. Raju Pratap Singh's name appeared immediately above it. However, in the list posted by Madan Agrahari, Anil Singh's name was missing altogether, while Vinod Dubey's name appeared below Raju Pratap Singh's. Other members were also added to that list. Metropolitan president says no changes have been made Asked about the many changes, Metropolitan President Ramesh Pratap Gupta said that no changes had been made to the list. The first list remains unchanged. People may be posting that same list from their social media accounts. Repeated changes seen in BJP for the first time This is the first time that repeated changes have been seen in a party such as the BJP. The list containing the added names was not issued by the metropolitan president on any public platform. Instead, some of the newly inducted members did so themselves. The list was sent to everyone individually. Senior BJP leader and Backward Classes Commission member Chiranjiv Chaurasia posted on Sunday morning that the metropolitan president had sent him the list on Sunday itself. Among the newly inducted members, Madan Agrahari posted the list bearing his name from his Facebook account. There are more objections There are further objections to the list of specially invited members. These objections are not being voiced on a public platform, but there is considerable discussion about them within the party. The name of Dr Radh Mohan Das Agrawal, a four-time city MLA who is currently a Rajya Sabha member and serves as the BJP's national general secretary, is missing from the list. In contrast, the list includes a name that has never held any important position in the BJP. What experts say Senior journalist Alok Dubey says, "There is considerable pressure within the BJP to accommodate its leaders. Every leader wants to fit into the organisation's structure. The revision of the Gorakhpur metropolitan unit's list is an example of this. Several senior leaders, including RMD, have been sidelined from the metropolitan team. Some of the names included have also drawn objections. Questions are being raised about this within the party. In such a situation, it would come as no surprise if a revised list is issued again."

stories.title: Kashi Vishwanath Temple CEO transferred:Assigned responsibility as Deputy Secretary in UPSSSC, had created SOP for crowd control at temple
stories.summary: Vishwabhushan Mishra, chief executive officer (CEO) of the Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple Trust, has been transferred after nearly two years and given charge as deputy secretary at the Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission (UPSSSC). The temple trust has not yet announced his replacement as CEO. Vishwabhushan Mishra had been serving as the CEO of the Kashi Vishwanath Temple Trust since January 2024. During his tenure, several changes were made to facilities for devotees, crowd management, security and darshan arrangements. SOP implemented during Sawan and Mahashivratri During Vishwabhushan Mishra's tenure, changes were made to the darshan arrangements to manage crowds during festivals. In view of the heavy crowds during festivals such as Sawan, New Year and Mahashivratri, the temple administration implemented SOPs for crowd control and darshan at different levels. When the crowd increased significantly, touch darshan in the sanctum sanctorum was temporarily stopped, and jhanki darshan was arranged. The aim was to enable more devotees to have darshan of Baba Vishwanath in less time. Handled Responsibilities During Kumbh-2019 and the Covid Period Too Before becoming the CEO of the Kashi Vishwanath Temple, Vishva Bhushan Mishra was posted as Additional Commissioner (Administration) in the Varanasi Division. Before that, he had handled administrative responsibilities in several districts of the state. He also discharged administrative responsibilities during Prayagraj Kumbh-2019 and the Covid period.

stories.title: 14 IAS and 34 PCS officers transferred in UP:Neha Sharma removed from Medical Education Department
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government transferred 14 IAS and 34 PCS officers at midnight on Sunday. The chief development officers (CDOs) of Saharanpur, Lakhimpur Kheri and Ambedkar Nagar were replaced. Dr Vishram, the Additional Commissioner of the Vindhyachal division who sings Birha folk songs, has been given the responsibility of Member (Judicial) in the Board of Revenue. Vishram is a 2010-batch PCS officer. In January this year, the Uttar Pradesh government promoted him to the IAS. stories.title: Nurse alleges she was kidnapped in a car and raped:Says she was hospitalised for days, police gave ₹1.50 lakh and told her to leave
stories.summary: “I came to Ghaziabad from Mumbai during the lockdown for a job. Here, a young man abducted me in a car and forcibly raped me. He made two videos of me. I was beaten and threatened. I sat at the Madhuban Bapudham police station all night. A medical examination was conducted on me.” "When my condition worsened in Ghaziabad, I was admitted to a government hospital, and subsequently remained admitted to GTB Delhi for several days. My FIR was not registered; instead, the police handed me ₹1.50 lakh and said, 'Go.' I want justice. What happened to me is beyond words." A 35-year-old nurse recounted this ordeal in a conversation with Dainik Bhaskar. The victim currently works at a hospital in Delhi and is residing in the Rajnagar Extension area of Ghaziabad. Youth called his friends and said: "Come over, I've got a girl with me" The victim nurse recounted, "This incident occurred on 25 August 2026. I was living alone in Rajnagar Extension. A youth hailing from near Morta knew me. One day, he suddenly pulled up beside me in his car and forced me inside. He then drove me to an under-construction building near Morta. “Once there, the youth forcibly raped me and assaulted me inside the car. He threatened, 'If you go to the police, you will be killed.' He then telephoned his friends in front of me and said, 'Brother, come over, I've got a girl with me.' Intimidating me, he added, 'Right now it's just me; if my friends arrive as well, things will end very badly for you.'” Recorded nude videos and sent them to a WhatsApp group The victim nurse said, “The accused drank beer and recorded nude videos of me. Threatening me, he said, 'You won't be able to do anything to me.' He had also snatched my phone and sent my nude video to some WhatsApp group.” “I was terrified and didn't even have my phone. For a long time, I remained cowering in fear, wondering who to seek help from. Later, he threw my phone away. I somehow managed to retrieve my phone out of his sight. He threatened and beat me again for a while. I began to feel dizzy, and as my condition deteriorated, he put me in the car and shoved me out outside a housing society.” "At 12:59 am, I called 112 to seek police help. The police arrived at the scene and took me with them. I also submitted a written complaint. The police took me to the crime scene, where I pointed out my clothes, but they were not recovered by the police." 12 to 13 police officers arrived and questioned me The victim nurse said, “Around 12 to 13 police officers arrived, including some female officers. They all questioned me and recorded a video of me. Among them were a sub-inspector and an inspector. The police took me to the Madhuban Bapudham police station.” "I stayed at the police station from 3:00 am to 6:00 am. At 6:00 am, my medical examination was conducted at the district hospital. I said that I wanted justice and asked them to register my report. I told the medical officer that I am a nurse myself, and the police were not helping me." Sub-Inspector handed over ₹1.50 lakh “A Sub-Inspector or Inspector named Ravindra Kumar from the police station was there. As soon as I left the hospital, he handed me ₹1.50 lakh in cash and told me to leave. The other police officers were wearing uniforms, but they did not have name plates on.” “My FIR was not registered. I emailed police officials in Ghaziabad detailing the entire incident. I have also sent my complaint to the Human Rights Commission. Even though I am associated with the health department myself, injustice is still being done to me. I only want justice; I have no need for money.” The nurse stated, "My condition is poor; I will have to be admitted again. I thought the police would register an FIR, but no case was filed here at all. Once my health improves, I will complain to senior officials again."

stories.title: Akhilesh Yadav unveils new strategy — 75 districts, 75 manifestos:SP will do this for the first time, after using one manifesto since Mulayam’s era
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav has formulated a new strategy for the 2027 UP Assembly elections. Breaking away from its long-standing tradition, the SP is set to ditch the practice of releasing 'a single manifesto for the entire state' for the first time. Instead, it will now release a distinct, exclusive 'micro-level' manifesto for every district — meaning 75 districts and 75 different visions. Since the days of Mulayam Singh Yadav, the SP had been releasing only a single election manifesto. Rather than discussing 'what we will do for the state', the party will now directly engage voters on 'what new initiatives we will bring to your district'. The party leadership has also issued a decree to district-level leaders to draw up a comprehensive report highlighting their region's top five major problems, stalled projects, and local employment schemes. The SP's strategic meeting was held two months ago, attended by Akhilesh Yadav and presidents from all districts. It was suggested during the meeting that local issues from every district should be included in the election manifesto. Its advantages were also highlighted. Office-bearers argued in favour of the proposal, stating that a single manifesto only accommodates the state's major issues, whereas regions like Purvanchal, West UP, Awadh, and Bundelkhand all have distinct concerns of their own. People will feel a genuine connection with the party only when their local issues find a place in the party's manifesto. Issues such as roads, water supply, electricity, healthcare services, education, and employment directly resonate with the public. Party chief Akhilesh Yadav gave his immediate approval. State president Shyamlal Pal asked all district presidents and office-bearers to gather information across five key areas in their respective districts: 1. Employment and industry 2. Education and healthcare services 3. Tourism and road transport 4. Construction of bridges 5. Issues faced by farmers and weavers Commenting on the matter, senior journalist Siddharth Kalhans noted that this practice is common in Western nations. He added that there is also a Gen Z and Gen Alpha effect at play here. In recent times, Gen Alpha has staged protests over local issues in various districts—problems that are often straightforward to resolve. In Western countries, political parties prepare manifestos at the local level, and Akhilesh Yadav is now introducing that concept to UP. It is a positive step, as no party has ever released a district-level manifesto before. In these changing times, it will certainly prove relevant. 5 Key Highlights of the District-Wise Manifesto 1. Rapid Resolution of Local Issues The primary basis of the district-level manifesto will be the foundational needs of that specific area. In districts where roads, irrigation, waterlogging, drinking water, or electricity are major concerns, schemes related to these will receive top priority. Special focus will be given to investment in industrial districts, infrastructure in tourist destinations, and visitor amenities in religious hubs. 2. Linking Major Projects Directly to Employment The SP’s promises will not be limited to merely building basic infrastructure such as roads, bridges, or buildings; instead, these projects will be directly tied to local employment creation. During the ‘Vision India’ event in Agra, Akhilesh Yadav presented a vision to develop Agra as an IT City, Firozabad as a Glass City, and Mathura as a Heritage City. Additionally, he signaled plans to boost local industry through projects like the Yamuna Riverfront development in the Agra-Mathura belt and the rejuvenation of the lake at Fatehpur Sikri. 3. Dedicated Focus on Youth, Education, and Government Jobs Gen Z and young people are positioned at the centre of this agenda. Key measures include robust mechanisms to prevent exam paper leaks, a transparent policy for outsourced workers, and new opportunities for government employment. Furthermore, pledges will cover the reopening of closed schools, alongside establishing new colleges, universities, IT hubs, skill development centres, and employment exchanges. 4. Addressing Farmers' Regional Issues A major part of the manifesto will revolve around the rural economy. Customised policies will be crafted to address the specific needs of farmers in each region. Region-wise policies could be as follows... 5. Reviving Local Artisans and Traditional Industries Schemes will be introduced to promote the traditional business of every district. For instance, the challenges faced by weavers in eastern UP, the perfume industry in Kannauj, the brass and utensil industry in Moradabad, and the wooden furniture trade in Saharanpur will form a key component of SP's district manifestos. Candidates' Agenda Will Be Clear Through the Manifesto SP Spokesperson: "We Will Seek Votes Based on Our Work" SP national spokesperson Juhi Singh states, "Our manifesto will be entirely micro-level. Today, several districts in the state lack hospitals, numerous schools have closed down, and Asha Jyoti Centres lie abandoned. These will be revived once an SP government is formed. Our sole objective is to understand grass-roots issues and provide permanent solutions. The public still remembers the development work carried out by Akhilesh Yadav between 2012 and 2017. The party continues to assist people at its own level as well. A government of the people is going to be formed in the state in 2027."

stories.title: Is there a conspiracy against Mayawati in BSP?:Anger over Akash asking about her health; distrust began 18 months ago
stories.summary: BSP supremo Mayawati appears to believe that people expelled from the party are conspiring against her. At a press conference on Sunday, 13 September, she said some people were spreading rumours that she was unwell, but insisted that she was completely fine. Mayawati blamed her nephew Akash Anand’s father-in-law, Ashok Siddharth, for the alleged conspiracy. She said Akash was acting on Siddharth’s instructions and suggested that his alleged conspiracy was still continuing. There was a time when Ashok Siddharth was considered one of Mayawati’s most trusted aides. He was widely regarded as the No. 2 leader in the BSP. So why did he suddenly fall out of favour with Mayawati? The story of their conflict began around 18 months ago. Ashok came under scrutiny after his son’s wedding Relations between Mayawati and Ashok Siddharth are believed to have started deteriorating after a lavish wedding ceremony for Siddharth’s son in Agra on 7 February, 2025. Siddharth reportedly used the wedding to display his political influence. Senior BSP leaders from several states where he had served as the party in-charge were invited to the ceremony. Akash Anand also attended the wedding, but Mayawati and Akash’s father, Anand Kumar, stayed away. Four days later, on 11th February, Mayawati called a meeting in Lucknow. The wedding was reportedly viewed within the party as an attempt by Ashok Siddharth and Akash Anand to display their political strength. Mayawati made it clear that she would not tolerate another power centre within the party. She warned leaders who had attended the wedding and, for the first time, expelled Ashok Siddharth from the BSP. First made MLC, then sent to Rajya Sabha Ashok Siddharth is originally from the Kayamganj area of Farrukhabad. Before entering politics, he worked as a refractionist in Kannauj, checking people’s eyesight and prescribing spectacles. He became associated with Kanshi Ram and Mayawati’s ideology through BAMCEF, an organisation of educated employees from SC, ST, OBC and minority communities. On Mayawati’s advice, Siddharth resigned from his government job in 2007 and joined the BSP. In 2009, Mayawati made him an MLC and sent him to the Rajya Sabha in 2016. His wife was also appointed vice-chairperson of the State Women’s Commission. In 2010, Siddharth was given the responsibility of expanding the BSP’s organisation in South India. He was made in-charge of states including Tamil Nadu and Karnataka. Lost election after election, but Mayawati continued to trust him The BSP lost power in Uttar Pradesh in 2012, winning only 89 seats. The party then aimed to improve its performance in the 2014 Lok Sabha elections, but failed to win a single seat. Siddharth was removed from his responsibility in South India and was instead given charge of the Lucknow-Kanpur region. The BSP suffered another major setback in the 2017 Assembly elections, winning only 19 seats. In the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, the party won 10 seats after forming an alliance with the Samajwadi Party. Mayawati later ended the alliance. The BSP contested the 2022 Assembly elections alone and was reduced to just one seat. Despite these setbacks, Mayawati continued to repose faith in Siddharth. Mayawati later arranged the marriage of her nephew Akash Anand with Pragya, Ashok Siddharth’s daughter, who was pursuing an MBBS at Hindu College in Lucknow. The couple got married in a Buddhist ceremony in Gurugram on 26 March, 2023. Mayawati herself attended the wedding. Maharashtra and Delhi election setbacks increased distrust Maharashtra Assembly elections, November 2024: Ashok Siddharth was made the BSP’s in-charge for Maharashtra. He faced allegations of distributing tickets at his own discretion. When the matter reached Mayawati, she immediately removed him from the post. The BSP contested 237 seats in Maharashtra and lost all of them. Its vote share fell to just 0.48%. Delhi Assembly elections, February 2025: Akash Anand was given overall responsibility for the Delhi elections, while Nitin Singh, considered close to Ashok Siddharth, was made the in-charge. There were allegations that tickets for some candidates had been finalised without Mayawati’s approval. Several candidates reportedly complained to Mayawati about Ashok Siddharth, Nitin Singh and Akash Anand. After the elections, the BSP lost its deposit on all 70 seats. Its vote share fell to just 0.58%. Akash also gradually fell out of Mayawati’s favour Around 7 months after being expelled from the party, Ashok Siddharth publicly apologised to Mayawati. In September 2025, she allowed him to return to the BSP and gave him organisational responsibilities. However, around a year later, on 3rd August, he was expelled from the party again. Mayawati accused him of being involved in anti-party activities. After Siddharth’s expulsion, Akash Anand also came under Mayawati’s criticism. In several of her posts, Mayawati referred to Akash not as her nephew but as Ashok Siddharth’s son-in-law. On 3rd September, she described Akash as immature and removed him from all his responsibilities. On 9th September, Mayawati said Akash could return only if Ashok Siddharth retired from politics. The following morning, Siddharth announced his retirement from politics. However, Mayawati then appeared to backtrack, saying Siddharth had delayed his decision to retire. Will the father-in-law and son-in-law return to the BSP? Senior journalist Syed Qasim said the possibility of Akash Anand and Ashok Siddharth joining another party was extremely low. According to him, the doors of the BSP have not been permanently closed to either leader. Siddharth has already been expelled from the party twice and brought back on both occasions. Qasim said Mayawati’s stance now appeared to be less harsh than before. He pointed out that she had referred to Siddharth as “Shri Ashok Siddharth” instead of using the “father-in-law and son-in-law” description, suggesting some softening of her position. According to him, factionalism within the BSP appears to be playing a bigger role than any individual decision or mistake. He said the rival faction had allegedly used Ashok Siddharth to politically corner Akash Anand. Whom will Mayawati choose as her successor? Senior journalist Ratnamani Lal said Mayawati’s sense of distrust had grown after the 1995 State Guest House incident. He said she does not easily trust people and that this distrust now appears to have extended beyond party leaders to her own family. For several decades, Mayawati has been looking for a trusted leader who can take charge of the organisation after her. However, whenever a leader appeared to be gaining too much influence within the party, they were sidelined. Mayawati also tried to promote Akash Anand, but later removed his responsibilities while describing him as immature. The question of who will eventually succeed Mayawati therefore remains open.

stories.title: Woman kills husband with boyfriend's help in Bareilly:Dumps body in gorge 4 km away; he had caught them in objectionable position
stories.summary: In Bareilly, a 38-year-old man was killed by his wife with the help of her boyfriend. The boyfriend used to visit the man's house when he was away. One day, the man saw him with his wife, after which the boyfriend fled. The husband had severely beaten his wife ever since. It was then that the wife decided to get rid of him. She got the opportunity on 10 September. She strangled her husband with a rope and killed him with the help of her boyfriend. The boyfriend then put the body in a sack, carried it 4 kilometres away on a motorcycle and dumped it in a ditch. The man's family learnt about their daughter-in-law's affair. They then filed a complaint with the police against her and her boyfriend. The truth came to light only after the police questioned the woman strictly on 17 September. The police arrested the woman and her boyfriend and recovered Pappu's body on Friday. The incident took place in the Bhuta police station area. Here is the full story in detail... They got married 4 years ago His brother Bundan said, "Pappu worked as a tailor. About four years ago, his family lived in Balia village in Budaun district. During that period, Raja alias Riyaz (35), a resident of Faiznagar, used to visit our home. Around the same time, he became friends with my sister-in-law, Nargis. The two began having an affair. After that, Raja often started visiting the house on one pretext or another." His closeness to his girlfriend increased further after leaving the village Meanwhile, around three years ago, Pappu sold his land in Budaun and had a house built in Faiznagar village in the Bhuta area. He then began living there with his wife, three sons and three daughters. After moving to Bhuta, Raja's meetings with his sister-in-law increased further. One day, the family saw Raja talking to his sister-in-law, Nargis. They told his brother Pappu about it. Pappu had gone out for work. When he returned, he too saw his wife with her boyfriend. A heated argument then broke out between Pappu and his wife. Pappu also beat her. Wife grabbed his feet, boyfriend strangled him with a rope According to the police, Pappu returned home from work on the night of 10 September. At the time, Nargis's boyfriend, Raja, was hiding inside the house. Nargis grabbed Pappu's feet, while Raja tightened a rope around his neck. He died on the spot. Raja then put the body in a sack, took it near the Mirzapur kiln and threw it into a ditch. Inspector Ravindra Kumar said that during police questioning, the accused, Raja, confessed to murdering Pappu over an affair. Pappu's body was recovered based on information provided by Raja. The wife and her boyfriend have been arrested in connection with the murder.

stories.title: Lucknow man dies by suicide on video call with girlfriend:He drank poison mixed in a soft drink, then shot himself in the temple
stories.summary: A young man in Lucknow died by suicide while speaking to his girlfriend on a video call. He rode his motorbike towards a forest, where he mixed poison into a soft drink and consumed it before shooting himself in the temple with a pistol. Blood was found at the scene, and the young man's motorbike was also found parked there. The incident took place in the Bijnor area on Friday afternoon. The deceased was identified as 25-year-old Karan Yadav, a resident of Raisingh Kheda. There was a gunshot wound to his temple, and foam was coming from his mouth. Police took him to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. See three pictures- He was a private car driver and left home at 9 a.m. Karan drove a private car for a person in Vrindavan Colony. At around 9 a.m., he left home on his motorcycle, saying he was going to work. At around 1 p.m., Karan was found unconscious in a forest near Jalim Kheda village. His motorcycle was parked by the roadside, while he was 100 metres inside the forest from the road. Foam was coming from his mouth, and blood was flowing from a gunshot wound to his left temple. A pistol was also found lying nearby. Police recovered an empty cold drink bottle, an empty water bottle, a disposable glass and two small open vials of medicine from the scene. Passersby saw body while travelling along edge of forest Passersby travelling towards the forest saw Karan lying unconscious and informed the police. The police reached the spot and immediately took Karan to Lokbandhu Hospital. However, doctors declared him dead as soon as he reached the hospital. Karan's family comprises his mother, Keshana, and his two elder brothers, Ranjeet and Sonu. According to the police, the pistol found at the scene was illegal. The investigation has revealed that the deceased was in a relationship with a young woman. Karan was speaking to the woman on a video call when the incident took place. He then consumed poison and shot himself in the temple with the pistol, committing suicide.

stories.title: Woman found with throat slit in Lucknow:Vegetable knife found 5 feet from body, another under pillow
stories.summary: A 70-year-old woman was murdered by having her throat slit inside her home in Banthra, Lucknow. She lived alone. A woman who arrived to deliver milk in the morning saw the body covered in blood. Both gates of the house were locked from the inside, while the door leading to the roof was found open. Police suspect that the killer may have escaped via the roof. Two knives were also found at the scene. A vegetable-cutting knife was found lying on the ground around 5 feet from the body. The second knife was found under the pillow on the deceased woman's cot. The forensic team collected evidence from the scene. DCP South Mohammad Mustaq said: All the household items were found in order. It appears that the house was entered through the roof and the crime was committed. A case has been registered against an unidentified person under the murder section. Four police teams have been formed to solve the case. It will be solved soon. See 3 pictures of the crime scene... About the woman Chhedana lived alone in Khurrampur village. Her husband, Shankarlal, died six years ago. She had two daughters, Ram Janki and Archana. Both are married. Ram Janki lives with her in-laws in Balaganj, while Archana lives with her in-laws in Thakurganj. Chhedana had two brothers-in-law. One, Amrit Lal, is retired from the RTO department, where he served as an enforcement constable, and lives with his family in Ashiyana. Her other brother-in-law, Nandkishore Gautam, is a deputy jailer in Jaunpur. His family lives near Sarosa-Bharosa in the Para police station area. Knife wounds inflicted along both cheeks and on the leg The deceased woman's throat had been slit. There were knife marks along the edges of both her cheeks. She had also been stabbed in the right leg below the knee, and there was a knife mark on her right palm. Her clothes were dishevelled as well. This suggests that she may have put up a strong struggle during the incident. Her elder daughter, Ram Janaki, said her mother used to wear a gold chain around her neck, earrings in her ears and anklets on her feet, but none of these were found on her body today. In the case, her brother-in-law Amritlal filed a complaint at Banthra police station, following which a case was registered against an unidentified person. Woman who arrived to deliver milk in the morning saw the body The incident took place in Khurrampur village under Banthra police station limits. At around 9:30 p.m. on Thursday, villagers saw Chedana outside her house. She then went inside. At around 7:30 a.m. on Friday, Asha, a woman from the village, went to deliver milk to her. The door did not open for a long time. Asha called out several times, but received no response. She then peered inside through the gate and saw Chedana's body lying in the veranda, covered in blood. As soon as they learned of this, people from the surrounding area reached the spot. Both main gates found locked from inside The deceased's house has two main gates. One of them always remains closed. The other gate was used to enter and leave the house. This gate, too, was found locked from inside. Meanwhile, the door leading to the staircase to the roof was open. For this reason, the police are also investigating the possibility that the killer escaped via the roof. Daughter says-Mother's jewellery missing The deceased woman's elder daughter, Ram Janki, said her mother wore a gold chain around her neck, earrings and anklets. When she reached home after learning about the incident, she did not see the jewellery on her mother's body. Her cheeks, neck, chest and other parts of her body had been slashed with a knife. Senior police officers also reached the scene after receiving the information. Police examined the crime scene. It is not yet known who killed her or why. Police are investigating the case. They looked over the back wall and found her dead on the cot Amritlal Gautam, the brother-in-law of the deceased, Chhedana, said, "I met my sister-in-law only yesterday evening before leaving. All the women were sitting at the door. This morning, when the door had remained unopened for a long time, people looked over the back wall. She was lying dead on the cot. Her neck and leg had been cut with a knife." Investigation into the murder is under way Deputy Commissioner of Police (South) Mohammad Mustaq said the circumstances surrounding the elderly woman's murder were being investigated. All the belongings in the house were found in order. At first glance, it is suspected that someone entered the house via the roof and committed the crime. The case will be solved soon.

stories.title: Youth protest UGC with 100 tractors:Police reach Agra with 4 hydras, 7 bulldozers; highway sit-in continues after scuffle
stories.summary: Around 1,200 young people took to the streets in Agra on Friday in protest against the UGC. Riding around 100 tractors, they set out from Sanwai village in Etmadpur for the district collectorate. However, around 200 metres from the village, police and the PAC stopped them by putting up barricades. The police arrived at the scene with four Hydra cranes and seven bulldozers. Two companies of the PAC and around 300 police personnel were deployed for security. The young protesters insisted on being allowed to go to the district collectorate. An argument broke out between the protesters and the police, following which pushing and shoving began. The police drove the protesters back towards the village. Both sides remained locked in a standoff until the afternoon. Around 3 p.m., the protesters removed the barricades and ran towards the Agra-Firozabad Highway. The police also chased them. The protesters then staged a sit-in on the highway and began reciting the Hanuman Chalisa. The protest led to long queues of vehicles on the highway. To bring the situation under control, the PAC has detained around 10 young protesters. Three pictures of the protest...

stories.title: Basic Education Minister Sandeep Singh’s wedding fixed:Tilak in Aligarh, wedding in Delhi; brother Saurabh to marry alongside
stories.summary: Sandeep Singh, a minister in the Uttar Pradesh government and the grandson of former Chief Minister Kalyan Singh, is set to get married. Sandeep and his younger brother Saurabh will have their tilak ceremony in Aligarh on 14 November. The two brothers will get married together in Delhi in the final week of November. Details of their future brides have not yet emerged. According to sources, Minister Sandeep's future bride belongs to a business family in Aligarh. The date and hotel for the wedding have not yet been disclosed. According to sources, the wedding may take place on one of 26, 27 or 28 November. There is also talk of a reception after the wedding. A separate feast may be organised in Lucknow. Cleaning begins at the family's Raj Palace residence According to Sandeep's father and former MP Rajveer Singh, a baby shower and tilak ceremony will be held in Aligarh. Preparations are being planned on a 100-bigha field along the Aligarh-Ramghat-Kalyan Marg. Cleaning, painting and whitewashing, as well as the installation of new stone, are also under way at the family's Raj Palace residence. Close relatives, supporters and acquaintances of the family from Aligarh, the Atrauli Assembly constituency and different parts of the state will attend the tilak ceremony. Preparations are under way to send invitations to workers and supporters at the booth level. There is also discussion of booking a wedding planner separately for the wedding. Work is under way on booking catering services and a German hanger. President and chief ministers of several states attended the sister's wedding eight years ago The Kalyan Singh family had previously hosted a major wedding ceremony in 2018. Kalyan Singh's granddaughter Purnima Singh married Praveen Raj Singh. Besides President Ram Nath Kovind, several state chief ministers and governors attended the ceremony. Get to know Saurabh Singh, the minister's younger brother Sandeep's younger brother, Saurabh Singh, remains active in the Atrauli Assembly constituency. When their father and elder brother are not present in the district, he represents the family at social and political events. Saurabh is also the young national president of the Akhil Bharatiya Lodhi Rajput Kalyan Mahasabha. His father, Rajveer Singh, is the organisation's patron.

stories.title: ‘If court sends me to jail, I won’t seek bail':Brij Bhushan says ready to go to jail for national interest; products banned in several countries
stories.summary: “Let the court punish me; let the court imprison me. I will not seek bail; I will go to jail for the sake of the country. At least this will spread awareness about adulterated food products in the country.” Former BJP MP from Kaiserganj in Gonda, Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, said this while speaking to the media on Friday morning. He said that he had not done anything merely to remain in the news. He said, "In politics, publicity, pamphlets and expenditure are its characteristics." He has always remained in the news for one reason or another. He is now in the news over the issue of adulterated ghee. Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh said that reports of adulterated sweets, mawa, khoya, curd and oil being sold from villages to cities keep emerging. He said people should be made aware of such cases. He also said that if he went to jail, it was possible that awareness would be created among the public against those selling adulterated products. Brij Bhushan also made several claims about Patanjali products. He mentioned several products, including honey, ghee and medicines. Also spoke about his own ghee and Baba Ramdev's ghee Comparing the ghee produced at his facility with the ghee associated with Baba Ramdev, Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh said that ghee is not produced on a large scale at his facility. The ghee produced there previously cost around ₹2,000, and he has said that its price would be increased to more than ₹3,000. Baba Ramdev's company has filed a ₹50 crore defamation case against Brij Bhushan. The Madhya Pradesh High Court heard the case on Tuesday (15 September). Brij Bhushan's lawyer sought more time from the court to file a reply. The court has scheduled the next hearing for 18 September. The case relates to Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh calling Patanjali's products, particularly its desi ghee, counterfeit. In 2022, Brij Bhushan had also called Patanjali's ghee "counterfeit" at a public event and appealed to people to keep a cow or buffalo at home. At the time, his statement had also led to a dispute between Baba Ramdev and Brij Bhushan. Patanjali ghee has already been fined In 2025, the Food Safety Department fined Patanjali in Pithoragarh after its ghee was found not to meet the prescribed standards. In 2020, the department had collected a sample of Patanjali's ghee in Pithoragarh for testing. The sample failed the initial test. The company then sent the sample for retesting. However, the ghee was again found not to meet the prescribed standards in the second test. A case was subsequently filed in court. The court then imposed a fine of ₹1 lakh on Patanjali. The long-running feud between Baba Ramdev and Brij Bhushan The dispute between Baba Ramdev and Brij Bhushan is quite old. On 17 August last year, Brij Bhushan said in Balrampur, "Ramdev is one-eyed. The person whose name he is earning his livelihood in the name of-the history of Maharishi Patanjali also originates here in Gonda." However, he later apologised for the statement. Explaining it, Brij Bhushan said, "I made a statement during the Lok Sabha election. After that, Acharya Balkrishna Bhatt called me on the phone and called me a fool. We also responded in kind, and that is when our dispute began. In Balrampur, I was talking about the history of Gonda, Balrampur and the Devipatan division." “It was during this that Maharishi Patanjali was mentioned. I remembered that when Baba Ramdev had set out on his Swadeshi Yatra, he had mentioned the birthplace of Maharishi Patanjali in Gonda and promised to restore it. He had made this promise to the people. In that context, I was reminded of Baba Ramdev. A few words slipped out of my mouth. I later realised that I should not have said that.” This happened around eight months ago. After seeing the acne on a student's face, Brij Bhushan stopped him by holding his hand. He asked him why he had so many pimples on his face. "This is fake oil that is coming out, understand? This is the ghee from Ramdev," he said. As soon as people heard Brij Bhushan make this statement from the stage, they began laughing. Had earlier made a statement about fake ghee as well On 24 November 2022, while he was an MP, Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh said at a religious discourse tent in Barabanki, “If there is no disease in the body, there is no one richer than that person. A poor person's child is born weak. A healthy person's child is born healthy. To stay healthy, it is essential to maintain cleanliness at home and have milk and ghee. Milk is easily available in villages. I, too, used to go out grazing buffaloes. Only by rearing buffaloes and cows can one get pure milk and ghee. Otherwise, one has to eat Ramdev's fake ghee.”
