stories.title: Minister Nishad asks who paid for Phoolan Devi’s killing:Called her an icon, warns against people who betrayed her
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh government minister Dr Sanjay Nishad said on Monday, "Be wary of those who orchestrated Phoolan Devi's murder. Phoolan Devi was an icon. When she became disillusioned with the Samajwadi Party (SP) and formed her own party, she was murdered to silence her voice." The Nishad Party president said: Why did the SP not demand an impartial investigation into her death? Were they afraid that the real faces would be exposed? The fishing community will not forget such political betrayals. It will hold them accountable for every betrayal. Her death should be investigated. It should also be established who paid for the contract killing. The minister appealed to the fishing community to remain alert ahead of the Assembly elections. He said, "The election season has begun. Those traders who did not come to share your joys and sorrows for four-and-a-half years have now started hopping around you like seasonal frogs under the pretext of panchayats, laying out their mats." The minister's reference was to Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav. Recently, Akhilesh had described himself as the true well-wisher of the Nishad community. He had said, "The Nishad community was given respect, recognition and rights under the Samajwadi Party government. It was the SP that secured Phoolan Devi's release and got her elected as an MP twice." Three major points made by Sanjay Nishad 1- Phoolan Devi is a symbol of rebellion and justice Minister Nishad said, "Phoolan Devi is a symbol of rebellion and justice. She is an inspiration for women. Every woman will have to become a Phoolan Devi. The earlier era was one of guns. Now it is the era of the button. She suffered a great deal of injustice." She had spoken to the then prime minister and sought security. She had said, "We are unsafe in Uttar Pradesh; we will live in another state. Give me a guarantee, and only then will I surrender; otherwise, I will deliver justice with my weapon." 2- Phoolan Devi joined the SP, but received death in return Sanjay Nishad said, "The Congress made a promise, but forgot it." Phoolan Devi then joined the SP. The SP made her a leader and an MP, but what did she get in return? Death. When Phoolan Devi became disillusioned with the SP, she formed the 'Eklavya Sena'. She later formed her own party. She was murdered 27 days later. When she became disillusioned, the reason for it should also be explained. An answer should also be given as to why there was a need to form another party. A Chaurasia linked to the SP has occupied Phoolan Devi's property. 3- These are seasonal leaders who only shed crocodile tears The minister said, "The Nishad community is now awake. It will no longer be misled by anyone. The entire fishing community-including Mallahs, Nishads, Kevats, Kashyaps, Binds, Dheewars, Kahars, Bathams, Rayakwars and Majhis-must be wary of such people. They are seasonal leaders. They shed crocodile tears, come to power by taking Nishad votes and then forget the fishing community. They give everything to their own people. The fishing community's independent political identity is now the Nishad Party. The fishing community is not one that rolls out carpets for others; it is a community that fights for the rights of the OBC community."

stories.title: Man shoots girlfriend’s brother, kills himself:Had eloped with girlfriend 4 days ago in Lakhimpur Kheri
stories.summary: In Lakhimpur Kheri, a lover shot his girlfriend's brother at around 7 a.m. on Friday. The bullet struck his abdomen. He then pressed a country-made pistol to his own temple and fired. The lover died on the spot after being shot in the head, while the girlfriend's brother is in critical condition. A doctor at the district hospital referred the injured man to Lucknow. The incident took place in Dulahi village, under the Padhua police station area, 47 km from the district headquarters. The deceased was identified as Idrish of Dulahi village, while the injured man was named Akhilesh. According to neighbours, Idrish and Akhilesh's sister had been having an affair for a long time. Four days earlier, on 14 September, Idrish and his girlfriend had left home and eloped. The girl's family had filed a case against Idrish, accusing him of abducting her with the intention of sexually exploiting her. Police found both of them on Thursday. Know the case chronologically A shooting took place in Dulhi village at around 7 a.m. on Friday. Idrish, 38, a village resident, shot Akhilesh, 33, who lived opposite his house. Idrish then placed a country-made pistol against his temple and shot himself. Idrish died on the spot from the gunshot wound, while Akhilesh was seriously injured after being shot in the abdomen. At around 7 a.m., Akhilesh was sitting outside his house, washing his face. During this time, Idrish also came out of his house. An exchange of abuse and an argument began between the two. They had been quarrelling over the same issue for the past four days. Their family members thought they were fighting with each other as usual, so they did not pay attention initially. After around half an hour of exchanging abuse and arguing, Idrish went inside his house and returned with a country-made pistol. He threatened to shoot Akhilesh. When the argument did not subside, Idrish opened fire at Akhilesh. The bullet hit Akhilesh in the abdomen. Hearing the sound of gunfire, members of both families and villagers reached the spot. People asked Idrish what he had done. During this, Idrish placed the country-made pistol against his temple and shot himself. The bullet passed through his temple, killing Idrish on the spot. He fell on the village road. The villagers informed the police about the incident. The police reached the spot and sent Idrish's body for a post-mortem examination. Akhilesh was taken to the district hospital for treatment. As his condition was serious, doctors referred him to Lucknow. His condition is still reported to be critical. Idrish and Akhilesh's houses face each other and are around 20 metres apart. Idrish accused of eloping with Akhilesh's sister A dispute over taking Akhilesh's younger sister away has emerged as the motive behind the shooting. According to police, Idrish had taken Akhilesh's sister with him around four days earlier. Akhilesh had filed a case against Idrish and his brothers in the matter. Police recovered the young woman. Tension had persisted between the two families since then. Idrish had married a year earlier Idrish (38) was the eldest of four brothers. His brothers Budha (32) and Hafiz (25) work as labourers in Delhi, while Munawwar (27) drives an auto-rickshaw in Delhi. Idrish had married in the Singahi area around a year earlier. His wife is pregnant and is living at her parental home. The family also has two sisters, both of whom are married. Had already served seven years in prison in a shooting case According to villagers, Idrish's name had surfaced in a shooting case around 15 years ago. At the time, he was accused of shooting two people. A case was registered against him under Section 307, and he was sentenced to seven years in prison. Idrish completed his sentence and was released from prison about a year ago. Akhilesh is a sanitation worker at the Nagar Panchayat Akhilesh has two brothers, Rahul and Chhotu. His mother's name is Aarti. The family has four sisters, one of whom is married. Akhilesh and his brother Rahul work as sanitation workers at Nighasan Nagar Panchayat. SP Dr Khyati Garg said: A dispute reportedly broke out between the two sides over taking the young woman with them. One person died in the incident, while another was injured. Evidence has been collected from the scene. The cause of the incident is being investigated.

stories.title: Ram Mandir priests can keep beard, moustache and hair:Stay clean-shaven or purification for rule violation; new guidelines explained
stories.summary: New guidelines have been issued for the priests of the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya. They state that the priests must either keep their hair, beards, moustaches, and ‘shikhas’ or remain completely clean-shaven. Applying a tilak will also be mandatory. They will have to wear yellow clothes every day. They will not be allowed to enter the temple without bathing after using the toilet. If the rules are violated, purification will be carried out with cow's milk, ghee, and curd. Swami Rajkumar Das, a member of the Ram Mandir Religious Committee and head of Shriramvallabhakunj, shared details of the new guidelines with Dainik Bhaskar. He said, The Ram Mandir Trust's Religious Committee held a meeting on 12 September. The guidelines were issued with everyone's consent. The priests have been informed about them. Everyone has been asked to follow the rules. Priests will not be allowed to take mobile phones into the sanctum sanctorum According to the guidelines, priests will not be allowed to take mobile phones into the sanctum sanctorum. They will have to avoid making statements about the temple on social media. They must not post anything on WhatsApp or other social media platforms that could send a wrong message to people about the Ram Mandir. They will have to behave courteously with devotees. Priests will have to avoid joking and casual banter During their duties, priests will have to remain at their designated positions. If they need to leave their position for an important task, they will first have to inform the shift in-charge of the reason. They may leave their duty station only after that. They will have to avoid unnecessary conversation, group discussions and joking. They will have to remain calm and try to handle any incident. If necessary, they will have to seek assistance and guidance from those responsible. They must not engage in unnecessary conversation with devotees, as this could create a wrong impression of the priests or the Ram Mandir in their minds. Inform Acharya Ji if there is any problem Apart from the offerings and prasad provided by the temple, no outside items may be taken into the sanctum sanctorum. Priests must refrain from making unnecessary comments or asserting their authority. In case of any problem or dissatisfaction, they must inform Acharya Ji and seek his guidance. When family members or close friends visit, Acharya Ji will assist them with darshan, prasad and other arrangements, or these will be carried out as per his instructions. If any priest provides such special assistance or treatment to another person, the priest concerned will be held responsible. The utensils (made of gold, silver and other metals) must be counted before being handed over to the attendants and again after cleaning.

stories.title: Long queues for iPhone 18 in Noida, crowds at mall:Buyer from Punjab waited since morning, bought 2 Pro Max phones
stories.summary: Sales of Apple's new iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max began in India today. A crowd of buyers started gathering from 6 am at the only Apple store in Uttar Pradesh, located in Noida. By 7 am, a long queue had formed. People from border states such as Punjab, Haryana and Uttarakhand are reaching Noida to buy the new iPhone. As it was the first day of the launch, the Apple retail store at DLF Mall in Sector 18 was opened ahead of its scheduled time, at 8 am. As soon as the store opened, employees welcomed customers with applause. People were allowed to enter one by one. Those who emerged carrying iPhones were seen dancing and singing. The first young man to come out with an iPhone said, "I have come from Punjab. Sales of the new phone have not started there yet, so I first went to Delhi. There was a very large crowd at the store there, so I took a cab and came straight to Noida. I reached here at 6 am and was the first person in the queue. I bought two iPhone 18 Pro Max phones." India has a total of six official Apple retail stores-two in Mumbai and one each in Delhi, Noida, Bengaluru and Pune. The new iPhone is currently available for sale only at these six stores. In view of the crowds, the company has decided to keep the stores open until 10 p.m. See four pictures... Price starts at ₹1.64 lakh The iPhone 18 Pro is priced from ₹1,64,900, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at ₹1,79,900. Both models are available in different storage variants. The new iPhone 18 Pro series has been launched in four colours: Black, Silver, Glacier and Burgundy. iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max have the largest batteries ever Apple also launched the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max on 9 September, along with its first foldable phone. These are the first premium iPhones to feature three 48-megapixel cameras: a main camera, a telephoto camera and an ultra-wide camera. Apple claimed that the iPhone 18 Pro would last for 24 hours and the Pro Max for 30 hours on a single charge. This is the longest battery life ever offered. stories.title: ‘Where should a judge go if he faces injustice?’:Judge who awarded 23 death sentences in UP speaks out; once said, ‘I’d rather die than fear’
stories.summary: A judge's job is to deliver justice, but where is he to go if he himself is subjected to injustice? Is a judge working under the administrative control of a district judge also obliged to comply with orders that are contrary to the law? Muzaffarnagar judge Ravi Kumar Diwakar made this observation on Thursday (17 September) while delivering his verdict in a 10-year-old case under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act. He acquitted the accused, who had been making rounds of the court for a long time. During the hearing, the judge expressed displeasure over the decision of the then district judge to withdraw 97 cases from his court and transfer them to other courts. In his verdict, Judge Ravi Kumar Diwakar wrote: No one in India is above the law. The country will be governed by the Constitution and the rule of law, not by the arbitrary conduct of any public servant. No public servant can behave like a king. They must provide the legal reason for every administrative order they issue. This raises the question: was the then district judge's decision to recall the cases on 18 August, without stating any reason, just 13 days before his retirement, justified? Ten days earlier, on 7 September, Judge Ravi Kumar Diwakar wrote in his verdict sentencing the accused in the Shahpur Shahjadi murder case to death, "I would prefer to die rather than be called a cowardly judge. As long as I can follow my principles, I will continue in service; otherwise, I will resign." In fact, during his 17-year judicial career, Judge Ravi Kumar Diwakar has sentenced 36 convicts to death. During his five-month tenure in Muzaffarnagar alone, he sentenced 23 convicts to death. Find out which case the verdict concerns Now read what the judge wrote in the verdict: Took charge on 29 November 2025 Judge Ravi Kumar Diwakar took charge at the Additional District and Sessions Court, Fast Track Court-3, in Muzaffarnagar on 29 November 2025. He began his judicial service in 2009 and was posted in Sambhal and Bareilly before Muzaffarnagar. He has also been in the news over the verdict he delivered in the Gyanvapi case. He has written to police and administrative officials several times, saying that he faces a threat.

stories.title: ‘In relationship for a year, he said he was Hindu’:Lucknow victim who clung to car says they met at club
stories.summary: "Shahnawaz and I had been in a relationship for about one year. We met regularly. Our last chat was on 25 August. Even after that, we met twice. I had also gone to his house," said Anamika Singh. A case came to light involving Anamika being hit by a car and dragged near Janeshwar Mishra Park on the morning of 16 September. In an exclusive interview with Dainik Bhaskar, Anamika spoke about the incident and her relationship with Shahnawaz. She said, I met him at a club. He initially told me that he was Hindu. Later, I found out that he was Muslim. He had introduced himself as Ayush Yash Thakur. We had been in a relationship for one year. He had assaulted me before as well. Read the full conversation with Anamika Anamika said-My hand got trapped in the car window Anamika said the incident took place at around 6:30 a.m. on 16 September. Shahnawaz had locked the window on the driver's side of the car. My hand got trapped in the window. I tried very hard to pull it out, but could not. The car was then accelerated. After some time, the window was opened and I was dragged along the road. My entire body was injured. My hand was also injured and has marks from being trapped in the window. If another car had arrived at that time or I had come under the car, I could have lost my life. There used to be arguments over other girls Anamika said that Shahnawaz and she used to argue over his going out with other girls. When she asked him about the girls, he told her they were his friends. She later felt that he was hiding some things from her about the relationship. I kept tolerating things in this relationship, but the incident on 16 September was very serious for me. 'I had been assaulted before as well' Anamika alleges that Shahnawaz had assaulted her several times in the past. On one occasion, she was also assaulted in front of his friend Ashish Gautam. She said, What would have happened to my family if I had died that day? Disagreements in a relationship are one thing, but putting someone's life at risk is another. Victim asks: Why should I settle? According to Anamika, a man from Shahnawaz's family came to her house after the incident. She was asked to settle the matter. She said, ‘Why should I settle when I could have lost my life in the incident?’ She is currently staying at her friend's house. Shahnawaz is now accusing me of following him. This is not true. We had been in regular contact and meeting each other before the incident. I had even gone for tea with his paternal aunt and sister. I was not deliberately following him. They first met at a club Anamika said that she and Shahnawaz first met at a club. They spoke there, and she took his number the next day. Later, she found some information about him on social media, which led to a dispute between them. Anamika said she was studying in the third semester of an LLB course, while Shahnawaz was in the second semester. The two had not studied together. 'The video was made during our relationship' Speaking about the video that has surfaced, Anamika said, This video was made during our relationship. I made it myself as a joke. We remained in contact and continued meeting even after the video was made. She said the video showed the two of them talking. She can be heard addressing Shahnawaz by the name Ali, and the two can be heard discussing their breakup. 'Who would have been responsible if I had died?' Anamika said, If another car had arrived or I had come under the vehicle in the 16 September incident, I could have lost my life. Having a dispute in a relationship is one thing, but putting someone's life at risk is another.

stories.title: 47 gamblers arrested in Varanasi get bail:Gamblers from 7 districts released on ₹20,000 bonds; Roshan, Rafiq also freed
stories.summary: Special Operations Group-2 and Sigra police had busted a large-scale gambling operation being run in a house in the Rath Yatra area of Varanasi's Sigra police station jurisdiction. However, the police could not send any of those arrested to jail. DCP Crime Neetu Kadian had said in a statement that Gangsters Act proceedings would be initiated against all of them this time so that they could not get away, but the ACJM-4 court released all of them from the court itself on bonds of ₹20,000 each. Masterminds arrested The masterminds behind the gambling operation, Roshan and Rafiq, were also among those arrested. They were granted bail immediately. Gamblers from seven districts used to visit this gambling den. Roshan, Rafiq and Vijay used to organise the gambling there. Roshan and Rafiq were arrested at the spot, while police are still searching for Vijay. A man named Vishal Singh had taken the house on lease and handed it over. Police could not send them to jail Police conducted medical examinations of the 47 gamblers arrested from the Rath Yatra area on Wednesday night and produced them before the ACJM-4 court on Thursday. The court granted bail to all of them on bonds of ₹20,000 each. The gamblers were from Chandauli, Bhadohi, Azamgarh, Sonbhadra, Prayagraj, Mirzapur and Varanasi. Police had prepared to send them to jail, but the court released them all. No one will be spared this time DCP Crime Neetu Kadian had said during the arrests, The punishment prescribed by law for gambling is less than seven years. That is why these people get bail. So I have focused on this. The provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita will be used, and the organised crime section will be invoked. Property will be attached under Sections 111 and 107 of the BNS. Only then can these people be stopped. The Gangster Act will be invoked. Sigra police register case under the Public Gambling Act Despite the DCP's instructions, the inadequate functioning of the Sigra police has come to light in this case. Sigra police registered a case under Sections 3/4 of the Public Gambling Act. The police produced all of them in court, where they were granted bail immediately. stories.title: BSc student beaten to death with hammer in Gorakhpur:Mobile chats hint at affair; father was also asked for ₹20 lakh extortion
stories.summary: A first-year BSc student sleeping outside his house was murdered in Gorakhpur in the early hours. The attacker struck him on the head with a heavy object while he was asleep, killing him. The post-mortem confirmed that he died from head injuries. The student also screamed during the attack, but no one heard him. The student was alone at home when the incident took place. As his father was suffering from kidney failure, the entire family had gone to Lucknow for treatment. Family members learnt about the incident when they found his blood-soaked body at home in the morning. Police are examining mobile call details and WhatsApp chats. The initial investigation has pointed to an affair, while the case involving ₹20 lakh in extortion money previously demanded from his father is also being investigated. The incident took place in Jayantipur village under the jurisdiction of Bansgaon police station. Went to sleep on the veranda after dinner Shubham Mishra (19), a resident of Jayantipur, was the youngest of two brothers and one sister. He was studying in the first year of a BSc course. After dinner on Wednesday night, he went to sleep on the veranda outside the house. At around 5 a.m. on Thursday, an unidentified attacker struck him on the head. Shubham, who was seriously injured, was taken by his family members and villagers to the PHC in an ambulance, where doctors declared him dead. After receiving information about the incident, Khajni Circle Officer Anuj Singh and a forensic team reached the spot. The team collected evidence from the scene. Mother lost consciousness on seeing the blood-soaked body Shubham's father, Swadesh Mishra, is a farmer. According to the family, he had been suffering from kidney disease for the past four-five years. The family had gone to Lucknow for a kidney transplant and treatment. Shubham was alone at home. After learning about the incident in the morning, his parents reached the village at around 11:30 a.m. Sudha Mishra let out a scream on seeing her son's blood-soaked body. She repeatedly fainted and, while crying, kept saying that she wanted to be taken to her son. His father also lost consciousness after his son's death. Villagers helped him. The body was post-mortemed at BRD Medical College at around 2:30 p.m. After this, the family did not take the body to the village and performed the last rites at Rajghat. Considering the father's condition, his cousin lit the funeral pyre. ₹20 lakh ransom demanded from father in 2021 Shubham's father, Swadesh Mishra, owned a sweet shop in the town. According to the family, a ransom of ₹20 lakh was demanded from him in 2021. Gangster Shani Singh was accused in the case. After the case was registered, the police provided security to the family. Following Shubham's murder, the police are also including this old case in the investigation. A gangster has been detained and is being questioned. FIR registered against unidentified person on uncle's complaint An FIR has been registered against an unidentified person at Bansgaon police station on the written complaint of the deceased's uncle, Nagendra Mishra. Nagendra said the family did not suspect anyone and had no enmity with anyone. Police are examining the deceased's mobile phone call details and WhatsApp chats. In addition, information is being collected from CCTV cameras installed around the scene, mobile locations and people who had been in contact with the deceased. Southern SP Dinesh Kumar Puri said eight police teams had been formed to solve the case. Investigations are being conducted on all fronts to determine the motive for the murder and identify the attackers.

stories.title: Rain alert in 39 UP districts:Delivery boy falls into open pit in Kanpur; floods hit 15 Gonda villages, 10,000 stranded
stories.summary: The monsoon's withdrawal from Uttar Pradesh is drawing near. Its retreat via Rajasthan will begin over the next 24 hours. Rainfall will gradually come to an end across the state after that. Sunshine has prevailed in most cities, including Lucknow, Varanasi, Kanpur and Prayagraj, since Friday morning, although clouds continue to move across the sky. In Kanpur, a delivery worker fell into an open pothole on the road along with his motorcycle after it rained. Passers-by pulled him out after he remained in the pothole for about 2 minutes. He suffered a broken nasal bone in the accident. Fortunately, he was wearing a helmet, which prevented serious head injuries. A video of the incident, which took place on Tuesday night, emerged on Thursday. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an alert for light rain accompanied by thunder and lightning in 39 districts today. However, the weather will remain mostly clear. According to the IMD, rainfall activity is likely to decrease in western Uttar Pradesh from 20 September as the monsoon withdraws. The weather will become dry across the state from 22 September. Meanwhile, the water levels of rivers swollen by continuous rain have now begun to recede. In Gonda, the Ghaghra River has fallen to 20 cm below the danger mark. Over the past 24 hours, floodwater has receded from five villages, but nearly 10,000 people in 15 villages are still affected by the flooding. Several homes and roads remain waterlogged. See picture of the rain and floods Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said: Amid signs of the monsoon's withdrawal, rain is occurring at some places in Uttar Pradesh because of the western disturbance over Himachal Pradesh. In addition, moisture-laden winds coming from the Arabian Sea are forming clouds, while the cyclonic system over the state is gathering these clouds in one place. As a result, cloud movement continues over the state. Light to moderate rain is occurring along with strong winds. See which districts have been issued a rain alert today:

stories.title: Kanpur pharma trader murder:Son may also be arrested; Subrat caught in 6 police questions, to be confronted with wife, contract killer
stories.summary: Police have found several crucial pieces of evidence against Subrat, the son, in the murder case of a millionaire medicine trader in Kanpur. His arrest is now almost certain on the basis of this evidence. After suspicious activity came to light in the murder case, police have been summoning Subrat to the police station for questioning continuously for the past two days. During questioning, he answered several questions but remained silent in response to others. The police investigation revealed that two days before the murder, on 3 September, Vishal bought a SIM card from Jio, using which he spoke to Subrat six times. Police asked Subrat why these calls had been made, but he was unable to answer. Vishal worked at Subrat's shop on Birhana Road from 2010 to 2022. Vinit Minocha dismissed him from the job in 2022. Despite this, Subrat denied recognising Vishal in CCTV footage. Subrat did not answer this question either. Meanwhile, jailed murder accused Shalu Minocha and contract killer Vishal will be confronted with Subrat after their PCR (police custody remand) is approved. This will help firmly establish the evidence being found against Subrat. The remand of the three accused arrested so far will be heard on 19 September (tomorrow). Businessman Vineet Minocha was murdered in a room of his flat on 5 September. His daughter-in-law Shalu has been accused of plotting the murder. She is accused of having her father-in-law killed by a domestic worker. Read the full report... Read what questions the police asked Subrat- Received 45,000 for expenses, hosted a 49,000 party Deputy Commissioner of Police (West) SM Qasim Abidi had said that on the night of Vineet Minocha's murder, on 5 September, his son Subrat and daughter-in-law Shalu had gone to a couples' kitty party at Cosmojin Lounge in Tilak Nagar. Subrat had organised the party. This was revealed on Thursday (10 September) by Shalu's brother Dheeraj Arora and sister Sonia Mehrotra. Thirty-five people, all connected with the pharmaceutical trade, attended the couple's party. Restaurant records showed that both of them arrived at the party at 10:30 p.m., even though it was scheduled to begin at 11:30 p.m. It was also confirmed that they left their lounge at 3 a.m. The police investigation and the lounge records revealed another detail: the party had been booked at the rate of ₹1,400 per plate. The party bill came to around ₹49,000. During police questioning, Subrat had said that he received ₹35,000 as a salary and Shalu received ₹10,000 for expenses. The question was therefore raised: how was a party costing ₹49,000 organised with monthly expenses of ₹45,000? He had no answer. Photos and videos deleted from social media accounts A police investigation revealed that a few days after the murder, Subrat had also set a wallpaper featuring his firm, 'Pharma Traders', on his Facebook account. After receiving several comments one after another, Subrat removed the post from his account. He also deleted the photos and reels posted on his Facebook and Instagram profiles. Now, find out what the case was about Businessman Vineet Minocha lived with his family in flat C-104 on the first floor of Ratan Orbit Apartment. The four-room flat with a dining room is said to be worth more than ₹1 crore. Vineet ran a pharmaceutical firm called 'Pharma Traders' on Birhana Road. Vineet ran the business with his son, Subrat. Its annual turnover was ₹50 crore to ₹60 crore. The family comprises his wife, Punita; son, Subrat; daughter-in-law, Shalu; and five-year-old grandson, Shrijay. Shalu and Subrat were married in Nainital seven years ago. His wife, Punita, is a marriage counsellor and lives in Ghaziabad with their daughter, Subhani, and son-in-law. Shalu Minocha's father, Naresh Arora, is a textile businessman. He lives in Thakurganj, Lucknow. On the night of 5 September, the pharmaceutical businessman was stabbed more than 26 times in the neck and chest and killed. Police caught businessman's shop employee Vishal Gautam and his associate Rajkishore during an encounter on the night of 6 September. Vishal had said that he carried out the crime at the behest of his daughter-in-law, Shalu. Meanwhile, apartment security guard Madan Singh had said that Shalu called Vishal to the house, after which the police arrested Shalu and sent her to jail. On Wednesday, the police sought 24-hour custodial remand of Shalu and Vishal, but because of the strike, 19 September was set as the date for hearing the case. Punita's will also under investigation During the police investigation, a copy of the will prepared in June 2022 by Vineet's wife, Punita Minocha, was also found at the registry office. Police are investigating it. It is not yet clear whose name the property had been bequeathed to in the will. Police are also examining the document in connection with possible motives behind the murder.

stories.title: Accident exposes ₹41 lakh cash bag robbery:4 men drove 118km from Bhopal to Firozabad in 2 hours; bag provided clue
stories.summary: Four criminals who fled with ₹41 lakh from a car belonging to animal traders in Firozabad were caught by police after a road accident in Morena. After committing the crime at around 2 a.m., the accused fled towards Gwalior in a car. After covering 118 km in about two hours, their car collided with a truck while overtaking on a flyover in Morena at 4 a.m. The incident took place on 15 September. After the accident, all four criminals were trapped inside the car in an injured condition. BJP leader Arjun Tomar, who was passing by, stopped to help them. The injured men asked him to take the bags out of the car and hand them over. When one of the bags felt hard, he became suspicious. Meanwhile, police also reached the spot. A search found ₹41 lakh in cash inside the bags. Pistols, daggers and black masks were also recovered from the car. Daily Bhaskar's investigation traced the links to Bhopal. Read the report... After 10 days of surveillance, he called four criminals from Bhopal According to City Circle Officer Firozabad Santosh Singh, Bhopal resident Raj had arrived in Firozabad to stay with relatives around 10 days earlier. During this period, he kept watch on the movements of animal traders Jaan Mohammad, Raheesh and Anees. He noticed that the traders left home at around 2 a.m. carrying large sums of money to reach the morning market early. Raj shared this information with four criminals from Bhopal and called them to Firozabad. According to the police, the accused have been identified as Rehan (22), Khalid (40), Arsw (35) and Abid (27). Arsav and Abid are criminals under police surveillance in Bhopal. See the injured criminals at the hospital... Traders returned to collect their phone; criminals seized the opportunity and took out the bags The traders left for the market by car at 2 a.m., but after travelling about 20 metres, one of them remembered that he had left his mobile phone at home. The car was turned back. He went to get the phone, while the other two traders went a little further ahead to use the bathroom. Meanwhile, the criminals took two bags filled with cash from the car and fled. The two bags contained a total of ₹41 lakh. Before the traders could understand what had happened, the accused had already driven away in the car. After receiving the information, Firozabad police began pursuing them. The accused crossed Tundla and proceeded towards Madhya Pradesh. Car collides with truck in Morena, 118 km away After escaping the Firozabad police cordon, the accused continued towards Gwalior at high speed. According to the police, they covered the distance of about 118 km in approximately two hours. At around 4 a.m., while overtaking on a flyover in the Kotwali police station area of Morena, their car collided from behind with a truck travelling ahead. The collision was so severe that all four occupants of the car were injured. Meanwhile, an FRV from the Civil Lines police station area passed by. After seeing the accident, the police personnel informed an ambulance and began removing the injured from the vehicle. A short while later, BJP leader Arjun Tomar also reached the spot. He was travelling towards Machkund on a motorcycle with his friend Ashok Parmar. 'There are clothes in the bag'... It felt hard when he lifted it According to Arjun Tomar, the injured men said they were from Bhopal. A man wearing a black shirt asked him to take a bag out of the car and said it contained clothes. He was injured, yet his entire attention was focused on the bag. When Tomar picked up one of the bags, it felt hard. He suspected it might contain valuables. Meanwhile, another injured person informed him that there was another bag. Tomar handed both bags over to the police and asked them to keep the bags in their possession. He left after the ambulance departed. When the police searched the bags, they found bundles of currency notes inside. After this, the incident was no longer merely a road accident. The police began questioning the injured people and contacted the Firozabad police. This was how the entire chain of the theft of ₹41 lakh came to light. Police examined mobile phones, traced the matter to relatives After the accident, police took the injured people's mobile phones into custody. They contacted the numbers at the top of the call lists. When the people who answered were asked to identify the injured, they disconnected the calls. During this time, police learnt that the injured people's relatives had already been informed about the accident. They had asked their relatives living in Morena to reach the hospital. Morena police informed Firozabad police about the car, cash and weapons. Following this, a team from Firozabad police arrived to take further action. Old criminal records also came under investigation Firozabad police are now also gathering information about the accused's previous criminal records. According to Bhopal police records, it has emerged that some of the accused already have cases registered against them. Police records reportedly mention old cases related to gambling, assault, and theft against Khalid Qureshi in Bhopal. He is reportedly a history-sheeter from the Ashoka Garden area. Police are now gathering information on the remaining accused's past cases and their links with one another. Investigation from ATM cloning to a ₹41 lakh crime Records and intelligence inputs available to the police also mention old cases linked to accused Abid involving ATM cloning. A key part of the investigation now is to determine whether he was previously associated with an old interstate crime network and whether he was also connected to the planning of this crime. For now, the police are examining the accused's mobile phones, call details, contacts with one another, their movements from Firozabad to Morena, and records of their old cases. Police probing links spanning three states The crime began in Firozabad, Uttar Pradesh; the accused were arrested in Morena, Madhya Pradesh, after an accident, and their links to Bhopal have emerged. The scope of the investigation has therefore expanded beyond Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh to the Gwalior-Chambal region. Police are trying to determine whether only four people were involved in the crime or whether a larger network was also operating behind them. The investigation is being taken forward by connecting the links from the young man who conducted the reconnaissance to the accused summoned from Bhopal. Rasulpur police station in-charge Pradeep Kumar said an FIR had been registered against the accused for the robbery of ₹41 lakh. During questioning, information will be gathered about their local network and others linked to the crime.

stories.summary: Hetamapur village in Barabanki… Until a month ago, everything was fine here, but suddenly the Saryu River changed its course and wreaked havoc. In the severe flood that came after 18 years, 25 concrete houses were swept away by the river like pieces of straw. As the river continues to erode the land, it has now reached the famous Mahant Guru Narayan Temple. Meanwhile, a part of the mosque is hanging in the air over the river. To save the temple, people ranging from the MLA to a minister approached Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. The Chief Minister directed the DM to save the temple by any means necessary, without worrying about the budget. When the Dainik Bhaskar team reached Hetamapur village to see and understand the situation, it witnessed the helplessness of families watching their homes being destroyed. Read ground report… Hetamapur village is located in Ramnagar tehsil, around 50 km from the district headquarters. The village is home to the Mahant Guru Narayan Temple, the meditation site of Baba Narayan Das, and a temple dedicated to Lord Shankar. A large number of people from nearby districts used to visit these temples for darshan. With a large number of devotees visiting the area, many villagers earned their livelihood by selling prasad, garlands, and flowers. There is also a mosque directly opposite these temples. Overall, these religious places were a source of livelihood for many people in the village. There was no flood-like situation here until Raksha Bandhan on 28 August, 2026. But suddenly, the Saryu began moving towards the village. As the river's flow intensified, erosion also began. More than 500 bighas of farmland were washed away. Paddy had been planted in these fields only a few days earlier. After this, the river began eroding the village houses. From 5 September, houses started getting swallowed by the river one after another. On 11 September, the river's current suddenly became stronger, and 10 houses were swept away at once. ‘My son built the house by saving every single rupee; river swallowed it’ Kalawati, who sells sweets in front of the Mahant Guru Narayan Temple, has lost her concrete house to the river. She is now living under a thatched roof. While making sweets and wiping her tears, Kalawati says, “We had a big house, but the river swallowed it. When my grandchildren ask for money, I don't understand where to get it from! My son built the house by cutting down on his needs and saving every single rupee. Now he cries day and night.” Kalawati says, “I am sitting behind the temple and making prasad so that I can arrange two meals a day.” ‘9 bighas of farmland was shed away, ready crop on 4 bighas submerged’ Like Kalawati, the family of Ramtej, who lives on the edge of the village, is living under the shadow of fear. His concrete house is now just 10 metres from the river's eroding edge. Ramtej's wife Sunita stands on the roof, staring at the swollen river and the workers trying to stop the erosion. Sunita says, “Our 9 bighas of farmland have been washed away by the river. There was a ready crop of pointed gourd on 4 bighas, and that too has been submerged. Now only this house is left. If this also goes, we will be on the streets. If there is no house, how will our children go outside to earn? They cannot leave us alone in this condition.” Manakvara's house is right next to theirs. There is a fear that it will soon be swept away by the river. She says, “We built the house 10-12 years ago. We made a lot of effort to save it. Now there is no hope left. Erosion had happened here before too, but no one's house was cut away. This time, nothing is being spared. Please do something so that we can get help.” Her eyes filled with tears as she said this. Sunita's son, Maiku, says that the way the river's current is moving forward, their hopes are fading. “We don't know whether the house will survive or not.” 80 workers engaged in saving temple, next 2 days extremely crucial The destruction caused by the Saryu river has now reached the village's most sacred and important centre of faith. The river water is surging just a few metres from the Mahant Guru Narayan Temple. The district administration has deployed a team of 80 workers to save the temple from erosion. The workers are tying heavy boulders in large iron nets and placing them along the riverbank so that the direction of the current can be diverted. Soil and gravel are also being filled into sacks and placed at the erosion sites. However, 200 metres away from the temple, the river has now started eroding land from the other side. The next 2-3 days are considered extremely sensitive for the entire area. On the other hand, nearly half of the village mosque located directly opposite the temple has been swallowed by the river, while the remaining part is hanging in the air. This has left villagers both angry and saddened. Munna, whose house, built on 1 bigha and 15 bighas of land, has been swallowed by the Saryu, says, “Our house and livelihood are gone, and we have no sorrow about that. The administration is working hard to save the temple, and that is a very good thing, but our mosque should also have been saved. If 2-4 tractor-loads of stones had been placed behind the mosque as well, perhaps it could have been saved.” Niyaz, a villager who has lost 30 bighas of land, says around ₹90 lakh worth of property has disappeared into the river before his eyes. “Seeing the speed of the erosion, we have removed the doors, windows, and even the bricks from our house ourselves so that we can save whatever we can. The entire map of the village has changed.” Stones are being laid along the riverbank to save the village. A part of the mosque is hanging in the air over the river. ₹40 crore budget spent, new spurs built at ₹10 crore also washed away Flooding of the Ghaghra-Saryu is not new to Barabanki. Serious questions are being raised over the quality of construction work carried out at the administrative level. In 2007, a massive 54.6-km-long embankment was built from Ganeshpur to Chalahari Ghat to protect around 150 villages from erosion. This year, 7 separate projects costing ₹40 crore were approved to stop erosion by the Saryu. Under these projects, eight very strong ‘thokar’ (spurs) were built along the riverbank. Despite this, villages such as Kedarpur and Baburi were washed away by the river last year. This year too, the Yogi government approved a budget of ₹10.36 crore to strengthen the Ganeshpur-Chalahari embankment. With this amount, large spurs were built at three highly sensitive locations so that the direct current of the river would not hit the embankment and villages. A nearly 20-metre section near the newly built spur at Nayapurwa could not withstand the pressure of the river and was washed away by the strong current. After the spur broke, the river's main current began hitting the residential area of Hetamapur village directly, and the destruction began. MP alleges corruption Political statements have also intensified after the tragedy in Hetamapur. Local Congress MP Tanuj Punia visited the flood- and erosion-affected areas and heard the grievances of villagers. MP Tanuj Punia accused officials of the Irrigation and Flood Division of corruption and serious negligence. He said, “Last month itself, we had written a letter to the Flood Control Department seeking information about what preparations had been made to stop erosion before the monsoon and how much budget had been spent and where. But the officials did not consider it appropriate to give any response.” Villagers forced to take shelter at Batnera relief camp The families whose houses have been completely swept away by the river in Hetamapur are currently forced to take shelter at the flood relief camp in Batnera, around 2 km from the village. According to Vipul Singh, tehsildar of Ramnagar tehsil, “Around 30 families have been directly rendered homeless. More than 50 houses are at risk from erosion. The administration has provided financial assistance and distributed food supplies from the disaster relief fund as per the rules.” The biggest challenge is to permanently rehabilitate the homeless families. For this, government land near the Lalpur Karauta area is being identified. As soon as the land allocation is finalised, all the affected families will be given land leases and permanently settled there.

stories.title: Nepali girls ‘sold’ to bear fair-skinned babies:₹1cr deal covers pregnancy to delivery without marriage; trafficking racket at UP border
stories.summary: Nepali girls are allegedly being sold to people who want a fair-skinned child. These girls are brought from the Nepal border adjoining Uttar Pradesh. Brokers are allegedly being paid up to ₹1 crore for arranging for a girl to have a child without marriage. Of this, the girl receives ₹20-25 lakh. This new trend has been seen among couples who do not have children and want a child. Instead of IVF, such couples are having children with Nepali girls. Most of these cases involve couples where the woman is unable to become pregnant. There is also a fear that the IVF case could go wrong and the child could be born weak. Girls are brought to India from Nepal through brokers after paying large sums of money. They are kept here for one to one-and-a-half years. They are made pregnant through sexual relations. After the child is born, they are sent back to Nepal. Dainik Bhaskar has exposed this trend. We went to Nepal posing as relatives of a couple in need. We reached the gang that was selling girls. How does this gang work? What kind of girls are involved in it? Read the full investigation... Through a source near the India-Nepal border adjoining Uttar Pradesh, we came to know about a Nepalese agent, Sushma Thapa. She was in Bhutwal, Nepal, 35 km inside the border. Sushma works as an agent for a gang supplying Nepali girls. We called her and told her that there was a wealthy couple. They had been married for eight years, but the wife was unable to conceive. They wanted a girl to have sexual relations with the husband, become pregnant and give birth to their child. We spoke to Sushma several times about this. Once she became convinced that it was a genuine case and there was no possibility of fraud, she agreed to meet us. We went there and spoke to Sushma. Sushma: Who will stay with the girl? Reporter: Family members will stay with her. We will also have to take care of her. Sushma: Yes, sir, that is true, because she will have to be taken care of more carefully than glass. Reporter: Will the girl agree to have physical relations? Sushma: If she gets money, she will have physical relations, won't she? Look, sir, I had told you that two years ago I took Rs 1 crore in such a case. The girl was not agreeing for less. She said... “I am taking a risk. I could even die because of this.” I had assured her that nothing would happen. She had an operation. Reporter: It has become very easy now. If she is properly taken care of, there is no problem. Sushma: She was taken care of so well, sir, that the party fed her so much dry fruit and fruit that she gained a lot of weight. She even stopped being able to walk around. Anyway, she is married now. I approached her again once for the same work, but she refused. Now we wanted to know which areas of Nepal these girls come from. How do brokers convince their families to supply the girls? Do they have to follow any legal process to take them away? Read the conversation ahead… Reporter: Will these girls come from the mountains? Sushma: They can be from the mountains. They can be from Palpa or Pokhara, or even farther away. Reporter: So they will be from the hills. Will we have to go to the mountains? Sushma: No, sir, we will call them here if you say so. Reporter: Okay, but there should be no fraud. Sushma: Once you like the girl, the paperwork will be done. You will give the money when you are about to take her. Reporter: What will happen in the paperwork? There is a guarantee, right? Do we need any government permission for this? Sushma: Sir, there are two ways. One is without paperwork, where there is just a discussion and, with mutual consent, you take the girl with you. The other is a proper agreement, in which there is a deal between the two families. Reporter: Won't this be misused later? Sushma: No, sir, the papers will only be with us and you. Earlier, we had sent a girl to the US. Everything was clearly mentioned in the agreement. Because sometimes you come across someone crazy who later comes to make a claim. Bhaskar reporter enters the entire network in Nepal After nearly a month of further conversations, we got Sushma to admit that a larger network was working with her. We asked Sushma who all were involved and told her that we would have to meet everyone. Our relatives would come to finalise the deal, so they would meet everyone. Sushma was initially not ready. But then she demanded some money in the name of rent and travel expenses. After receiving the money, she called us to Nepal again. She introduced us to two agents from Pokhara, Nepal, Deepu and Om. Reporter: How will the girl cross the border? There is a lot of checking. Deepu: (pointing towards the female broker) These people will get her across. There will be no problem crossing the border. She will reach you by car after crossing the border. Before everything is finalised, we will meet the people who need the girl. Reporter: Yes... we will arrange the meeting. Deepu: Look, it should not happen that you take her from here and sell her. Or put her into the business. Or that she is being tortured. If there is any problem, the police will arrest us and there will be a case. This is such a case that if you go inside, it will be difficult to get out. You can get bail in India, but not in Nepal. We need a full inquiry. Look, the girl has no father. She only has her mother. So we told her that we would first show her the house. She could see whether she would be able to stay there or not. Only then would we confirm. Reporter: Absolutely, that is the right thing. Tell me, will the girl also have a medical report? Deepu: Don't worry, we will get the medical done. Three girls introduced, brokers said there would be no discussion about money After meeting the three agents, we had understood that these three were sending Nepali girls to India by luring them with money. We told the agents that we now wanted to meet the girls and confirm that they were not being misled. The agents were initially not ready. Then they put forward a condition that there would be no mention of the money deal during the conversation. We then reached the location in Nepal given by the agents to meet the girls. After waiting until around 7 pm, the agents told us that the girl coming from the hills of Nepal had been stranded because of a landslide. They then arranged a video call with her. Reporter: Where do you live? Are you married? Geeta: In Nepal near Siliguri... Yes, I am married. Reporter: Will you still stay for a year despite this? Geeta: Yes, I am divorced. I am 35 years old. Reporter: So who else is there in the family? Geeta: My mother and my 20-year-old son. Reporter: So he won't have any problem? Geeta: No, he won't have any problem. Reporter: Who else is there in the family? Geeta: My mother and the person who is with you is my elder brother. This is my family. Reporter: So your brother has told you that you will have to have physical relations? Geeta: Yes, my brother has told me. Reporter: Will any family member go with you? Geeta: Yes... my younger sister will go. We asked the agents to introduce us to some more girls. The agent introduced us to 20-year-old Ruby Thapa, who was from Gulmi in the hilly region of Nepal. Reporter: Who is there in the family? Ruby: Brother, father, mother, sister. Everyone farms in the village. I am 20 years old, and my brothers and sisters are younger. Reporter: What are you doing currently? Ruby: I pack goods in a factory. Reporter: Do you know why we are meeting? Ruby: Yes, I mean, you need a young girl, don't you? I have some health problems and I am not strong. Reporter: You will be taken care of properly. Ruby: Okay. Reporter: Have you had physical relations before or not? Ruby: No. The next day, agent Sushma called and asked us to meet another Nepali girl. The girl's name was given as Rupa Thapa. However, she did not arrive even by 7 pm. We were told that there had been a landslide in the Tansen and Palpa areas. To understand the network more closely, we continued speaking to agent Sushma. Reporter: Does this happen along the border? Sushma: Yes. We have sent girls five times before. Reporter: Do you work alone or are other people involved? Sushma: Other people are involved too. Reporter: The IVF people must also be connected, right? They must be the ones who bring such cases. Sushma: IVF people take the cases themselves here. We do not work with them because we do not get any money from them. The girls receive only 20–25% of the money Needy women in Nepal are allegedly drawn into this network for money. Agents give them 20–25% of the amount received and keep the rest. Several people are involved in the network and divide the remaining ₹75–80 lakh among themselves. The women agree because ₹20–25 lakh is a substantial amount for them, and the brokers are people they know. Staying in someone else’s home for a year to 18 months requires trust, which the brokers allegedly provide. Why Nepali women? As the woman is from another country, there is a perception that the possibility of the biological mother later making a claim after the child grows up is lower. Some people believe this arrangement would help them maintain social security. However, if a Nepali woman files a complaint alleging abuse or assault, a case of human trafficking can be registered.

The Nandigram seat was vacated by Adhikari after he won both constituencies. The Rejinagar seat bypoll candidate is former district BJP president Sarkar. Polling for these by-elections is scheduled for October sixth.

stories.title: Delhi to hold month-long Seva Sankalp Abhiyan from September 17, projects worth Rs 13,820 crore lined up
stories.summary: The Delhi government will launch a month-long public service campaign, the 'Seva Sankalp Abhiyan', from September 17 to October 17 to mark Prime Minister Narendra Modi's birthday, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta announced on Monday.

stories.title: Yogi Adityanath announces welfare measures, tech push for lawyers in UP
stories.summary: In a strong rebuke of the previous administration, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath highlighted shortcomings in governance and infrastructure. He revealed plans to provide tablets to 400 law officers for enhanced case management. Additionally, a cashless insurance scheme of up to Rs 5 lakh will be launched for advocates, while robust police infrastructure and training facilities are being prioritized.

stories.title: 'Tareekh Pe Tareekh': 100% complete, still no keys - Inside RERA’s extension loop
stories.summary: A growing number of housing developments are running past their scheduled completion dates, leading to frequent regulatory extensions that lack a guarantee of timely delivery. MahaRERA's data highlights a substantial volume of these extensions processed annually. Developers often tout impressive completion figures while still pending crucial approvals. The oversight framework fails to secure buyer possession effectively, raising concerns about the effectiveness of the system.

stories.title: 'Forcibly defeated': Mayawati flags 'govt irregularities' in Rajasthan municipal polls
Cases against 3 DMK leaders over remarks against TN CM Vijay's speech
stories.summary: In a significant move, Chennai and Kallakurichi police have initiated legal proceedings against three DMK leaders following protest remarks made on September twelfth. Notably, former minister P K Sekarbabu has been charged in Chennai for his contentious protest speech, while DMK MP A Raja faces allegations for derogatory comments aimed at a state minister. Additional cases have also emerged in Kallakurichi and Cuddalore, all linked to the same protests.

stories.title: In 1998, 31 Przewalski’s horses entered Chernobyl and reached 137 by 2018
stories.summary: After the Chernobyl disaster, an abandoned radioactive landscape became an unlikely refuge for Przewalski’s horses, a species once lost from the wild. Introduced in 1998–99, the population suffered transport deaths and poaching but continued breeding. By 2018, 137 horses were documented in Ukraine, with others established across the Belarusian border.

stories.title: More than 19,000 housing pockets have rooftop solar systems, benefits 9 lakh households
Ram temple trust rejects claim ex-Air Marshal Mishra skipped CEO interview round
Indian-origin UK nurse wins $250,000 Global Nursing Award for boosting organ donation among South Asians
stories.summary: In a remarkable achievement, Indian-origin nurse Agimol Pradeep has clinched the Aster Guardians Global Nursing Award 2026, celebrated for her impactful advocacy in organ and stem-cell donation. The $250,000 award will see half allocated to Upahaar's efforts in expanding organ donation initiatives. This recognition not only emphasizes the vital contributions of nurses to healthcare but also aligns with Kerala's efforts to bolster its nursing workforce amid persistent global shortages.

stories.title: ‘Serious lapse’: Air India CEO summoned after 3 foreigners 'skip' immigration check
NMC seeks report on allegations medical college made ₹3.75 lakh hostel payment mandatory for MBBS internship
'First step towards safety': Meta to report child sexual abuse cases to law enforcement
All of Ukraine is a target: Russia on strike near Poland
Saudi military airbase hit as Houthis launch fresh attacks
AI 'fearmongering' will be good for no one: China
Trump slams AI guardrails, calls it a 'sick conspiracy'
J&K: Police bust LeT-linked OGW network, arrest 3 for aiding terrorists
Pak ups reward for Masood Azhar by PKR 20L ahead of FATF meet
Row at Dhaka University over photos of Jinnah, Jamaat ex-chief
Kai Cenat And Gigi Alayah Reunion Rumors? North West reacts on TikTok; Fashion Week sightings revive questions
stories.summary: Kai Cenat and Gabrielle “Gigi” Alayah have sparked fresh reunion rumors after being spotted together during New York Fashion Week. Cenat was seen blowing kisses to Alayah after his Vivet runway show, with her appearing to return the gesture. North West then added to the speculation by commenting on Alayah’s TikTok, “can’t believe that u n kai are back together.” Neither has confirmed that they are dating again.

stories.title: Owens Presses For Surveillance Details: Conservative demands suspect info; Turning Point reviews footage
stories.summary: Candace Owens has questioned Turning Point Action over the vandalism of Charlie Kirk’s memorial statue at the organisation’s Arizona headquarters. She urged the group to share more details from its surveillance cameras, including descriptions of the suspects or their vehicle, so the public could help identify those responsible. Turning Point condemned the incident and said it was working with law enforcement while planning to restore the damaged statue.

stories.summary: No Talks On This So Far: TDP; LJP For Transparency
